title: 100 Million Bugs Later: A Field Report From the Agentic Era (sponsored by CodeRabbit) (DVT212-S)
description: CodeRabbit reviews code generated by major coding agents: 30M+ pull requests and 200K+ independent code reviews each day across open source and enterprises. AI-co-authored PRs carry about 1.7x more issues and up to 2.74x more security issues than human-written code. He introduces Agentic Change Management: an independent, agent-agnostic quality gate that assesses every change, surfaces what needs human attention, and explains what it approves. title: 10x Faster Vector Indexes: GPU Acceleration in Amazon OpenSearch with NVIDIA cuVS (sponsored by NVIDIA) (DAT318-S)
description: At billion-vector scale, vector index construction can become a performance and cost bottleneck for retrieval, RAG, and AI workloads. Amazon OpenSearch Service Vector Acceleration uses NVIDIA cuVS to accelerate index construction, delivering up to 10x faster builds at a quarter of the indexing cost while preserving the OpenSearch experience. This 300-level session goes under the hood of the architecture: how eligible builds are offloaded to managed GPU workers, how cuVS and CAGRA accelerate graph construction through the Faiss backend, and how the graph is converted into an HNSW index for CPU-based search. We will examine how segment size, quantization, and ingestion patterns affect GPU utilization, build speed, and efficiency. Attendees will leave with guidance for identifying good-fit workloads, optimizing ingestion, and modeling performance and cost benefits for their own deployments. This presentation is brought to you by NVIDIA, an AWS Partner.

description: AI is accelerating how fast code ships and how fast attackers find exploitable weaknesses, and annual pentests cannot keep pace. This talk will cover the delegate balance between autonomy, safety and control in Offensive Security. This presentation is brought to you by Terra, an AWS Partner.

title: Agentic AI Meets the Line-of-Business Buyer
description: Budget authority is migrating from CIOs to line-of-business leaders - CFOs, Chief Medical Officers, Heads of Manufacturing - who buy outcomes, not infrastructure. At the same time, agentic AI is making it possible to automate entire business processes end-to-end, not just assist them. The partners who win are the ones who can connect these two shifts: framing autonomous agents as measurable business outcomes (revenue acceleration, cost compression, speed-to-market) in the language LOB leaders understand.
location: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: Agentic AI Needs Agentic Infrastructure: Autonomy on Amazon EKS (sponsored by ScaleOps) (COP344-S)
description: Enterprises now ship software that reasons and acts on its own. The infrastructure underneath still waits for a human to edit YAML. This session makes the case that autonomous workloads demand autonomous infrastructure, and shows what it looks like on Amazon EKS today: agents held to fractional GPU allocations that track real consumption, pod requests that stay honest as behavior drifts, and Karpenter consolidating nodes fed by accurate signals. You'll hear how enterprises run this in production with ScaleOps, and where autonomous resource management goes next. Leave with a blueprint for infrastructure that manages itself. title: Agentic commerce in production: multi-agent orchestration on AgentCore
description: A single agent that both advises and sells gets fragile fast. This session shows a production multi-agent system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Strands Agents, running for real Shopify merchants, where an orchestrator coordinates two specialists: a wellness advisor in a regulated domain and a commerce agent that owns decision and checkout. We walk the decisions that matter: orchestration topology, intent routing and handoffs, shared versus isolated memory across agents, where the action boundary and per-agent guardrails live, and the latency and token cost that coordination multiplies. A demo follows one conversation from advice to checkout. You leave with an orchestration pattern, and the code to implement it directly in your online store.

description: AI agents are increasingly making real-world decisions — approving loans, issuing refunds, offering discounts — yet most fairness testing still focuses on whether chatbots use offensive language. title: Agentic Memory: Build AI Agents That Learn from Every Interaction
description: Today's AI agents forget everything after each conversation ends. A customer calls back about the same issue for the third time, and the agent starts from zero. In this chalk talk, we explore how to architect persistent memory systems for Amazon Connect Customer AI agents, enabling them to remember customer preferences, recall prior issue context, and adapt resolution strategies over time. We whiteboard real architectures using Customer Profiles, Bedrock knowledge bases, and DynamoDB to build agents that reduce repeat contacts and deliver personalized experiences, without retraining models. How do you recover without a valid backup? Learn where recovery breaks across S3, Glue Data Catalog, S3 Tables, and databases and pipelines around them, then how Rubrik recovers petabytes in hours, restoring only what changed, critical data first, within your RTO. description: Every agent your company runs, on a developer laptop, in a CI runner, or in an Amazon EKS pod, ends its work the same way, with an API call against your AWS account using a credential nobody reviewed. Endpoint tools stop at the laptop. The credentials that matter live in the cluster. This year's worst agent incidents involved no attacker. An agent did what it was permitted to do, and nobody rendered a decision at the moment a permitted step became an incident. In fifteen minutes, Sysdig follows one person's agents from their laptop into EKS, shows what each action would reach in your account, and stops the one whose reach includes admin-equivalent permissions before it executes. We'll examine where AI genuinely improves review quality, where it creates false confidence, and why human judgment remains the deciding factor. You'll leave with a practical framework for combining AI speed with human accountability in your own review process.
location: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: A leader's guide to advanced team models in an agentic world
description: You built multi-skilled teams for cloud. That shape does not absorb agents. Cheaper execution does not remove work, it relocates it into judgment, verification, and spotting confidently wrong answers. The question we want answered is not about reporting lines, it is "does this new world include me?" The twenty-year senior, the junior who cannot get in, the manager of a smaller team: each needs a different answer. Four operating models return, from today's anti-pattern to the hourglass, with a first-person account of what works inside Amazon and what doesn't. The answer is yes, but the entry requirement has changed.

speakers.name: Jonathan Allen
speakers.title: Executive in Residence, AMAZON WEB SERVICES

speakers.name: Carrie Wood
speakers.title: Director, AWS Senior Talent & Transformation, Amazon

title: A leader's guide to escaping proof-of-concept purgatory
description: Drawing on 1,000+ customer conversations about building competitive advantage with data and AI, Rahul Pathak, VP of AWS Data & AI GTM, shares what separates organizations getting real value from agentic AI from those stuck in pilots. When everyone has the same models, your data is the only differentiator. Rahul covers how to set goals worth deploying against, why working backwards from outcomes matters, why cross-functional teams outperform centralized AI functions, what governance must exist before agents reach production, not after, and how to create urgency without a mandate. Field notes from 1,000+ rooms, and a playbook for Monday morning.

title: A leader’s guide to governing AI, on behalf of humans
description: AI deployments can reason, problem-solve, and act with increasing agency. Yet governance models built for deterministic software are no longer sufficient. AWS Executive in Residence Ryan Seaman and Dr. Bernadette Han, organizational psychologist at the American Psychological Association (APA), bring technology and human behavior into one governance conversation. As AI interacts with people, influences decisions, and takes actions, governance must address not only what AI can do, but how it behaves with people and what happens as a result. Bernadette introduces the EEI-AI Behavioral Architecture™, translating psychological science into behavioral requirements organizations can design for, test, observe, and govern responsibly.

speakers.name: Dr. Bernadette Han
speakers.title: Head of APA Learn, American Psychological Association

title: A leader's guide to how AI is changing Amazon’s ways of working
description: AI is changing how Amazon hires, builds, manages, and deploys teams across every function to innovate and deliver on behalf of customers. This session shares Amazon's emerging framework: the mental models fueling transformation, a state model for understanding where teams are on the AI journey, and real case studies of teams that have crossed from AI-enhanced to AI-native and beyond. We'll walk through the implications, share the questions we're still wrestling with, and offer practical recommendations for leaders navigating the same transition. First-person data from an organization at scale, shared with candor.

speakers.name: Stephen Brozovich
speakers.title: Executive in Residence, Amazon Web Services

title: A leader's guide to how Amazon built its data foundation for agents
description: Organizations racing to put AI agents on top of their data keep hitting the same walls: security, privacy, scale, and data they can't trust. In this session, Anas Fattahi (VP, Amazon Business Data Technologies) and G2 Krishnamoorthy (VP, AWS Databases) share how years of foundational investment positioned Amazon to move quickly when the agentic AI moment arrived, and where the hard problems still live. You'll hear which bets paid off, what's working now, what they're still building, and how to inspect your own setup against what they've learned.

title: A leader's guide to modernizing systems for AI, with AI
description: Every enterprise faces the same sequencing problem: "Before we can deploy AI, we need to fix our legacy systems." This is technology's most expensive false binary. Organizations that made real progress rejected that sequence. They use AI to understand undocumented code, decompose monoliths, and rebuild the very systems blocking deployment. One airline uses AI to comprehend reservation logic only three people understand. Another enterprise uses agents to reverse-engineer decades of business rules into microservices. The recursive unlock: the technology you want to deploy removes what blocks it. This session covers the funding, sequencing, and organizational decisions that make it work.

speakers.name: Matthias Patzak
speakers.title: Executive in Residence, Amazon Web Services

speakers.name: Sree Ratnasinghe
speakers.title: Director, Customer Solutions, AWS Strategic Accounts, Amazon Web services

title: A leader's guide to reimagining complex business processes with agents
description: Most enterprises use AI as an assistant, automating individual tasks for incremental 20% gains. The leaders unlocking profound productivity gains are doing something different: reimagining entire business processes from the outcome backward, so every step hands forward context, confidence, and decision authority, not just data. This session shows what it takes to transform your most strategic operations with agentic AI and scale them, then Thomson Reuters walks through the lessons of rebuilding its M&A process end-to-end. You leave knowing which processes to reimagine and how to move them into production, where value compounds.

speakers.name: Helena Yin Koeppl
speakers.title: Director, Executive in Residence, Amazon Web Services

speakers.name: Romeo Romeo
speakers.title: VP, AI Ventures and Tech M&A, Thomson Reuters (UK)

speakers.name: Simone Zucchet
speakers.title: Head of UKI SA - Advertising, Publishing and Information Services, Amazon Web Services

title: A leader's guide to scaling AI adoption without losing control
description: I gave the organization AI tools — why did adoption stall? Most enterprises equip teams with AI and expect transformation to follow. It doesn't. Amazon scaled agentic AI to thousands of production deployments not by mandate, but by investing in what surrounds the model: governance that guards what truly matters — customer trust, privacy, security, and cost — while loosening its grip everywhere else, a culture where experimentation and oversight coexist, and upskilling that turns casual prompters into confident builders. This session names the structural bets that move adoption, the debts you're quietly acquiring, and why losing control isn't the failure — over-constraining is.

speakers.name: Daniel Slater
speakers.title: Executive in Residence; Worldwide Head, Culture of Innovation, Amazon Web Services, Inc.

speakers.name: Erin Kraemer
speakers.title: Senior Principal Technical Product Manager, AWS

title: A leader's guide to security at the speed of AI, powered by Mythos
description: As AI capabilities advance, so do the capabilities of those who attack software. The pace of modern development has outgrown point-in-time security reviews, leaving vulnerabilities exploitable longer than any leader should accept. Periodic snapshots cannot keep up when code changes constantly, so security has to become continuous, evaluating posture as the code itself evolves. Amazon used frontier-model capabilities, through Mythos, to make security continuous at its own scale, finding issues and guiding builders to fix them as they work. This session explores that shift. Senior leaders will learn how to secure their organizations at AI speed.

title: A leader's guide to the AI speed trap
description: Your developers are faster with AI. Your organization isn't. AI tools accelerate individual teams, but organizational outcomes depend on what happens between teams: coordination, dependencies, and end-to-end value streams that extend far beyond code. Most productivity metrics miss this entirely because they stop at the team boundary. In this session, we present real patterns from startups, scaleups, digital natives, and large organizations, introduce measurement frameworks that capture what matters at the organizational level, and share practical approaches for turning team-level acceleration into outcomes your customers will notice.

speakers.name: Matthias Patzak
speakers.title: Executive in Residence, Amazon Web Services

title: A leader's guide to the AI you haven't seen yet
description: Most AI strategy is built for the AI leaders can see. The models in production today are the constrained ones, gated by capacity and cost, and that gate is lifting. When it lifts, a dozen breakthrough applications becomes a million, and AI systems get as cheap and as common as a website. Progress has stopped being predictable too: capability arrives in step changes that can obsolete a year of work in a quarter. This session asks what you would build if AI were free and never made a mistake, and how to tell a durable bet from a disposable one.

title: A leader's guide to the hardest investment decision in AI
description: Fund the platform or fund the use case? Demand proof before investing or invest to generate the proof? Scale the winner or explore the next opportunity? These decisions determine whether AI compounds or stalls, and they require the CIO and CFO to act together. Two former operators share how the best CIO-CFO pairs align on what to fund, what to kill, and what "good enough evidence" looks like when certainty isn't available. You leave with the approach that replaces "requestor and approver" with co-ownership, and the questions every pair should answer before their next AI investment.

title: A leader's guide to what separates AI leaders from the rest
description: In early 2026, the Reimagine research program interviewed senior technology leaders under conditions of candor: off-the-record, non-attributable, no marketing follow-up. What they said contradicts the prevailing conference narrative. Nobody is running agents autonomously, not one. The most advanced organizations are carrying the most technical debt. The AI generating real value looks nothing like the demos. This session synthesizes the patterns that emerged when executives stopped performing confidence and started sharing reality.

title: A leader's guide to what your board must know about AI (and shouldn't)
description: Your board is asking about AI — and that's a good thing. Their curiosity is the opening you need. But that attention can create more heat than light: dashboards and benchmarks that generate activity without moving the organization forward. The real opportunity is to channel that interest — show AI's true potential and turn your board into a genuine partner for a transformation that needs their conviction to succeed. In this session, assess where your board sits, understand the personas at play, and learn proven tactics to move them from curiosity to conviction.

speakers.name: Mario Thomas
speakers.title: Head of Applied AI & Emerging Technology Strategy, Amazon Web Services

speakers.name: Taimur Rashid
speakers.title: Managing Director, Frontier AI Engineering & Services, Amazon Web Services

title: A leader's guide to why agentic AI just made your data problem urgent
description: The data problem you tolerated for years just became an emergency. Agents do not politely work around missing metadata. They guess confidently, and you find out three weeks later. Enterprises assumed they could solve AI first and data second. They can't. You get the framework that separates compounding value from programs that never finish. AWS Marketing built an agentic system over thousands of warehouse tables. It worked. Its first output: an inventory of every undocumented decision in the warehouse. That exposure was worth more than the answers. You leave knowing what to fix first, and why analytical demand climbs.

title: A leader's guide to why your AI economics are wrong
description: Most AI business cases use ROI frameworks built for deterministic systems, measuring cost avoidance while missing the metrics that predict success. The gap between pilot and production economics is 10-50x, and most finance teams still model AI as capital expense rather than variable. This session names the three assumptions that guarantee your AI business case is wrong, and the costs that blindside CFOs in production. It presents the financial model Amazon uses internally to forecast AI operating expenditure. You leave knowing which line items to remove from your next business case, and which to add that nobody tracks yet.

title: Align cost with value through outcome-based pricing in AWS Marketplace
description: Customers increasingly expect software to be priced in terms of value delivered, paying only for results like resolved tickets or documents processed not API calls or compute hours or seats. In this Code Talk, learn how to implement outcome-based pricing and see live examples of metering and billing in AWS Marketplace. Follow along as we go from prototype to published listing, billing per resolved ticket, processed document, or any measurable result you choose.
location: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Code Talk

speakers.name: Dev SenGupta
speakers.title: Principal Product Manager, Technical - External Services, Amazon Web Services

title: Allianz: Scaling product reach with agentic commerce across channels
description: Customers increasingly start product discovery inside the AI assistants they use daily, and companies that aren't present miss them entirely. Learn how Allianz built a unified agentic-commerce backend on Amazon Bedrock, grounded in open standards. The same backend powers its own conversational AI across web and mobile and extends the same experience into third-party AI platforms through one AI gateway. We cover the agentic architecture and how shared MCP servers for corporate identity, GDPR compliance, consent, and authentication free business teams to focus on their core services. Customers discover products, get non-binding quotes, and connect to agencies across every channel.
location: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | White Theater

title: Amazon API Gateway: Migration strategies and agent-ready APIs
description: Unlock the full potential of Amazon API Gateway for modern workloads. In this chalk talk, we discuss migration strategies from legacy API platforms using OpenAPI extensions, schema validation, and Infrastructure as Code. Then we tackle the agentic era: how do you design APIs that AI agents can discover, authenticate against, and call reliably? We explore custom authorizers, mutual TLS, and exposing your endpoints as MCP-compatible tool definitions. Bring your questions—we'll work through them on the whiteboard.

speakers.name: Zac Burns
speakers.title: Senior Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services

title: Amazon Aurora architecture patterns for open table format analytics
description: Modern analytics architectures increasingly rely on open table formats like Apache Iceberg but combining operational and analytical data remains complex. This session explores emerging patterns for bridging Amazon Aurora with open table format analytics. Learn architectural patterns for bidirectional data flow between databases and data lakes. Topics include design patterns for analytical workloads, performance optimization and reverse ETL, and deep dives into maintaining transactional consistency when streaming database changes to Amazon S3 Tables, delivery guarantees, and type mapping.

speakers.name: Tim Stoakes
speakers.title: Sr. Principal Technologist, Amazon Web Services

title: Amazon Aurora DSQL: A developer's perspective
description: In this live coding session, we'll show you how to work with Amazon Aurora DSQL from a developer's perspective. We'll develop a sample application to highlight some of the ways developing for Aurora DSQL is different than PostgreSQL. We'll cover authentication and connection management, optimistic concurrency transaction patterns, primary key selection, analyzing query performance, and best practices.

speakers.name: Marc Bowes
speakers.title: Sr Principal Engineer, Amazon Web Services

title: Amazon Aurora HA and DR design patterns for global resilience
description: Amazon Aurora is a serverless relational database with unparalleled high performance and availability at global scale for PostgreSQL, MySQL, and DSQL. Aurora provides managed high availability (HA) and disaster recovery (DR) capabilities in and across AWS Regions. In this session, explore the Aurora HA and DR capabilities and discover design patterns that enable the development of resilient applications. Learn how to establish in-Region and cross-Region HA and DR using Aurora features including Multi-AZ deployments and Aurora Global Database, and how Aurora DSQL multi-Region clusters provides the highest level of availability and application resilience.
location: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

speakers.name: Tim Stoakes
speakers.title: Sr. Principal Technologist, Amazon Web Services

title: Amazon DocumentDB for expert practitioners
description: Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) is a fully managed database service for native document data model enterprise workloads. It removes the undifferentiated heavy lifting of operating a database so that teams can focus time on delivering value for customers. In this session, dive deep into the implementation details and trade-offs of features to improve compression and performance while lowering cost for various workloads.

speakers.name: Inderpreet Singh
speakers.title: Senior Product Manager - Tech, Amazon DocumentDB

description: Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) is a fully managed database service for native document data model enterprise workloads. title: Amazon DynamoDB: How to build a foundational service
description: Whether to take a dependency or reimplement something are important decisions in any system architecture, affecting performance, durability, and availability. Amazon DynamoDB serves millions of customers while also underpinning many AWS services, a dual role that forces rigorous decisions about dependencies, failure isolation, and multi-Region architecture. In this session, the DynamoDB engineering team walks through how those constraints shape architectural choices, including when DynamoDB uses DynamoDB to implement itself. The session presents a structured framework for dependency analysis, covering multi-zone and multi-Region tradeoffs, applicable to any system you build and operate, to help identify design risks before they become failures.
location: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

speakers.name: Amrith Kumar
speakers.title: Senior Principal Engineer, Amazon Web Services

title: Amazon EC2: New silicon, new instances, new possibilities
description: Amazon EC2 continues to push the boundaries of cloud compute. Join this session to explore the latest innovations — from new AWS Graviton processors to the newest Intel, AMD, and Mac instances built for demanding workloads. Hear how customers are using EC2 to accelerate application development, high-performance computing, and AI inference on the CPU. Learn how the AWS Nitro System delivers strong isolation and performance, and leave with practical guidance to match the right EC2 instance to your workload.
location: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

speakers.name: Scott Malkie
speakers.title: Specialist Solutions Architect, EC2, Amazon Web Services

speakers.name: Art Baudo
speakers.title: Principal Product Market Manager, AWS Village - Compute (EC2 / Graviton)

title: Amazon EKS incident response and remediation with AWS DevOps Agent
description: When an incident hits, engineers lose time pivoting between kubectl, metrics, logs, and traces to find root cause. In this builder session, you'll drive the AWS DevOps Agent through a production-realistic incident end to end: detect the anomaly from observability signals, correlate metrics, logs, and traces to a root cause, and execute automated remediation with a human-in-the-loop gate. You'll wire the observability inputs the agent consumes, review its diagnosis journal, and validate recovery. Leave with a repeatable detect-diagnose-remediate-verify pattern and a permission-scoped remediation playbook you can adapt to your own clusters.

title: Amazon EKS: Infrastructure as code, GitOps, or CI/CD
description: Explore diverse architectures for deploying workloads including agents on Amazon EKS. Learn about secure software supply chain automation options including CI/CD pipelines, IaC (using Terraform & CDK), and GitOps patterns with Argo CD. Discover how Amazon EKS Capabilities, a suite of fully-managed platform features for deployments and resource orchestration eliminate operational overhead for building on Kubernetes. You will understand how these approaches complement each other from developer, architect, and operator perspectives. Get insights on selecting the right deployment strategy based on team structure and skill sets, and learn how to effectively combine DevOps and GitOps patterns to match your needs.

description: Explore diverse architectures for deploying workloads including agents on Amazon EKS. Get insights on selecting the right deployment strategy based on team structure and skill sets, and learn how to effectively combine DevOps and GitOps patterns to match your needs.

title: Amazon EVS: How to deploy & operate your VMware stack in the cloud
description: What if you could rapidly migrate your VMware-based workloads to the cloud without giving up control over how you build, configure, and operate your environment? Amazon EVS lets you run the latest VMware Cloud Foundation software within your Amazon VPC using EC2 bare-metal instances. Use the tools and processes your team already knows, now backed by AWS scale and flexibility. Retain control of your virtualization stack, from networking and storage to disaster recovery. We'll walk through deployment workflows and integration patterns with AWS Partners and native AWS services. Hear lessons from a customer who fast-tracked their migration with EVS.
location: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Amazon Leo: Connectivity Beyond the Reach of Existing Networks (sponsored by Amazon Leo) (IND105-S)
description: Amazon Leo is building a constellation of over 3,200 low Earth orbit satellites to deliver fast, affordable broadband to unserved and underserved communities worldwide. In this session, learn how Leo's advanced satellite technology, purpose-built customer antennas, and deep integration with AWS will extend reliable connectivity to enterprises, governments, and individuals — wherever they are. Walk away with a clear understanding of Leo's architecture, use cases, and how it complements existing network infrastructure to close the global digital divide. This presentation is brought to you by Amazon Leo, an AWS Partner.
location: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: Amazon Linux: Securing and scaling your workloads on AWS
description: Amazon Linux powers the majority of workloads on AWS, from containers and AI/ML to enterprise applications and managed services. In this session, we introduce Amazon Linux 2027 (AL2027), cover its security enhancements, optimizations, and key features. Learn how AL2027 addresses the needs of modern AI/ML and container workloads, and what the roadmap means for your infrastructure planning. Whether you are planning a migration or evaluating your OS strategy, this session is for you.
location: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Amazon S3 cost optimization: when to tier, and when not to
description: Moving data to a colder storage class is the obvious way to cut Amazon S3 costs, but sometimes it makes your bill go up. Learn about the full cost model behind storage-class decisions: transition requests, minimum billable object sizes, per-object overhead, minimum durations, and retrieval. See why small objects, high-churn datasets, and request-heavy workloads are frequently cheaper left where they are, and how to spot them. Using S3 Storage Lens, S3 Inventory, and S3 Metadata, diagnose where you're spending and leave with clear guidance on when to tier, when to use S3 Intelligent-Tiering, and when to do nothing.
location: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | White Theater

speakers.name: Mark Twomey
speakers.title: Sr. WW Specialist SA Storage, Amazon Web Services

title: Amazon S3 performance: Architecture, design, and optimization
description: Go behind the scenes of Amazon S3 performance architecture while learning practical optimization strategies for today's most demanding workloads. Explore how internal systems for S3 manage massive throughput, handle concurrent requests, and balance loads across its distributed infrastructure. From request routing and partitioning strategies to multipart transfers and byte-range fetches, understand the technical foundations that power real-time analytics, AI/ML training, and high-frequency data pipelines. Then see how S3 Express One Zone extends these capabilities with consistent single-digit millisecond latency through directory buckets and compute co-location. Walk away with patterns to maximize performance at every tier.
location: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | White Theater

speakers.name: Jonathan Wong
speakers.title: Sr. Product Manager Technical (S3), Amazon Web Services (AWS)

title: Amazon S3 security and access control best practices
description: As organizations consolidate critical data in Amazon S3 across accounts, teams, and workloads, security and access control decisions multiply. Which identity model scales without becoming brittle? Where do you enforce encryption policy? How do you detect misconfigurations? This session walks you through a layered security framework for S3: perimeter controls that prevent unintended public exposure, identity and attribute-based access that scales across organizational boundaries, encryption options that satisfy compliance without adding operational friction, and monitoring that continuously validates your posture. You will learn how these layers compose into a cohesive strategy and which controls matter most as your environment grows.
location: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

speakers.name: Will Cavin
speakers.title: Principal Product Manager - Technical, Amazon Web Services

title: Amazon S3 security: Implementing access controls, policies & audits
description: Amazon S3 provides security settings and granular access controls to suit virtually any workload. In this workshop, learn how to manage access and define scalable user and resource-based policies using Amazon S3 access management tools. Learn techniques for monitoring and auditing data to find out who is accessing what data, from where, and when. Through practical scenarios, learn how to apply various S3 security tools and capabilities to meet diverse security requirements. Gain expertise in implementing robust security measures, from basic access controls to advanced audit systems, suitable for any workload complexity. Participants must bring a laptop for this session.

speakers.title: Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services

title: Amazon S3 Tables: A deep dive into storage built for Apache Iceberg
description: Amazon S3 Tables are setting a new standard for Apache Iceberg data lakes: fully managed, open, and AI-ready. In this session, learn everything you need to know about S3 Tables, from how we continuously optimize Iceberg tables as your data scales, to support for ingestion, migration, data protection, cost-efficiency, and performance. We’ll explore how S3 Tables make it easy for AI agents to build on Iceberg tables and dive into the latest re:Invent announcements. Hear real-world customer stories and walk away equipped to bring S3 Tables to your organization.
location: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | White Theater

title: Ambient accessibility: Architecting real-time ASL on a Wearable
description: What if a DHH person could wear a device and get sign language translation of every conversation around them in under a second? We architect a pipeline that ingests Amazon Bee's ambient audio, transcribes it, transforms English to ASL grammar, generates avatar animations, and streams signed video back. That one-second constraint drives every architectural tradeoff, from whether translation stages run on-device for speed or in the cloud for accuracy, to whether we sign full sentences or start mid-utterance with partial context. We explore the edge-cloud splits and pipeline staging that make sub-second delivery feasible.

speakers.name: Suresh Poopandi
speakers.title: Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services

title: Analyze your portfolio, prioritize what to fix, and transform it
description: You know your portfolio needs modernization, but which apps go first, and based on what criteria? In this workshop, you'll run the full analyze-prioritize-transform cycle end to end. Using AWS Transform's Agentic Readiness Analysis and Modernization Analysis, you'll evaluate applications from two angles: whether agents can safely reach your logic (API exposure, identity, state, guardrails, observability) and how cloud-native mature your architecture is (compute, data, security, operations). You'll interpret scores, scale across a portfolio with the orchestrator, then close the loop by triggering a containerization transformation on the app that needs it most. Laptop required.

title: An Epic Tale: Hyperscale Storage & Compute for the Fortnite Ecosystem
description: The metaverse will not be built by one studio. It will be built by thousands of teams shipping petabytes of content, running millions of build and render jobs across regions every day. The engineers behind Lore, Epic's distributed version control system for massive binary repositories, and Overmind, a multi-region ephemeral compute orchestrator, reveal the AWS architecture that makes it possible: self-managed scheduling on EC2, S3/DynamoDB/Keyspaces/Aurora for the data plane, EKS-hosted control planes running durable workflows, and MSK for replayable event streams. Leave with a concrete reference architecture and lessons on tenant isolation, regional sovereignty, and global platform scale.
location: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Orange Theater

speakers.name: Paul Sharpe
speakers.title: Technical Director, Cloud, Epic Games, Inc.

title: An insider’s look into architecture choices for Amazon DynamoDB
description: To overcome the performance and scale limitations of relational databases, AWS built Amazon DynamoDB to deliver single-digit millisecond performance at any scale - whether your application has tens of thousands or hundreds of millions of simultaneous users - for the most demanding applications on the planet. In this session, learn how some basic data structure decisions led to these characteristics. And how those same decisions provide immutable, point-in-time restore. Leave with a better understanding of why DynamoDB can operate at the scale it does, and a framework on how to use it for decisions in your own applications.

title: Answering CX questions 10x faster with Amazon Connect Customer and Amazon Quick
description: Amazon Connect Customer generates a deep set of signals from every customer interaction. Sentiment, intent, conversation analytics, resolution outcomes. It's all there and Connect Customer gives you built-in tools to explore it. But we wanted to go further. We wanted anyone in the organization to ask questions about customer interactions in plain language and get answers instantly. So we paired Connect Customer's analytics data lake with Amazon Quick. In this session, we walk through how we did it, including how we handled cross-account Lake Formation access, and show how our broader team now asks questions and reshapes queries on the fly. 10x faster from question to action.

title: Aon: Turning raw exposure data into faster underwriting
description: Insurers and brokers process thousands of Statements of Values annually, complex unstructured documents that require manual extraction and validation and delay quoting and bind decisions. In this lightning talk, learn how Aon built an AI-powered exposure data ingestion platform on Amazon Bedrock using Anthropic Claude, AWS Lambda, and Amazon S3. See how the platform transforms unstructured data into standardized, risk-ready information with improved address quality, geocoding precision, and hazard identification, reducing document processing from days to minutes and feeding higher-quality inputs to catastrophe models.

title: Apache Iceberg V3 on AWS: Lower Costs, Better Lakehouse Performance

Learn when deletion vectors outperform copy-on-write, how row lineage enables compliance without extra pipelines, and how V3 incremental processing cuts batch costs. title: Apache Iceberg V4: Fast commits, smart metadata, and portable tables

We'll walk through what's changing under the hood and what it means for the way you design and operate lakehouses. Discover how V4 delivers the speed and flexibility modern lakehouses demand.

In this chalk talk, the session walks through the AWS Well-Architected Framework pillar by pillar, exploring how each applies and where it bends at the edge. Bring your toughest design questions. description: Organizations deploying AI face a critical decision at every step. Which service handles which job, and will those decisions hold up as you scale? We cover model access patterns (API, custom model import, marketplace), deployment trade-offs between self-managed and fully managed inference, and cost-performance optimization at production scale.

title: Architecting anti-piracy defenses for video streaming with Amazon CloudFront
description: Modern streaming demands instant revocation, concurrent stream limits, device-bound sessions, and per-user policy decisions at the edge. In this chalk talk, whiteboard the full decision space with us. We'll map the trade-offs between signed URLs, signed cookies, and emerging token approaches like Content Access Tokens (CAT) built on CBOR Web Tokens, then diagram the architecture patterns behind them: embedding custom claims and evaluating them in CloudFront Functions, using CloudFront KeyValueStore for real-time revocation without key rotation, and chaining tokens across HLS/DASH segments. Bring your hardest content protection scenarios, such as credential sharing, restreaming, geo abuse. We'll work through them together at the board, leaving you with a framework for matching protection mechanisms to your security and business requirements.

title: Architecting Enterprise Agents on Bedrock
description: Enterprise agents on Amazon Bedrock are complex distributed systems, combining models, tools, memory, and orchestration into something that has to behave predictably in production. In this session, I walk through practical architecture patterns for building enterprise-grade agents: multi-agent coordination, tool routing, session management, and hybrid workflows using AWS Step Functions and AWS Lambda. Drawing from real production systems, I cover the trade-offs that matter most when moving agents from prototype to production, where reliability and scale actually get tested. Walk away with concrete patterns you can bring back to your own agent architecture.

It examines how data residency boundaries, network separation, operational controls, and cryptographic key management differ across these options, then demonstrates how to configure account access, data residency controls, and network ingress/egress policies for strict versus moderate requirements, including how to detect and prevent non-permitted data flows between hybrid infrastructure, the parent Region, and on-premises environments.

title: Architecting for non-deterministic components
description: Our systems used to behave the same way every time. Now we give them judgment and agency, so they decide and act on their own, and the same inputs can produce different outcomes. Designing reliable architectures around that non-determinism comes down to three questions: where to enforce determinism around the model, when to verify behavior through automated evaluation and reasoning versus human judgment, and how to adapt the patterns (event flows, orchestration, automation) for components that don’t behave predictably. This session presents the design patterns for building systems that decide and act, while preserving the reliability your architecture depends on.

It then expands to multi-site interconnections spanning Outposts and AWS Local Zones, extended VPC designs, and resilient architectures grounded in AWS Well-Architected principles. It closes with bare metal instances using high-throughput accelerated networking, kernel bypass, network interface card (NIC) selection, and rack topology for co-located workloads where every microsecond matters. description: TPublishers sit on enormous archives: decades of articles, millions of photos, entire histories of coverage. Most of it is invisible the moment someone needs more than a keyword match. ArcXP built Ask the News to close that gap: a standalone, API-first product giving publishers natural-language access to their own content, powered by MongoDB Atlas Vector Search. The system combines lexical and vector search so results reflect what was meant, not what was said. One of the hardest parts was visual: a pipeline that generated descriptions and embeddings for roughly five million historical images, making decades of archives searchable by meaning for the first time. You'll leave understanding a working pattern for combining lexical and vector search, and a model for exposing natural-language search as an API-first product, not a bolt-on feature. You leave with a recovery validation approach and an understanding of why least privilege, vault lock, and validation are non-negotiable.

title: Attesting to Secrets in Zero Knowledge
description: It is possible to prove factual statements about systems to observers without revealing any details about those systems beyond the stated claims. This is surprising, but not as surprising as the fact that it is borderline practical using Zero Knowledge Proofs. This talk will give an overview of the mathematical foundations of Zero Knowledge Proofs and introduce both interactive and non-interactive proof schemes. It will then dive into the details of some of the current general purpose Zero Knowledge proof systems (e.g., zk-SNARK and zk-STARK) and show how to use Zero Knowledge libraries to attest to (or prove) properties of software systems without sharing the implementations of those systems.

title: AWS Lambda MicroVMs: Strong isolation for agents & beyond
description: Agents running generated code, multi-tenant platforms, and untrusted workloads all need strong isolation, but each traditional compute option forces a tradeoff. description: In this talk, we’ll walk through an independent eval of Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, which manages the ingestion, parsing, and retrieval steps in a RAG application. In the first half, we’ll cover our methodology, including how we developed a dataset that queries documents such as tickets, wiki pages, and product docs, and what we decided to score: latency, cost, relevance, and citation support. We’ll also cover how we analyzed the results with research rigor, including p50 and p95 latency and confidence intervals around our metrics. In the second half, we’ll expand this into a conceptual understanding of evals and observability: why they’re important, how other companies are implementing them in production, and the terminology you need to know. This presentation is brought to you by Braintrust, an AWS Partner.

title: Beyond Benchmarks: Evaluating AI Safety with Formal Guarantees
description: As AI systems become increasingly capable and autonomous, safety evaluation is emerging as a critical challenge. While current evaluations largely rely on benchmark performance and empirical red-teaming, these approaches provide limited guarantees about real-world risk. This talk will explore an emerging direction in AI safety: evaluating model behavior with formal statistical guarantees. We will discuss how ideas from reliability engineering, robustness certification, and risk assessment can be applied to quantify catastrophic failure probabilities, the assumptions behind such guarantees, and their implications for deploying and governing frontier AI systems. This topic is highly relevant to the future of trustworthy and accountable AI.

title: Beyond chatbots: Event-driven AI agents on Apache Flink
description: Most AI agents wait for a prompt. Apache Flink Agents flips that—agents react autonomously to live event streams as Flink operators, with exactly-once guarantees, durable state, and millisecond latency. Learn how this event-driven foundation differs from request-response frameworks, then see an ops agent detect a failing Flink job, diagnose it with an LLM on Amazon Bedrock, retrieve a runbook, and remediate—no human in the loop. Hear from Flink committers on production agents at Alibaba and LinkedIn, and from AWS contributors building Bedrock and other AWS integrations upstream.

We'll design and build with Kiro, pay down tech debt with AWS Transform, catch vulnerabilities early with AWS Continuum (formerly known as AWS Security Agent), ship through safe CI/CD pipelines, and resolve production issues with AWS DevOps Agent—then feed what we learn back into the next task. description: Deploying AI voice agents beyond English introduces unique challenges: accent handling, language detection, code-switching between languages mid-conversation, and cultural nuances in conversation flow. title: Beyond RSA: Post-quantum data encryption using ML-KEM in AWS KMS
description: RSA and Elliptic Curve Cryptography secure nearly every application today, and both are vulnerable to future cryptographically relevant quantum computers. Data captured now can be decrypted later, so applications needing long-term confidentiality should adopt post-quantum encryption well before those computers arrive. AWS KMS now offers ML-KEM, the NIST-standardized replacement for RSA and ECDH key establishment and ultimately encryption under asymmetric keys. It protects the private keys in FIPS 140-3 Level 3 HSMs. In this session, learn about ML-KEM and how to use it as a building block for quantum-safe encryption using Hybrid Public Key Encryption (HPKE).

title: Build a Live App in Under 20 Minutes, Then See How It Actually Worked (sponsored by MongoDB) (AIM397-S)
description: Most teams know what they want to build long before they have something they can show someone. This workshop gets you there fast, then shows you what's behind that build. First, you'll build a real app. Using MongoDB Build Lab from your laptop, turn an idea (a search tool, an AI assistant, a dashboard, anything) into a working, deployed app backed by MongoDB Atlas. title: Build an agentic AI system on Amazon EKS with CPU-only inference
description: In this workshop, build a multi-agent AI system on Amazon EKS with EKS Auto Mode that serves every model on CPU instances. Deploy four inference components: a fine-tuned intent router and a fine-tuned embedding model for vector search (both ONNX, trained on CPU), a cross-encoder re-ranker for retrieval quality, and a quantized generative analyst served with llama.cpp and grounded by RAG context from OpenSearch. Amazon Bedrock generates the synthetic training data, judges every answer through a faithfulness gate, and answers the edge cases the small models cannot. You'll finish by running the control test that puts a frontier LLM in the same seat, so you know whether the small model is good enough on your workload. By the end, you'll have a working multi-agent system on standard compute, using open-source tooling you can adapt.

title: Build a security boundary for AI agents with WAF and Network Firewall
description: AI agents built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore accept untrusted input and make outbound API calls, creating both ingress and egress attack surfaces. title: Build a security boundary for AI agents with WAF and Network Firewall

In this builders' session, learn to close both gaps with AWS managed controls. Put AWS WAF Bot Control in front of your Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway to classify callers and admit only the classes you choose, then route the agent through AWS Network Firewall and use domain category filtering to decide which destination categories it may reach. Run each control in count or alert mode, then enforce it and verify the allowed and the refused path. Leave with a two-boundary pattern you can apply to your own agent deployments.

In this chalk talk, discuss design principles for agentic Serverless: single-responsibility tools with clear input/output schemas, MCP-compatible interfaces for universal agent consumption, and multi-tenant isolation that keeps workloads secure. We'll whiteboard the trade-offs that matter—provisioned concurrency versus on-demand cold starts, cost per invocation at agent scale, and where Serverless fits versus where you need different compute.

description: Most data stacks were built for dashboards, not AI. Duplicated pipelines, competing definitions, and slow reporting make it difficult to deliver the fresh, trusted, governed data AI demands. Learn how a fast growing organization replaced engineering heavy operations with a self serve model built on AWS, Fivetran, and dbt. Understand how to standardize ingestion, apply governed transformations and semantic definitions, and cut pipeline development from months to days. You'll walk away with a practical approach to freeing engineering time, providing business teams with trusted access to data, and building a governed foundation that scales AI from experiments to production. description: This session explores how Vercel and AWS work together to support the development and deployment of AI agents. You’ll learn about first party connectivity to AWS databases and services through the Vercel Marketplace, along with the backend capabilities agents need, including APIs, durable workflows, queues, cron jobs, and MCP servers. You’ll see how these building blocks, together with the EVE framework, can simplify agent development, followed by a live demo showing how to build an agent using Vercel and AWS. description: Ever get a text that your Mastercard was used in a transaction you didn't make? We then introduce the Lightsail Partner Program and the benefits available to partners who build their practice on Lightsail. Bring your scenarios. We'll work through partner economics, discuss real use cases, and how Lightsail helps partners tackle onboarding and scaling challenges. You'll leave with a clearer understanding of how to leverage Lightsail to build your partner business.

title: Building a private service fabric across AWS accounts and orgs
description: Deploying workloads across AWS accounts, whether across an organization, between business units, or alongside acquired entities, creates connectivity complexity that traditional networking options don't cleanly solve. You face IP coordination headaches, overly broad network surface exposure, and heavy per-resource infrastructure just to share a service privately. Bidirectional sharing doubles the problem. In this session, build a private service fabric, a federated architecture where multiple organizations share services privately and bidirectionally with independent governance. Combine Amazon VPC Lattice, resource gateways, AWS PrivateLink, and AWS Resource Access Manager into a cross-organization platform covering bidirectional topologies and federated governance.

We'll work through architecture patterns for defining semantic data annotations, propagating semantics across lakehouse tables, and exposing discoverable, agent-ready metadata at query time.

description: Quantum computers could revolutionize fields like pharmacy and logistics, but today's hardware is too error-prone for practical use. In this talk, we demonstrate quantum processor digital twins developed by Quantum Elements and powered by AWS HPC infrastructure - that faithfully mimic real hardware at experimental scale. Attendees will leave understanding why error correction matters and how classical compute accelerates the path to useful quantum computing.

title: Building event-driven, multi-agent swarms on serverless
description: Multi-agent AI systems need communication that is decoupled, observable, and scalable. In this chalk talk, we show how to coordinate swarms of independent agents through event choreography on Amazon EventBridge. Each agent reacts to events and emits new ones rather than being told what to do by a central controller. We discuss how to handle multi-agent failure modes like cascading hallucinations and runaway event loops (circular delegation), and how to prevent independent agents from taking conflicting actions.

title: Building fast with automated reasoning at Amazon S3 scale
description: S3 has a long history of using automated reasoning, but a core challenge has been applying these techniques to large systems while maintaining development velocity. Over time, we've learned to balance cutting-edge science with engineering velocity to accelerate development. We'll share diverse techniques for validating critical storage components, from black-box model-based validation using formal API specifications, to white-box verification with specialized concurrency checkers for ensuring transaction serializability and crash consistency. You'll learn how S3 engineers and scientists are advancing systems verification with new tools and ideas that you can apply to your own systems.

Using scenarios drawn from recent large-scale events, examine trade-offs between consistency, latency, and availability, and discover operational best practices for detecting, responding to, and recovering from failures.

title: Build layered defenses for agentic AI from prompt to tool execution
description: Attendees build a defense-in-depth security architecture for an AI agent. You start with a pre-deployed Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway with Lambda tools, then run adversarial test scenarios to observe how gateway and tools respond without controls. You layer defenses from Bedrock Guardrails for prompt-attack detection, through AgentCore Policy Engine with Cedar policies-based tool authorization, including Dogwood temporal policies, and finally native rate limits paired with CloudWatch anomaly detection. By progressing through each scenario again, you verify how each protection aligns with a layered security pattern you can apply to your agentic workload.

title: Build long-running agents that persist for days on AgentCore
description: Most agents handle a single request and forget everything. Production workloads are different — an incident investigation spans hours, a document review takes days, a customer onboarding stretches across weeks. These agents need to persist state, survive restarts, and pick up exactly where they left off. This session covers how to build long-running agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore using Runtime for durable execution and Memory for cross-session context. Learn checkpointing patterns, human-in-the-loop pause and resume, and cost strategies that keep idle agents from burning through your budget.

title: Build ransomware recovery with AWS Backup air-gapped vaults

Participants must bring a laptop.

title: Build stateful agentic AI workflows with Aurora, MCP, and AgentCore
description: Most agentic AI architectures stitch together separate stores for vectors and workflow state, adding cost and operational overhead. In this session, explore how Aurora PostgreSQL consolidates these roles into a single database, using pgvector for semantic retrieval, PostgreSQL full-text search for keyword queries, and native state persistence for multi-agent checkpointing. Learn to connect agents directly to Aurora using Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, govern every interaction with row-level security and audit trails, and orchestrate resilient, stateful workflows with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Strands Agents, and LangGraph without additional infrastructure. Build with tested patterns for governed, real-time agentic systems.

This session shows AWS developers how to ship on the modern Slack Platform: Code Channels, a new space where agents like Claude Code, Devin, and Cursor collaborate with teams in real time; the Slack Agent Kit for building first-class agents; deep bidirectional MCP support, including the Slackbot MCP Client; Real-Time Search (RTS) for grounding agents in live workspace context; and Block Kit for rich, interactive UI. title: Build the full agent optimization loop on AgentCore
description: How do you know your agent is still performing? Stop guessing. This workshop walks you through the full optimization loop on AgentCore: instrument with OpenTelemetry traces, score with built-in and custom evaluators, generate data-backed recommendations that rewrite your system prompt or tool descriptions, validate offline with batch evaluation, then split live traffic with A/B testing through AgentCore Gateway until you have statistical confidence to promote. You will run every step hands-on, ship a measurably better agent configuration, and leave with a repeatable process that replaces guess-and-check prompt iteration with evidence.

title: Build the Patient Record Your Healthcare AI Agents Actually Need
description: The average US patient has records scattered across 40+ systems. Medication lists conflict, allergies are duplicated, and clinical notes contradict structured data. Every AI agent you connect downstream inherits that mess. In this builder session, you use AWS HealthLake to resolve patient identities across fragmented sources, normalize clinical concepts to SNOMED/LOINC/RxNorm, and produce a unified, queryable FHIR record. Then you use a unified SDK to wire Amazon Connect Health agents to your clean data layer, simulate a patient encounter, and generate a structured clinical note that writes back to HealthLake. You leave with a deployable data foundation that accelerates Connect Health agent integration today and supports any custom agent you choose to connect tomorrow.

title: Build the Right Next Thing: A Forward Deployed Approach to AI ROI (sponsored by Slalom) (AIM283-S)
description: Two years ago, standing up generative AI technology was the hard part. Today, Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore make the path to production more straightforward—but technology alone does not create value. AI initiatives often stall because ROI is undefined and business, user, and technical priorities are disconnected. Learn how Slalom’s Forward Deployed Expertise (FDX) model places a cross-functional team spanning product, business, industry, UX, and technology alongside customers. Using real data, these teams compare opportunities, prioritize the highest-value use cases, and co-build the right next thing through production, adoption, and measurable outcomes. title: Build-time context for faster agentic incident response
description: AI agents can fix production issues, but only with the right context. In this talk, an AI agent builds a feature and, in the same pull request, creates the context it needs on call: instrumentation, alarms, dashboards, and skills, all as code. Then you break the live app. Watch an agent use those skills with Amazon CloudWatch Omni and AWS DevOps Agent to triage, find the root cause, and ship the fix. Leave with patterns that give agents the context to operate what they build.

title: Build Trust in AI with Agent Observability​ (sponsored by Splunk, a Cisco Company) (AIM109-S)
description: AI agents behave (and fail) in unpredictable and nuanced ways that erode customer trust before engineering teams know anything is wrong. Teams want to deploy agents into critical business workflows, but it's hard to know if agents are behaving as intended or returning wrong answers.​ ​ In this talk, you’ll learn how to observe the entire AI stack, optimize tokenomics, and see a demo on how to evaluate and control agent behavior with guardrails to stop harmful or inaccurate outputs. All of this can be done in near real- time and at low cost.​ This presentation is brought to you by Splunk, a Cisco Company, an AWS Partner.

title: Build voice-enabled applications with Amazon Polly and Amazon Transcribe

With Transcribe, you'll turn speech into text for captions, search, and analytics, handling real-time streaming and batch workloads. We'll show how these services work together to power voice agents, accessibility features, and conversational experiences, giving your applications the ability to both speak and listen naturally across a wide range of use cases and customer scenarios.

title: Built by Agents: Rethinking Reliability for AI-Native Companies (sponsored by Traversal) (DVT101-S)
description: AI is changing how quickly software can be built, shipped, and scaled. For AI-native companies, that can mean more services and complexity earlier in their growth. Many traditional reliability practices were designed for a different pace, when teams had more time to document, instrument, and build operational knowledge as they scaled. This conversation brings together leaders from a fast-growing legal AI company and one of the world’s largest digital banks, alongside leaders from Traversal, the AI SRE that diagnoses, fixes, and prevents incidents across enterprise environments. They’ll discuss how AI is changing development and operations, new failure modes in AI-native systems, how lean teams approach reliability as they scale, and the role of AI SREs in a broader shift toward AI understanding, managing, and improving production systems. This presentation is brought to you by Traversal, an AWS Partner.

title: Canva's migration to AWS Graviton: from 2% to 54% in 10 months

Walk away with practical, battle-tested patterns for planning and executing large-scale Arm migrations, whether you're just getting started or looking to accelerate an existing effort.

title: Cell-based architecture: Designing blast-radius boundaries
description: Cell-based architecture limits the blast radius of failures by partitioning systems into independent, isolated units. But deciding cell boundaries — by customer, geography, or workload — involves trade-offs between operational complexity and fault isolation. This session reveals the decision framework for cell sizing, routing, and cross-cell coordination. You'll learn when cells outperform active-active patterns, how to implement cell-aware deployments, and the true operational cost of cell management. Walk away with a reusable pattern for systems, where failures stay contained, impact reduced, and availability increased.

title: Charting the AI Search Frontier: From Retrieval to Reasoning
description: Large language models have shifted expectations about search: from retrieving documents to answering questions directly; from single-type data to multi-modal data; from one-shot lookup to multi-step reasoning. This is the new frontier of search empowered by AI. What should you know about the AI Search frontier? How can you make AI search provide the highest accuracy on your data, while keeping latency and costs in check? Join us to chart the course — and leave with a practical map.

title: Choosing a game server instance without guessing
description: Most game studios pick server instances by vibes. This chalk talk replaces that with a number you measure on your game: cost per player at your tick rate. At the whiteboard we answer three questions: what does one tick cost, how many players fit, and what does a player cost? You’ll see how to time the whole tick in Unreal Engine and Unity, load a server with bots or thin clients against a failure rule set up front, and repeat across instances. Then we share what we measured on modern Amazon EC2 instances across AWS Graviton, AMD, and Intel: where clock speed pays, and where price decides.

title: Choosing the right AWS storage for low-latency workloads
description: Not all latency-sensitive workloads have the same storage requirements. From AI/ML training checkpoints to real-time analytics and high-frequency data pipelines, choosing between Amazon S3 Express One Zone, Amazon FSx for Lustre, and instance storage depends on access patterns, throughput needs, and cost constraints. title: Coding high-throughput data pipelines with AWS Lambda durable functions
description: Processing large datasets usually means hand-wiring queues, coordinators, and state tracking. In this code talk, we live-build a high-throughput data pipeline with Lambda durable functions instead. You'll see the fan-out/fan-in pattern in code: split a large dataset across parallel durable executions, isolate and retry the branches that fail without reprocessing the ones that succeeded, and offload checkpoints to S3 so a job too big for a single invocation survives restarts. We'll tune concurrency to protect a downstream database from overload, then compare the durable-functions approach with other design patterns on both developer velocity and cost. Leave with patterns you can apply to your own data workloads immediately.

You create scoped IAM execution roles with permissions boundaries, enforce mandatory Amazon Bedrock Guardrails through IAM policy, validate agent policies with IAM Access Analyzer, and add deterministic Cedar enforcement in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. The result constrains what agents can do while still letting legitimate actions through.

title: Content at the Speed of Live: AI-Powered Media Ops at Live Nation
description: Live Nation's subsidiaries generate petabytes of live event content across siloed storage. When an artist creates a viral moment, teams need it in fans' hands in minutes not days. In this session, learn how Live Nation built a platform that unifies fragmented media silos so teams can search, create, and publish in near-real time. Built using the guidance for a Media Lake on AWS, along with Amazon Bedrock, the platform uses AI-driven moment detection to surface key content automatically. We cover architecture, lessons from festival-scale deployment, and impact on fan experience.

description: An agent's context window is a finite attention budget, and database-backed agents must keep that context current, selective, and traceable. In this session, architect solutions to trace a task as it builds context using Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey, Amazon Neptune, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Examine how agents cache hot state, retrieve operational rows, apply SQL filters, maintain vector and full-text indexes, refresh stale records, traverse knowledge-graph relationships, load skills, and discover MCP tools. Explore freshness policies, invalidation, provenance ledgers, access boundaries, and compaction patterns for production-grade agentic applications.

title: Context engineering for production agents on AgentCore
description: An agent is only as good as what fills its context window. System prompts, skills, tool definitions, conversation history, retrieved documents, long-term memory, they all compete for limited space. Get the mix wrong and you waste tokens, degrade reasoning, or lose critical instructions mid-conversation. This chalk talk breaks down every layer of context that shapes agent behavior on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. We cover how to structure system prompts, define skills effectively, manage tool context through gateway, retain the right conversation history, and use Memory strategies to persist what matters across sessions. Bring your agents, we optimize them live.

title: Context Over Code: Making AI-Native Development Work at Scale
description: AI coding assistants generate code quickly, but that's not the problem most teams need solved. After rolling out an AI coding companion to 150+ engineers, we learned the real unlock was rethinking how we work, not how fast we type. This session covers our path from AI code companion to AI-Driven Development Lifecycle: building a Context Store with Bedrock Knowledge Bases and MCP to surface decades of institutional knowledge, implementing steering and verification patterns, and managing the organizational change that makes AI-native development stick. You'll leave with a framework for scaling AI beyond individual productivity.
location: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Context to Action: Turning Agent Memory into a Customer Retention Lever (sponsored by MongoDB) (AIM246-S)
description: When a customer calls, a support rep has seconds to understand what they need, what device they're on, and how to solve it fast. Get it right, and you earn trust. Get it wrong, and churn becomes a real risk. T-Mobile closes that gap with agent memory: session context pre-populated before the call starts, enriched turn by turn as it unfolds, with real-time graph traversal connecting customer, device, and issue so the rep sees the full picture. MongoDB Atlas runs it all, from vector search over T-Mobile's knowledge corpus to in-call graph traversal to the live session-memory documents. Afterward, AWS Neptune turns that history into a graph shaping future routing and retention. Walk away with an architecture pattern for building agent memory in real time, and a way to decide what belongs in short-term memory versus what should persist. Featuring T-Mobile, presented by MongoDB. This presentation is brought to you by MongoDB, an AWS Partner.
location: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Continuous Attack Chains Across Every Surface (sponsored by Terra) (SEC224-S)
description: Most security tools score vulnerabilities in isolation, but attackers do not think in isolation. This session shows how Terra continuously chains signals into real attack paths across web applications, APIs, AI systems, and network infrastructure using agentic AI, the same way a human adversary would pivot from one weak point to the next. Every proposed chain is validated by an expert human pentester before it becomes a finding, turning a pile of low severity noise into a small number of confirmed, exploitable risks. Learn how continuous, cross surface attack chaining changes what a security team should actually prioritize first. This presentation is brought to you by Terra, an AWS Partner.
location: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) on AWS
description: Whether you're shipping a monolith or hundreds of microservices, every change needs to reach production safely and quickly. AWS gives you a unified set of tools to plan, build, test, and deploy code—with safety woven into every stage. In this session, learn how to assemble end-to-end CI/CD pipelines using infrastructure as code, then layer in safe-deployment strategies—canary and linear traffic shifting, automated CloudWatch alarm gates, and one-click stage rollbacks—so you can release with confidence and recover in seconds when something goes wrong.
location: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | White Theater

title: Controlling the AI Software Factory (sponsored by LaunchDarkly) (DVT221-S)
description: AI isn't just making software faster; it's changing how software is produced. Engineering teams now run agents that write code, review PRs, validate releases, and deploy around the clock. The promise is real, but so is a new problem: how do you stay in control of systems that never stop evolving? Edith Harbaugh, CEO of LaunchDarkly, argues the defining challenge of the AI era isn't generating code, it's controlling autonomous systems in production, where agents drift and the old detect-fix-redeploy playbook breaks down. She'll share what LaunchDarkly learned building its own AI software factory, and how engineers stay in charge. This presentation is brought to you by LaunchDarkly, an AWS Partner.
location: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Control what goes out: egress security for AI workloads
description: Most AWS workloads send traffic out in two ways, DNS queries and network connections, and attackers can abuse both to exfiltrate data. This session shows how to lock down both paths. We cover DNS Firewall enhancements for the DNS path, Network Firewall improvements for outbound connection control, and how running DNS Firewall and Network Firewall together gives you one view of DNS security. We also cover URL and domain categories, managed threat intelligence, and extending egress protection to containerized and AI workloads.
location: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Conversational AI to accelerate Apache Spark operations on Amazon EMR
description: Customers manage dozens of Apache Spark applications on Amazon EMR — and every major upgrade, unexpected failure, or performance regression pulls engineers away into reactive firefighting. In this workshop, experience a fundamentally different approach with AI-powered agents that handle the undifferentiated heavy lifting of Spark modernization and incident resolution. You'll work hands-on with conversational agents such as the Apache Spark Upgrade Agent and the Apache Spark Troubleshooting Agent across real-world scenarios on EMR Serverless and EMR on EC2 to simplify the operational burden through natural language, automated code transformation, workload analysis and data quality validation.

title: Core banking agent-ready: From composable to agentic financial services on AWS
description: The shift from composable to agentic banking is a re-architecture. Discover the reference architecture for turning a core banking platform into an intelligent core with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for orchestration, Amazon ECS for the control plane, Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases for domain context, and Amazon EventBridge for event-driven ingestion. We explore two consumption patterns ISVs can offer bank customers: exposing core banking APIs to customer-owned agents, and shipping a managed agentic layer for conversational AI and autonomous lending, deposit, and payment operations, eliminating up to 70% of repetitive manual work. Learn the hard-won lessons on infrastructure, governance, and product differentiation.

title: Correlate app signals to infra root cause in hybrid environments
description: Your app is slow, but is it the code, the container, or the underlying host? When your stack spans clouds, hybrid, and on-prem, correlating application performance to infrastructure health means jumping between tools and guessing at root cause. Join this session as we walk through how to map application signals such as traces, errors, and latency directly to the infrastructure, regardless of where it runs. You'll see how to pinpoint whether the problem is your app or the compute it sits on, without stitching dashboards together manually.

title: Correlate database query latency to user impact
description: Diagnosing performance degradation across distributed applications requires more than isolated database or application metrics. It demands correlated, end-to-end telemetry. This code talk demonstrates a scenario that unifies database performance signals with application-layer telemetry using OpenTelemetry and Amazon CloudWatch. Learn how to implement trace-to-query correlation, design log aggregation patterns for accelerated root cause analysis, and build metric relationships that surface bottlenecks across the full stack. You'll be able to connect a slow database query to its downstream user impact.
