title: Cost-effective serverless data integrations and workflows for AI-ready data
description: AI is only as good as the data beneath it and building high-quality, well-integrated data products shouldn't break your budget. In this session, learn how to build cost-effective AI-ready datasets using AWS Glue, Amazon MWAA and Apache Iceberg. We'll show how Glue Data Quality and Glue serverless ETL, now with generative AI-assisted development, lets you ingest, transform, and prepare high-quality data at scale. We’ll demonstrate how Amazon MWAA serverless empowers a single DAG to coordinate workloads across AWS Glue, and other engines - all of this while paying only for what you use. Pairing this setup with Apache Iceberg further enhances your AI workloads with query-ready production data pipelines that move the needle without breaking the bank.
location: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | White Theater

title: Cost optimization for Amazon DynamoDB
description: Developers love building on powerful, serverless Amazon DynamoDB, and as their production tables grow in size and traffic, they want to discover what mechanisms and optimizations can be applied to reduce costs. Cost optimization can be done both in the design phase and during operations. In this session, learn how to model and measure costs, explore Database Savings Plans to reduce spend on predictable workloads, and discover cost optimization tools that can help you along the way.

title: Craft, Don’t Vibe, Your MVP
description: Many people today use LLMs only for code generation. The best teams embrace AI across all stages of the SDLC. The decisions made before building the first version of your product directly affect its viability and success. Rather than relying on vibe coding to make these decisions implicitly, agents can be used to evaluate architectural options, compare trade-offs and challenge assumptions before a single line of code is created. This session explores how high-performing teams are investing time capturing standards, patterns and expertise, making them available for agents to apply consistently. Learn from practical real world examples how AI is being used to accelerate the delivery of production-ready systems, rather than those that carry technical debt from day one.

title: Creating resilient multi-channel customer experiences for NAB with Amazon Connect (sponsored by Deloitte) (AIM225-S)
description: National Australia Bank (NAB) modernized its digital customer service capability by migrating priority banker groups from legacy messaging platforms to Amazon Connect Chat. The transformation delivered a scalable, integrated, and future-ready messaging environment while improving banker productivity, operational control, and reporting capabilities, and enabling a pathway to enhanced self-service and assisted-service experiences. Deloitte led the end-to-end migration through a structured release approach, encompassing experience design, backlog and epic management, governance, business readiness, training, cutover planning, and operational risk management using AWS services. This session explores the strategy, execution, and lessons learned from delivering a successful enterprise messaging transformation. This presentation is brought to you by Deloitte, an AWS Partner.

title: Crossing the kill chain: IR when attackers pivot between clouds
description: When a threat actor compromises credentials in one cloud and pivots into another, the kill chain crosses boundaries that no single-cloud tool can follow. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard the detection and response patterns for cross-cloud lateral movement using Security Hub, Inspector, and multicloud telemetry sources.

title: Cross-modal search with Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings
description: Build search and RAG that understand more than text. In this hands-on workshop, you'll use Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings that embeds text, documents, images, video, and audio into one semantic space for cross-modal retrieval. You'll generate embeddings across modalities, load them into a vector store, and build a working app that searches with text, an image, or an audio clip and retrieves relevant results from any modality. We'll cover indexing strategies, query routing, and accuracy tuning for production agentic RAG. Bring your laptop.

title: Crypto escape room: race to migrate to quantum resistance
description: The migration to post-quantum cryptography is underway and here's a chance to hone your skills. In this gamified builders' session, each team races a countdown clock through different cryptographic migration challenges: TLS endpoint migration, ML-DSA key for code signing, quantum ready PKI, and an audit of your PQ posture. Teams complete quests using the AWS Key Management Service (KMS), AWS Private Certificate Authority, and AWS Secrets Manager services. A live leaderboard tracks progress across teams. Leave with new skills and the confidence to build quantum-resistant cryptographic infrastructure.

title: Cryptographic computing on AWS: homomorphic encryption in practice
description: What if your customers' data needs to stay invisible even to you? Cryptographic computing makes computation on encrypted data without decrypting it possible. Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) has become practical for ML inference. In this session, learn what FHE is, why it now works at scale on AWS, and how to get started. We will walk through two examples: encrypted ML inference on medical images and financial transactions, and encrypted ETL that aggregates records without exposing individual values. Leave with a deployment blueprint built for regulated industries.

title: Customize and serve models at scale on Amazon EKS
description: Serving and customizing models in production often involves running expensive GPUs at high utilization, maintaining low latency as traffic spikes, and scaling to demand without over-provisioning. Increasingly teams are doing it on Amazon EKS. This session covers how to efficiently run GPU workloads, select the right accelerator for each workload, and apply optimization techniques that increase utilization and lower costs. Explore model customization through fine-tuning and RAG, and serving and autoscaling patterns that keep inference fast and efficient. See how hybrid workloads span cloud and on-premises GPUs with EKS Hybrid Nodes and where AWS is investing next.

title: Customize open models for accuracy, cost, and latency on SageMaker AI
description: An off-the-shelf model may not meet the accuracy, cost, or latency requirements of your specialized business task. In this session, see how a new first-party application gives Accounts Payable teams one live view of purchase orders, invoices and payments matched against billing records no console login required.

description: AI agents degrade as conversations exceed context windows. You need retrieval strategies, compression policies, and adaptive storage backends. We'll explore trade-offs between framework and agent-controlled context, how plugins compose without coupling, and where abstractions break under extreme workloads. We cover partitioning strategies, predicate pushdown optimizations, compaction tradeoffs, graviton efficiencies, intelligent-tiering storage and how to eliminate common anti-patterns that inflate your bill. Learn from practical examples of real-world workloads on Amazon S3 Tables, Amazon Athena, Amazon Redshift, Amazon S3, Amazon EMR and leave with a comprehensive playbook to lower you analytics costs.

description: Getting AI agents into production across a regulated enterprise means solving governance and security first. In this session, learn how Danske Bank built "AI City"—a governed, reusable platform that cut time-to-production from months to days. See how they structured the platform so new teams can ship agents without rebuilding authorization, logging, or model access controls from scratch, with production examples from personal banking, compliance, and capital markets, and explore the Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore architecture underneath it all.

title: Dark Factory or Human in Every Loop: Building the Agentic SDLC in Between (sponsored by Port IO) (IND103-S)
description: Your developers ship faster than ever. Your organization doesn't. The bottleneck moved from writing the code to everything that happens after it. Agents can help, but only with a trustworthy picture of your org and real permission to act in it. That's an agentic SDLC. Nobody ships you one, because yours is shaped like your organization. So we'll build one live for a company that doesn't exist: a t-shirt printer whose three factories disagree on what a medium is. Then we take the humans out and see how dark the factory gets. An agent built it in two hours. This presentation is brought to you by Port IO, an AWS Partner.

title: Data & AI Security, Resilience and Recovery in AWS (sponsored by Veeam) (AIM293-S)
description: As AI adoption accelerates on AWS, cloud and platform teams need to know exactly what Veeam can do to keep their data secure and their environments resilient. This session takes you on a tour of Veeam's capabilities built for the AWS developer and cloud practitioner: discovering sensitive data, monitoring AI agent activity, and closing visibility gaps before they become incidents. You'll see how security posture and backup protection work together in practice, giving teams confidence in what's protected. And when something does go wrong, precise, granular recovery means restoring exactly what changed, nothing more. This presentation is brought to you by Veeam, an AWS Partner.

title: Datacenter to Cloud: Safety, Security, & Trust for AI Agents & Models (sponsored by Red Hat) (SEC102-S)
description: Deploying enterprise AI requires a unified framework across four governance pillars: Safety, Security, Risk, and Trust. Demystify multi-layer vulnerabilities spanning base models, agentic harnesses, and tool usage, addressing threats like Mythos model risks. Learn defense-in-depth strategies for agents—including sandboxing, privilege control, reasoning tracing, and dynamic red-teaming—to mitigate prompt injection, data leakage, and excessive agency. We’ll map these practices to global frameworks like NIST AI RMF and the EU AI Act to ensure continuous production readiness. This presentation is brought to you by Red Hat, an AWS Partner.

Learn to build a business glossary and metadata forms, create an analysis-ready dataset with an ETL job, and trace end-to-end data lineage. Gain hands-on experience enforcing data quality rules, enriching and publishing a governed data product, and sharing it through a publish-and-subscribe model with approval workflows and least-privilege access. Discover how to deliver trustworthy, explainable answers with the Gen-AI data agent. Leave equipped to build the governance and metadata foundation that makes data — and the AI that runs on it — trustworthy across your organization. You must bring your laptop to participate.

description: Federated data ownership is easy to draw and hard to enforce. Is governance enforced in process, or in the platform? Enforce it in the platform, and the hard part becomes the seam between central policy and self-serve provisioning most teams never build. On Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio we architect that seam: one project per data-domain for blast-radius isolation, contracts that block non-compliant publication, policy that cascades but only tightens, and a reconciler turning Git-committed JSON into infrastructure. Experian runs it across dozens of data domains in regulated financial services, cutting domain onboarding from months to self-serve.

title: Deep dive on S3 Files with use case architectures and best practices
description: What if every application, AI agent, and team in your organization could access S3 data as a shared file system? With S3 Files, connect thousands of compute resources to your data in S3 through a high-performance file interface that scales to multiple terabytes per second. Stop duplicating data between object and file storage. Stop building staging workflows just to read a file. In this session, you'll see how S3 Files turns S3 into the shared file system your workloads already expect, and how customers are replacing copy-heavy pipelines with direct file access today.

title: Deepfakes, Deception, and the New Rules of Reality (sponsored by KnowBe4) (AIM270-S)
description: Deepfakes are transforming the rules of trust. As AI-generated voice, video, and imagery become easier to create, attackers use synthetic media to make deception feel familiar, urgent, and credible. In this session, KnowBe4 shows how deepfakes fit into broader social engineering campaigns built around narrative, timing, and cross-channel reinforcement. The fake clip is rarely the whole attack; it is one piece of a larger story designed to short-circuit judgment when it matters most. Attendees will learn what separates an interesting tech demo from a nation-state-level attack. They will see how these attacks work and why convincing stories and cognitive biases override technical skepticism even in well-trained people. Perry Carpenter will also cover how organizations can prepare for high-stakes moments when trust is under pressure—before the call comes in, not after This presentation is brought to you by KnowBe4, an AWS Partner.

title: Defeat Player Evasion: AI Moderation at Scale on Amazon Bedrock.
description: Players evade moderation with leetspeak, homoglyphs, emoji sequences, and fast-evolving slang. Brute-force AI classification catches evasion but is cost-prohibitive at scale. In this workshop, build a tiered moderation pipeline on Amazon Bedrock that routes 80–90% of traffic through deterministic normalization and pre-filters before invoking a model. Ambiguous content gets classified by Amazon Nova at sub-500ms latency. Only the hardest cases escalate to multi-agent analysis on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for context-dependent decisions. Configure per-category thresholds, instrument cost-per-decision tracking, and stress-test against real gaming evasion patterns. Walk away with a deployable, cost-optimized pipeline. Laptop required

title: Defending the Three Lanes: Preventing Toxic Agentic Combinations with Cyera and AWS (sponsored by Cyera) (AIM3300-S)
description: Agentic AI is entering production faster than enterprise authorization models can keep up, and most access decisions are made without regard to the sensitivity of the data agents can reach, turning over-permissioned agents into high-value targets. This session introduces the three lanes: the data agents touch, the identity they act as, and the actions they take, as the framework for defending agentic AI on AWS. See how Cyera's Agent Guardian extends Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity with data-aware authorization to enforce least privilege, monitor agent-to-data activity, and prove it to auditors. This presentation is brought to you by Cyera, an AWS Partner.
location: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Defense-in-Depth for Containers on Amazon EKS: A Layering Story
description: On a default Amazon EKS cluster, a single pod is a compromise away from the whole cluster - shared node credentials, flat networking, implicit trust, open egress. In this code-first session we start there, then trace how EKS security grew layer by layer as the threat model matured. We rebuild an over-privileged workload live, adding one control at a time: scoped pod identity, admin and DNS network policies, and private certificate trust with zero-downtime CA rotation. We finish by running a lateral-movement attempt against the hardened workload and watching it fail at multiple layers — the whole point of defense-in-depth.

title: Defense in depth for Strands AI agents with Cedar, AgentCore, and Rex
description: AI agents that generate and execute code on remote systems need more than a single permission check - they need policy enforcement at every trust boundary. In this builders' session, you’ll configure Cedar policies at two distinct enforcement points for a Strands pre-built operations agent : AgentCore Policy on AgentCore Gateway and Trusted Remote Execution (REX) on the target remote host. You’ll see why both are necessary, how they compose, and how the agent gracefully adapts when it hits either boundary.

description: Autonomous agents demand multi-step reasoning, tool calling, and long-running sessions. title: Deploy a HIPAA-Compliant AI Agent with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
description: Your clinical team wants an AI agent that summarizes patient notes—but one leaked SSN means a $1.5M HIPAA penalty. Guardrails automatically redact low-risk identifiers and block critical PHI, routing flagged content through Amazon EventBridge to an SQS review queue. AWS CloudTrail captures the full audit trail, and IAM restricts the agent to BAA-covered services only. You leave with a deployable CDK stack ready for production.

title: Deploy AI agents on containers with Amazon S3 Files and S3 Vectors

A background process generates embeddings stored in S3 Vectors, giving agents long-term memory they query semantically. Deploy a self-managed orchestrator that spawns agents, routes tasks via file system events, and retrieves vector history. Fine-tune synchronization, monitor with CloudWatch, and establish DR with cross-Region replication. Walk away with a production-ready, self-managed multi-agent system.

This talk walks through how we traced that utilization gap, found where throughput was being lost, and identified the signals that could have exposed the problem earlier. Through this production experience, we’ll look at what it means to design for operability before scale, when performance, utilization, and cost problems are still easier to fix.

title: Designing performant and cost-effective data lakes on Amazon S3 Tables
description: Apache Iceberg data lakes that aren't thoughtfully planned can accumulate small files, excessive metadata, and redundant snapshots, ultimately degrading query performance and inflating costs. For each, we'll walk through the trade-offs, what happens when you get it wrong vs. right, and how Amazon S3 Tables can automate the heavy lifting for you. Leave with actionable strategies to balance performance and cost at scale.

title: Designing Portable Multicloud Architectures with Open Specifications
description: Enterprises pursuing multicloud strategies often equate portability with containerization — but true architectural portability requires deliberate decisions across the full stack. At each layer, we explore how open specifications enable portability — and in what parts of your architecture does portability matter most. Along the way, we challenge common myths: that managed services equal lock-in, that Kubernetes equals portable, and that open source alone guarantees freedom. Through interactive whiteboarding, we'll design portable architecture patterns together — examining real trade-offs, open specifications like Apache Iceberg, OpenTelemetry, OPA, and MCP, and how to make deliberate portability decisions across your stack.

title: Deterministic control for probabilistic agents: proving safety holds
description: AI agents are probabilistic: vulnerable to prompt injection, hallucination, and unexpected tool composition. The controls around them must be deterministic. This session explores how to define provable safety envelopes for autonomous agents, drawing from the authorization and formal verification research behind AgentCore policy. We examine how automated reasoning guarantees policy correctness, how neuro-symbolic approaches combine LLM flexibility with mathematical verification for policy authoring, and how agents' action spaces can be reduced before execution. Attendees will also get a first look at new research extending these guarantees to emerging agentic authorization challenges.

title: Deterministic meets probabilistic: Patterns for reliable AI integration
description: Production systems demand determinism. AI outputs are probabilistic. The boundary between these two worlds is where this must be resolved. This chalk talk will whiteboard the contracts and integration patterns that hold that boundary: typed interfaces treating model output as untrusted input, propose/commit separation so AI never performs its own side effects, asymmetric verification, bounded generate-verify-repair loops, and compensating actions in place of rollback. We'll work through typical anti-patterns that quietly reach production, where to place the contract in your architecture to avoid these, and the reliability arithmetic that these patterns enable.

description: New regulations and geopolitical shifts are pushing organizations to rethink how they protect data and control access in the cloud, while still adopting AI. This session covers how AWS helps customers meet digital sovereignty requirements without giving up capability, through offerings that include the AWS European Sovereign Cloud and controls you can verify and enforce. title: Disaggregated inference at scale: when to split prefill from decode
description: Disaggregated inference separates prefill and decode onto independent GPU pools, eliminating the interference that lets one long prompt stall every active generation — and letting each phase scale on its own terms. It isn't free: KV cache must cross the network, and a well-cached unified deployment can still win. The difference is your traffic. In this hands-on builders session, you run both architectures on NVIDIA GPU-based Amazon EC2 instances, move KV cache between pools over Elastic Fabric Adapter, and benchmark them against realistic agentic traffic. Learn the decision framework — input length, prefix reuse, latency SLO — and leave with runnable configurations.

We'll walk through the request lifecycle, debate trade-offs around latency, budgets, and MCP tool calls, and show how the same broker pattern governs any agent touching sensitive data.

title: Drug discovery and materials use cases with Amazon Braket and Q-CTRL
description: Classically hard problems such as simulating strongly correlated electrons and 1D NMR spectra, critical to material and drug discovery, can be sped up on quantum computers but until now had not been demonstrated. Q-CTRL shows how Fire Opal on Amazon Braket enables simulating 1D NMR spectra for spin systems up to 34 qubits and achieved a 3,000x speedup on the Fermi-Hubbard model at 120 qubits, demonstrating practical quantum advantage. This chalk talk unpacks how AWS hybrid workflows enabled these outcomes and what enterprises should do now to capture ROI with quantum.

title: DynamoDB: the database designed for trillion-scale vector search
description: As vector search becomes a standard component of AI applications, scaling to billions or even trillions of vectors while maintaining single-digit millisecond latency and high recall remains a significant challenge. In this session, deep dive into the decisions made when building vector indexes for DynamoDB, including how vector indexes shard alongside table data, the scatter-gather query mechanism that keeps latencies tight, and the filtering that avoids recall degradation at scale. Learn how the partition key in DynamoDB maps naturally to multi-tenant workloads, enabling per-tenant index isolation without operational overhead. Discover the trade-offs between recall, latency, and cost in production for real-time vector search.

title: EC2 at 20: Rebuilding the control plane while it is running
description: Amazon EC2 launched in 2006 as four services backed by a single MySQL database. Twenty years later, it is one of the largest distributed systems ever built — and most of that original architecture had to be replaced while serving production traffic, with no maintenance window and no change to the API contract customers depend on. In this session, EC2 engineers dive deep on two of the hardest migrations: making the control plane Availability Zone independent so a single-AZ event cannot escalate into a regional one, and moving EC2 metadata off MySQL. We walk through the failure modes that forced each decision, how correctness was verified before every cutover, how we proved a single-AZ failure stays in a single AZ, and the things we got wrong along the way. You will leave with migration and isolation patterns you can apply to your own systems at any scale.

title: EFA deep dive: Architecture, evolution, and scaling with OpenAI
description: We built EFA to deliver multi-tenant, elastic, high-performance networking with portability across every instance type and accelerator through Libfabric. The architecture that followed, such as multipath packet spraying, out-of-order delivery, and encryption of every byte in transit, has scaled from HPC workloads to the backbone of today's largest AI training clusters. Now it's evolving again to support disaggregated inference and expert parallelism. OpenAI joins to share how they adapted their production inference stack to EFA on EC2 UltraServers, covering Reliable Datagram semantics for GPU-to-GPU collectives, NCCL tuning, and topology-aware communication patterns that unlock new performance.

This session explores EFA's origins in high-performance computing (HPC) and its evolution into the backbone of today's largest AI training and inference architectures. Discover how early architecture decisions now unlock novel use cases across pretraining, reinforcement learning, and disaggregated inference with hundreds of thousands of accelerators. We dive into recent innovations including library integrations, protocol optimizations, and performance gains.

title: Encoding Authorization in Logic from Puzzles to Production

Through practical examples, we'll explore new capabilities that help publishers reach customers at scale and help organizations govern and consume containers with confidence. Whether you publish container software or run it in production, you'll leave with a clear picture of how ECR is becoming the center of the container software supply chain.

title: Enterprise AI is missing a key ingredient: The knowledge layer (sponsored by Neo4j) (AIM286-S)
description: You don't need another post-mortem to know why enterprise AI projects fail. Organizations that have moved AI from pilot to production know it runs on context. A knowledge layer shows AI how facts relate, what's changed, and what's already been decided. Trained on siloed data, a model sees disconnected records, not relationships, and can't reason well without that context. The knowledge layer connects GenAI and agentic systems to data that's organized and accessible. In this session, we'll cover why the knowledge layer is the missing piece your enterprise AI needs, and what your organization gains from implementing one: Trust every AI answer, back to your source data. Prove every AI decision with a complete audit trail. Synthesize intelligence across disparate systems and teams. Use your existing data investments instead of replacing them. description: Seventy-four percent of industrial IoT projects stall somewhere between pilot and production. The hard part is that the pilot worked. That is exactly what makes the failure so difficult to diagnose. Pilots succeed because a few hundred sensors over a few weeks fits comfortably in almost any database. Production does not. Storage costs compound faster than the budget that approved them, ingest hits a cliff with no warning, and the real-time dashboard that sold the project turns into a loading screen. See where industrial systems and typical AWS pipelines reach their limits and how to scale beyond them. We’ll explore a proven architecture using AWS IoT Core, Amazon Kinesis, AWS Lambda, and a single Postgres database to support more than one million connected devices reporting every second. title: Evaluate, Disclose, Safeguard: A Production-Readiness Framework for AI Agents
description: Every organization is building AI agents, but few have made it to production. You can't prove it works, you can't prove it's responsible, and compliance won't sign off. In this chalk talk, we walk through a production-readiness framework for AI agents on Amazon Connect. First, evaluation: measuring resolution with the Connect Simulation API to score AI agents on the same bar as human agents. Second, responsible AI: disclosure patterns that build trust, escalation triggers for sensitive journeys, and harm avoidance for regulated industries. Third, safeguards: defense-in-depth governance for agents that process refunds and access sensitive data, including asymmetric PII, MCP tool authorization for human confirmation, and automated escalation when confidence drops. Leave with a checklist: what to measure, what to disclose, what to block, and when to ship.

title: Event-driven agents at scale: building agentic AI on Amazon MSK
description: Production agents need to dispatch long-running actions, wait on external systems, fan results out to analytics, and re-enter the conversation when work finishes — not sit in a synchronous loop. In this session, we present reusable patterns for building multi-tenant, event-driven agentic systems on Amazon MSK: dispatch-and-resume for long-running tool calls, topic and partition design keyed to tenant and conversation, decoupling the agent loop from channels and analytics, and durability and replay so in-flight work survives deploys and retries. We walk through how alerts from Amazon GuardDuty and AWS Security Hub flow through Amazon EventBridge, triggering AWS Lambda functions that invoke agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, with human-in-the-loop controls for high-severity events. Discover best practices for reducing alert fatigue, accelerating MTTR, and scaling security operations for financial services and other regulated industries where every response must be explainable and audit ready.

title: Event storming: Find your service boundaries before production does
description: Split a system in the wrong place and you get a distributed monolith: coupled services with network hops instead of function calls. This session tackles the problem most teams get wrong, where to draw the boundary, using Event Storming. Together we map a real domain, trace information flow between actors, and identify natural division points, deciding ownership, data locality, transaction scope, and deployment independence at each boundary. Every decision is evidence based, grounded in observed event flow rather than intuition. Then you go hands on, taking one boundary and deploying it as an independent service on AWS. Leave with a repeatable method for boundary definition plus working code you built yourself. Bring your laptop.

description: LLM inference on Kubernetes is bottlenecked by loading multi-gigabyte model weights through the storage → network → CPU → PCIe → GPU path. We walk through when each technique shines, how they compose together, and the tradeoffs platform teams face when optimizing inference cold starts on Amazon EKS. Learn how kro and ACK enable declarative provisioning of optimized storage pipelines, allowing platform teams to compose reusable stacks.

title: Expedite model loading times on Kubernetes using kro and ACK - from storage to GPU
description: LLM inference on Kubernetes is bottlenecked by loading multi-gigabyte model weights through the storage → network → CPU → PCIe → GPU path. In this chalk talk we benchmark four approaches to accelerating model delivery to GPU memory: SOCI for lazy-loading container image layers, s5cmd parallel downloads, Mountpoint for Amazon S3 CSI streaming, and Run.ai Model Streamer for direct S3-to-GPU pipelining. We walk through when each technique shines, how they compose together, and the tradeoffs platform teams face when optimizing inference cold starts on Amazon EKS. Learn how kro and ACK enable declarative provisioning of optimized storage pipelines, allowing platform teams to compose reusable stacks.

title: Experience catalog federation on AWS: build a multi-cloud open data lakehouse
description: Enterprise data teams have distributed data catalogs across multiple cloud providers, each with partial visibility and no shared query surface. This hands-on workshop demonstrates how catalog federation unifies cross-cloud data silos into an open data lakehouse architecture on AWS. Using Amazon S3 Tables as the storage foundation with Apache Iceberg as the open, engine-neutral table format for seamless interoperability and zero data duplication across AWS, Snowflake, and Databricks, you'll federate remote catalogs to build a unified lakehouse on AWS to run AI-assisted business analytics.

title: Exploit a software vulnerability, then stop it: From code to containment
description: Step into the role of a DevSecOps engineer tasked with hardening your organization's web applications after a security audit. In this hands-on workshop, a simulated lab walks you through real threat scenarios, and you respond using layered AWS security services. Start with Amazon Inspector Code Security to catch vulnerabilities pre-deployment, then use Kiro's agentic capabilities to auto-remediate issues without leaving your IDE. Scan EC2 instances and SBOMs for supply-chain risk, apply virtual patches via AWS WAF, and fully remediate with AWS Systems Manager. Finally, contain an active GuardDuty-detected incident by blocking C2 communication with Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall and AWS Network Firewall, proving that layered defenses hold even against unpatched vulnerabilities.

title: Explore agentic data engineering in Amazon SageMaker
description: Data engineering teams lose time to siloed data, manual ETL, and tribal knowledge. This session shows how agents change that in Amazon SageMaker. Use SageMaker Data Agent to trace errors, refactor code, and deploy pipelines in natural language, then bring your own agents through MCP servers to work with third-party clients and models directly on your data. See how the same agentic approach extends across SageMaker, so teams can consolidate fragmented pipelines, standardize environments, and put agents to work on more of the data engineering lifecycle.

title: Extend Amazon EKS clusters for on-premises and edge use cases
description: This chalk talk covers strategies for modernizing distributed applications with Amazon EKS across AWS Regions, AWS Local Zones, and AWS Outposts. It demonstrates how EKS delivers a consistent experience across these deployment options, minimizing latency and enabling data residency. Through a real-world scenario, the session deploys an application to an EKS cluster across distributed environments while maintaining a unified control plane. It covers practical use cases, best practices, and patterns for architecting resilient and scalable applications, following AWS Well-Architected Framework principles for consistency and security.

title: Extend AWS WAF to the APIs your AI agents call (sponsored by Wallarm) (SEC218-S)
description: Network and edge controls stop the traffic patterns they were built to recognize. AI agents introduce a different pattern: authenticated requests, at machine speed, against business logic rather than known vulnerabilities. Teams running AWS WAF often find these requests pass inspection because nothing about them is malformed. In this session, examine how agent-driven traffic reaches APIs, which risks fall outside signature and rate-based inspection, and what an additive API security layer contributes. Learn how teams instrument existing AWS WAF deployments for API-level visibility, apply real-time redaction to sensitive data in responses, and enforce without adding latency. This presentation is brought to you by Wallarm, an AWS Partner.

title: Extending your cloud network with Amazon Leo satellite connectivity
description: Your cloud network doesn't have to end where fiber does. In this interactive whiteboard session, you'll design hybrid network architectures that combine Amazon Leo's low-earth orbit satellite connectivity with AWS networking services including VPN, Transit Gateway, and Cloud WAN. We'll start with Leo's real-world performance characteristics: latency, throughput, and availability. Then, we'll work through three architecture patterns: first-day connectivity for new sites, primary connectivity for remote locations, and satellite-based redundancy for existing terrestrial links. You'll leave with reference architectures you can adapt to your environment and a clear understanding of how the constellation fits in your network design.

title: Fanatics path to AWS: 5 data centers, 1,800 servers, 48% savings
description: If your migration is stuck because no one can agree on what moves first while licensing costs compound and dependencies stay undocumented, the problem isn’t willingness. It’s sequencing. Fanatics Commerce had 1800 servers across five data centers and projected 48% infrastructure savings on AWS. Their team shares the structured path: OLA for licensing clarity, DAP for dependency mapping, EBA for organizational alignment, MAP for execution. Walk away with: (1) a concrete OLA-to-MAP sequence, (2) an AI-assisted dependency mapping approach that surfaced connections no one had documented (3) a phased AWS Transform modernization strategy that earns engineering trust before scaling.

description: When an IAM request is denied, teams can spend valuable time finding the root cause. In this session, we'll walk through how the feature works, how to put it to use, and considerations for larger AWS environments where different policy types are owned by different teams.

title: Faster tech debt remediation without the setup overhead
description: In this Code Talk, learn how continuous modernization enables faster tech debt analysis and remediation by starting directly from your cloud accounts. Instead of manually connecting code repositories upfront, you can begin identifying tech debt immediately using lifecycle-event signals from your cloud environment. The platform then provides an easy path to resolution with automatic generation of pull requests. We will walk through the account-first workflow and how it gets you from discovery to remediation faster with less setup.
location: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Fault-tolerant AI agents: Choosing the right recovery pattern
description: When an AI agent crashes at step 20 of 30, you can't just start over. Once state accumulates, a blind retry becomes dangerous. Most teams default to the wrong recovery strategy because they apply stateless retry thinking to stateful workflows. In this session, we compare three approaches: replay-based recovery with idempotent tool execution, checkpoint-and-resume with human-in-the-loop pause/resume, and event-driven compensation across trust boundaries. We'll whiteboard each pattern, map it to real failure scenarios, and build a decision framework based on your agent's state model and fault domain.

title: Find and fix storage bottlenecks for self-managed OLTP on EC2 with EBS
description: ​​When you run a self-managed OLTP database on Amazon EC2, the storage bottleneck is rarely where you assume. This hands-on session teaches a repeatable method for finding and fixing it. Use Flexible IO tester and a PostgreSQL/pgbench workload to connect storage metrics to database symptoms. Measure latency, IOPS, throughput, and queue depth; determine whether the limit is the volume, instance bandwidth, or I/O pattern; then tune the right EBS volume configuration. Validate every change with EBS detailed performance statistics and CloudWatch. Leave with a proven sizing-and-tuning method for database workloads on EC2.

First, serverless training of large language models on AWS. Second, enterprise-grade inference serving. Third, observability and evaluation tools optimizing toward smaller, performant models. You take a real AWS Security Hub finding category and work through four control layers. An SCP stops the misconfiguration, an AWS CloudFormation Guard rule catches it before deployment, an AWS Config rule detects existing violations, and AI-generated auto-remediation corrects drift. Each finding you remediate this way becomes a rule that keeps it from coming back.

The bottleneck isn't the model; it's the data. In this session, see how Amazon Connect Decisions uses agentic AI teammates to eliminate that gap. Watch a supply chain planner go from zero to a running demand forecast — connecting raw CSVs with no pre-cleaning, letting AI intelligently map and type-convert data, catching and fixing quality issues conversationally, and encoding tribal knowledge from a Word doc into live decision rules. No ETL code, no JIRA tickets, no months-long implementation. Onboarding in weeks, not months.

We unpack where good architecture and operable architecture diverge, which trade-offs are worth making early, and what questions your team should be asking before committing to a design. The best architecture is one you can actually run in production.

The shift is not that attackers are unstoppable — it is that they operate on a faster clock than the systems meant to contain them. Their advantage is freshness: exploiting what changed before defenders reconcile it, exploiting uncertainty before it becomes understanding, and exploiting stale proof before records drift from reality. AI compresses discovery and action, scaling tasks that once required teams. In this session, learn how defense can be rebuilt around real‑time truth, continuous visibility, and inspectable, defensible action. This presentation is brought to you by Booz Allen, an AWS Partner.

title: From 1 to 20,000: Scale reliably on AWS Trainium with AWS EKS
description: As AI workloads scale, infrastructure failures become inevitable, causing stalled jobs, degraded throughput, and wasted accelerator capacity. In this chalk talk, we’ll show how to build resilient AI workloads on AWS Trainium with AWS EKS. We’ll whiteboard the full resiliency stack: Neuron DRA Driver for topology-aware scheduling; UltraServer Operator for provisioning UltraServer workloads; Neuron Observer for sub-second fault detection; and Device Taint for automated recovery. We’ll walk through how these patterns support fault-tolerant distributed training and large-scale inference workloads from a single accelerator to 20,000. You’ll leave with reusable operational patterns for running AI workloads reliably at any scale.

description: The workflows that matter most in financial services span multiple systems, require multiple types of expertise, and today rely on people as the coordination layer. One person pulls data, another reviews it for compliance, a third routes it for approval. That coordination tax is where your team's time disappears. Amazon Quick changes that equation. title: From carbon data to action: Optimize AI workloads on AWS
description: Not all workloads are equal in carbon impact, but how do you know which choices matter most? In this chalk talk, we pull back the curtain on how AWS measures and allocates cloud emissions, balancing scientific rigor with practical usability. Through real-world examples, you'll see how this data reveals meaningful differences across diverse AI workloads. You'll leave with an understanding of the methodology behind your carbon data and how to apply those insights to build AI workloads with a lower environmental footprint, and, often, lower cost.

title: From chatbot to proactive agent: Connect AI to your nonprofit systems
description: Agents stall at the demo stage because core enterprise systems — ERPs, legacy databases, and internal APIs — were never built for AI. In this session, we whiteboard two patterns to bridge the gap: request-driven integration via Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway with access-control interceptors, and event-driven routing via Amazon EventBridge with confidence-based human-in-the-loop fallback. We trace both approaches using a legacy system with no modern API surface — wrapping its interfaces as MCP tools without modifying the original code. The patterns apply whether your blocker is a SOAP endpoint, a stored-procedure layer, or a REST API with no auth story for agents. Leave with a maturity rubric and two practical reference architectures.

Learn how AWS enables progressive modernization from zero-copy federation via BDC Connect, to Iceberg-based lakehouse architectures, to AI-powered analytics with Amazon Bedrock, SageMaker, and QuickSight. title: From self-managed to AWS managed: agentic AI for Kafka and MQ migrations
description: Migrating self-managed Apache Kafka and RabbitMQ to Amazon MSK and Amazon MQ is hard. Topic mapping, offset translation, ACL migration, and the notoriously long cutover phase slow teams down for weeks. In this chalk talk, we walk through these challenges and show how agentic AI paired with AWS replication tooling compresses the longest migration phase from days to minutes. Watch a complete live migration executed end-to-end in under 60 minutes and leave with a repeatable playbook for your own migration.

title: From shopping agents to shoppers: Amazon CloudFront patterns for peak retail
description: Peak retail traffic is no longer just more shoppers. AI shopping agents, scrapers, and personalized experiences now collide on the same edge. In this session, learn advanced Amazon CloudFront patterns to handle all three. See how to classify and verify agentic traffic using CloudFront Functions, Amazon CloudFront KeyValueStore, and AWS WAF Bot Control, then serve tiered responses without touching origin. Hear how you can serve AI-powered personalization on every page in about a millisecond by encoding decision-tree models in KeyValueStore, fed by an Amazon Bedrock pipeline. Discover battle-tested patterns for your next cyber week.

description: AI is reshaping cybersecurity, but security teams must act faster without adding complexity. Sempra Energy, AWS, and Accenture deployed Accenture Cyber.AI on AWS to create a unified view of cyber risk and identify the highest-priority actions across the enterprise. Learn how the team integrated existing security investments, addressed governance and architecture requirements, and operationalized AI-driven risk management. Speakers will share key design decisions, implementation lessons, and practical guidance for using AI to improve cyber resilience, strengthen security operations, and maintain control of data and infrastructure in cloud environments. This presentation is brought to you by Accenture, an AWS Partner.

title: From static to dynamic - modernizing bidirectional federation
description: Static credentials remain the most common source of identity-related security incidents, yet many workloads still rely on them across trust boundaries. AWS now eliminates them in both directions. Humans and workloads outside AWS can use OIDC, SAML, or X.509 certificates to federate in and obtain temporary AWS credentials. Conversely, IAM outbound identity federation lets AWS workloads exchange IAM identities for short-lived JWTs when calling external clouds like Azure and Google Cloud, AI providers like OpenAI or Anthropic, SaaS platforms like Databricks and Snowflake, and your own applications. This session covers how to configure trust, scope credentials, and enforce authorization controls.
location: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Red Theater

Learn how the agent improves continuously from production results, expert corrections, and revised context your team contributes. We'll demonstrate the full observe-evaluate-improve cycle with an underwriting agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and the Strands Agents Framework, then discuss how the pattern applies to claims, fraud, and customer service agents.

Using Amazon Inspector and AWS Continuum (formerly AWS Security Agent), you discover and validate existing flaws, reproduce the exploit chain, and push Continuum-generated fixes through CI/CD. When Amazon GuardDuty detects the active exploitation, including credential theft and prompt injection against an AI assistant, you isolate the compromised instance and harden it. Walk away with a repeatable closed-loop workflow: Inspector finds it, GuardDuty catches it, Continuum fixes it.

title: Future-proof your keys: HSMs to AWS KMS in the post-quantum era
description: Cryptography is changing fast. The dedicated HSM you rely on today, whether AWS CloudHSM or an on-premises appliance, carries operational overhead that will only grow as the industry moves toward post-quantum cryptography (PQC) and stricter digital sovereignty requirements. AWS Key Management Service (KMS) now covers most workloads that once required dedicated HSMs, with the same FIPS 140-3 Level 3 security, lower cost, and zero infrastructure management, while giving you a clear on-ramp to PQC and the sovereignty controls to keep your keys and data under your control. In this chalk talk, bring your architecture and we'll work through it together: we'll assess your workload, map signature and encryption migration paths, and show how moving to KMS puts you on the fastest path to post-quantum readiness. Meet the AWS Cryptography team and leave with a plan and concrete next steps.

title: Gemini gets closer to traders with AWS Outposts and AWS Local Zones
description: Gemini, a NASDAQ-listed crypto exchange, serves trading clients with diverse latency needs. For the most latency-sensitive workloads, AWS Outposts at Gemini's NY5 facility runs matching-engine-adjacent with sub-millisecond connectivity via cross-connects. For cloud-native traders, AWS Local Zones in NYC deliver sub-2ms latency through VPC Peering: bringing compute into the New York area cut round-trip latency roughly 80%, with provisioning in minutes rather than months. For customers prioritizing simplicity, the Region offers a fully managed API, including agentic trading systems connecting via MCP. Hear how Gemini's tiered model turns compute placement into a competitive lever you can apply to your own location-sensitive workloads.

In this hands-on workshop, take the on-call seat: inject real faults into a live microservices store on Amazon EKS, partner with the agent to root-cause them in minutes, and judge its mitigation plans. title: Hands-on with the AWS Network Firewall proxy for secure egress
description: AWS Network Firewall now gives you the flexibility to act as an explicit forward proxy for outbound traffic on the firewall you already run. Clients connect to it directly by its proxy FQDN, so no route-table changes are required. The proxy attaches to a NAT gateway and terminates each client connection, letting one firewall consolidate egress for multiple VPCs regardless of overlapping CIDRs. In this builders session you'll get hands-on deploying the proxy and building layered egress controls, up to and including outbound TLS inspection. You'll leave knowing when and how to use the firewall proxy to centralize and enforce egress controls for private workloads.

title: Hidden trade-offs in distributed architectures
description: Asynchronous event-driven architectures enable loosely coupled, scalable, and resilient systems. But the devil is in the details, and hidden complexity emerges when components interact under real-world pressure. Consistency, latency, failure handling, and cost aren't determined by architecture diagrams but by the trade-offs behind the integration patterns and services you choose. Through a real-world case study using AWS Lambda, Amazon DynamoDB, DynamoDB Streams, and AWS Step Functions, you'll investigate unexpected system behavior and uncover the trade-offs behind it. You'll leave with a sharper intuition to see beyond cloud abstractions and make more intentional architectural decisions for resilient systems.

Kiwibank, New Zealand's only 100% NZ-owned bank, must compete against four far larger Australian-owned banks — with a fraction of the resources. Working with Accenture and AWS, Kiwibank is building a governed enterprise AI layer that every future application can draw from. The result: a compounding AI advantage that grows with each new use case, letting the bank launch products faster, serve customers more intelligently, and scale without proportional cost growth. A five-person team built this across 2 billion records and 400 million identities with sub-second response. That data commands premium value, and identity became infrastructure, not a cleanup project. This presentation is brought to you by Senzing, an AWS Partner.

title: How to think about NUMA: Optimizing AI inference on EC2
description: Non-Uniform Memory Access (NUMA) topology shapes how every byte of model weight reaches a compute core, and misalignment silently costs throughput. This session explains why NUMA matters for memory locality when running models on EC2, and what changes across Graviton-, Intel-, and AMD-based instances. CPU inference requires deliberate alignment of threads to data, especially as SIMD and AMX instructions amplify memory bandwidth demands per core. Even on GPU instances, host-side NUMA affects preprocessing and KV cache offload. Understand your hardware topology and leverage it to get the most from your inference workloads.

title: Inside AWS Trainium3: Hardware innovations for better AI economics
description: What does it take to build a chip purpose-made for AI? In this deep dive, we explore Trainium3 architecture innovations: NeuronCore innovations that delivers higher TFLOPs, hardware-accelerated quantization, softmax acceleration, near-memory compute and Mixture-of-Experts optimizations. We'll share micro-benchmark data showing how these choices translate to real performance for Mixture-of-Experts and other demanding workloads. At the system level, we examine the Trn3 UltraServer family, scaling from 32 to 144 chips via NeuronLink fabric to enables up to 4.4x more performance. Leave with a deep understanding of how to evaluate and leverage purpose-built AI Chips for your AI workloads.
location: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Inside Bayer’s AI agent: Interpretability as governance (sponsored by Thoughtworks) (IND3309-S)
description: Enterprise AI governance has focused on controls around agents—identity, permissions, sandboxing, and audit trails. But what happens inside the model? This session explores a live production system: Bayer’s PRINCE research assistant, built with Thoughtworks on AWS to give researchers access to 18,000+ preclinical study reports. We’ll share how Thoughtworks’ AI Research Labs applies mechanistic interpretability research, published at ICML, NeurIPS, and AAAI, to understand why the assistant answers, cites, or refuses queries. See how sparse autoencoders identify internal circuits behind refusal, how targeted steering changes behavior without retraining, and why this matters in regulated environments. Leave with a practical framework for making interpretability a core component of AI governance. This presentation is brought to you by Thoughtworks, an AWS Partner.
location: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Industry Theater

title: Inside NKI: How AWS designed a kernel language for peak AI performance
description: What does a kernel language need to unlock peak performance on Trainium, AWS purpose built AI chips to deliver better price performance? The AWS Neuron Kernel Interface (NKI) is a Python-embedded DSL that goes beyond framework-level abstractions, giving developers direct access to Trainium's three-level memory hierarchy and four compute engines. Explore the design choices that enable hardware-level optimization, dissect production kernels powering FlashAttention variants, MoE routing, and on-device collectives, and debate where tile-based languages converge or diverge across accelerator architectures. Discover how NKI extends to support MXFP8 and disaggregated inference, and leave equipped to write custom, hardware-optimized kernels.

title: Inside Real AI Software Factories: Lessons From the Teams Building Them (sponsored by LaunchDarkly) (DVT222-S)
description: Everyone's talking about AI software factories. Far fewer have actually built one. In this panel, engineering leaders, partners, and teams putting agents into production go past the hype to the real work: where agents accelerate delivery, where they break, and what it takes to keep humans in control as autonomy scales. Expect specifics, not theory—what worked, what didn't, and what they'd do differently. Whether you're experimenting with coding agents or scaling toward autonomous delivery, you'll leave with practical patterns for building a factory that's genuinely fast and safe. Join us for an honest conversation about engineering at agent speed. This presentation is brought to you by LaunchDarkly, an AWS Partner.
location: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Inside the Agentic Engineering Org of the Future (sponsored by Harness) (AIM257-S)
description: What does it actually take to become an AI-native engineering organization? A senior technology executive from a Fortune 500 enterprise sits down with Harness Field CTO Nick Durkin to talk through what it's really taken to go all in on agentic software delivery, orchestrating agents across the entire SDLC instead of one-off automations. They'll get into what that transformation actually looks like end to end, how they decide when an agent runs on its own versus when a human stays in the loop, how agentic engineering has affected cloud migration and consumption, and what it takes to do this at the scale of a Fortune 500 engineering org. This presentation is brought to you by Harness, an AWS Partner.

title: Inside the Architecture: Building Secure AI Applications on AWS (sponsored by TrendAI™) (SEC225-S)
description: AI is rapidly moving from experimentation to production, creating new challenges for developers, architects, and security teams. In this technical session, explore the real-world architectures enterprises use to build and secure AI applications on AWS. Learn how organizations leverage Amazon Bedrock, EKS, ECS, Security Lake, CloudTrail, and cloud-native automation to protect AI workloads, monitor risk across multi-account environments, and streamline security operations. Through practical deployment patterns and lessons learned from large-scale AWS environments, discover how to build AI applications that are secure, scalable, and production-ready. The session draws on deployment patterns described for TrendAI Vision One on AWS, including AI workload protection, cloud telemetry integration, and AWS-native architecture approaches. This presentation is brought to you by TrendAI™, an AWS Partner.

title: Inside the Governed Agentic Software Factory at Enterprise Scale (sponsored by CloudBees) (DVT217-S)
description: Code is now abundant. AI agents now write, test and deploy code autonomously; the bottleneck has shifted from generating code to governing what reaches production. Loreli Cadapan, VP of Product at CloudBees, takes you inside the governed agentic software factories that the world’s most regulated engineering organizations are building, where every change, human or agent, is visible, auditable and accountable. The work starts after the code changes: encode existing rules as enforceable policy across your toolchain, keep humans in the loop where it matters, and ship software you can stand behind. Because you write code for a reason, and we make sure that reason becomes true. This presentation is brought to you by CloudBees, an AWS Partner.
location: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Builder Theater

title: Inside T-Mobile's Kinetic Edge: Real-Time Physical AI at Scale
description: In a Physical AI world, tokens traveling across a telecom network must trigger real-world actions with sub-millisecond latency. Learn how T-Mobile built its Kinetic Edge Platform using AWS Outposts, Amazon SageMaker, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, delivering deterministic performance, ultra-low latency, and precise synchronization on a network serving 130M+ customers. We'll cover how to assess Physical AI network requirements and map them to AWS infrastructure options. You'll leave knowing how to build AI into the network edge and where it creates the most value.
location: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | White Theater

description: The UK AI Security Institute leads global research into harmful AI capabilities, assessing frontier models for risks like offensive cybersecurity, bioweapon design, and psychological manipulation. In this talk, UK AISI representatives walk through how they built their evaluation infrastructure on Amazon Bedrock, from model access and prompt orchestration to result analysis. Hear highlights from recent research projects and the engineering decisions that make safety evaluation repeatable at scale. Leave with a clearer picture of how rigorous AI safety research runs in production on AWS.
location: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: Inside Zeta Global's open lakehouse architecture on AWS
description: Are you building a data lakehouse and wondering how others have approached the same challenges? Go behind the scenes of a real AWS customer data architecture. Zeta Global's AI Marketing Platform serves thousands of clients using 245 million consumer profiles, but mutli-hour data lag times and rising per-tenant costs were limiting growth. Learn how Zeta built an open streaming lakehouse with Amazon S3 Tables, Amazon EMR, and Amazon MSK that processes 10 TB daily across 10,000+ Apache Iceberg tables, cutting time-to-insight from hours to minutes while maximizing multi-tenant infrastructure efficiency at scale.
location: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: Instant Play Demos on Twitch – Increasing Player Engagement
description: From game builds to live campaigns, take a deep dive into the best practices and constraints around launching Instant Play Demos on Twitch, powered by Amazon GameLift Streams. This innovative approach to game marketing enables developers to reach potential players and let them try your game before they buy it. No downloads or installs required, just a WebRTC enabled browser and an internet connection. Learn what kind of content makes for a great demo, engine-specific best practices, and the benefits of launching a campaign and how they perform compared to traditional marketing channels.

title: Integrating AI agents with event-driven architectures
description: Most multi-agent systems start with direct API calls between agents—then debugging becomes impossible, one slow agent blocks the chain, and replaying a failed workflow means re-running everything. In this chalk talk, discuss why event-driven patterns solve these coordination problems and how to design multi-agent systems using EventBridge for routing, human-in-the-loop controls that pause and resume agent actions via events, and compute selection—such as Lambda, Fargate, or AgentCore—based on your agent's execution profile. Bring architecture questions; we'll whiteboard patterns for decoupling agents across domains without sacrificing observability.

title: Intelligent, right-sized compute on Amazon EKS
description: Running Kubernetes at scale is a constant trade-off between performance, availability, and cost. This session covers the year's advances in Amazon EKS compute: faster node provisioning and consolidation, finer control over how and when your data plane changes, and new capabilities that match capacity to what workloads actually use rather than what they request. Whether you run Karpenter directly or fully managed EKS Auto Mode, you will see how to cut waste, raise utilization, and get more predictable efficiency for demanding CPU, GPU, and AI/ML workloads. Expect practical patterns and live demos you can apply to your own clusters.

title: Intent-Based Access Control for AI Agents that Actually Do Things (sponsored by WorkOS) (SEC210-S)
description: Agent permissions offer two bad options: approve every action manually, or skip permissions and trust the prompt. Auto-approve protects your laptop; it won't stop an agent from deleting a thousand CRM records. Roles and scopes suit static users, not agents whose next action depends on the last prompt. This session introduces Intent-Based Access Control (IBAC), where the agent's intent, not a pre-assigned role, is the unit of permission. WorkOS built Airlock on it: mission-bound tokens, every call evaluated against intent, decisions resolving to allow, deny, or escalate. Live demo across Gmail and Linear, including a blocked exfiltration and real-time human approval. This presentation is brought to you by WorkOS, an AWS Partner.
location: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Introducing AWS Context: Build governed intelligence for agents at scale
description: AI agents need to understand what your data means, how it connects, and which definitions and rules apply to each use case. AWS Context automatically builds a governed knowledge graph by unifying structured and unstructured data, managed knowledge bases, and technical and business metadata from AWS and third-party sources. This shared foundation grounds agents in your organization’s data, business rules, relationships, and domain knowledge. In this session, dive into the reference architecture and learn best practices for integrating agents with AWS Context, including considerations for identity management, workload sizing, and production deployments.
location: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | White Theater

title: Inverting the medallion: Serving reads without hitting Gold
description: Most teams default to Gold as the serving layer. For regulated systems-of-record like health data stores, ledgers, compliance archives, that's rarely the right choice. They're built for durability and interoperability, not production read traffic. The inverted pattern writes promote up the medallion, reads come from purpose-built Silver projections and Gold holds contractual semantics and never serves directly. In this chalk talk, work through change-data-capture synthesis without source support, write/read path splitting, and a routing gateway developers can't bypass. Bring your most painful regulated read path. Leave knowing when to invert, how to scope projections, and what your gateway must enforce.

title: Investigate Incidents Across Teams with AWS DevOps Agent
description: Production incidents typically involve multiple teams, but tooling and investigations are often siloed. In this chalk talk, explore how AWS DevOps Agent meets teams where incident response already happens. See how engineers can interact with the agent directly from tools like Slack, consolidating investigation activity, findings, and recommended actions alongside team communication. Bring your multi-team incident patterns and discuss approaches to faster, more connected incident response across AWS, multicloud, and on-prem environments.

title: Investigating AI threats: extending IR to the generative AI layer
description: As organizations adopt generative AI on AWS, security teams need to extend their investigation capabilities into the AI layer. In this hands-on workshop, participants work through a realistic multi-phase incident — tracing a compromised credential from initial exposure through privilege escalation into Amazon Bedrock knowledge bases and AI agents. Using GuardDuty, Security Hub, CloudTrail, and Athena, you'll reconstruct the full attack chain and walk away with the skills to detect, investigate, and respond when threat actors pivot from traditional cloud resources into generative AI workloads.

title: It's live. Now what? Operating AI on Amazon Bedrock
description: Your AI workload is live, and now you own it: latency creeping up, costs outgrowing usage, and no line from spend to teams. Start with the metrics that matter on Amazon Bedrock: time to first token, latency, throttles, and cache tokens. Then learn why latency alone cannot tell you what broke, and how output tokens per second separates a slower model from a longer answer. Also learn why throttling starts before you reach your quota. Finally, attribute token spend to teams using request metadata and caller identity. Leave with an instrumentation checklist and the alarms worth paging on.
location: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

speakers.name: Rashim Gupta
speakers.title: Senior Manager, Product Management, Amazon Web Services

title: Java to Graviton: three migration tools, one decision tree
description: There are now three ways to migrate Java from x86 to Graviton. AWS Transform Custom runs at scale across hundreds of repos with managed CI/CD and validation. The open-source Java skill runs locally in any agentic IDE, no AWS credentials needed. The Arm MCP server (in Kiro) goes broader, covering non-Java languages and general x86-to-Arm patterns. Each fits a different team size, repo count, and migration timeline. We demo all three on the same codebase, show where each succeeds and where it hands off, and give you a decision framework so you pick the right tool before you start.
location: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Journey to post-quantum (PQ) authentication in AWS
description: You use certificates for identity, keys for token signing, and long-lived roots of trust. Now you need to migrate to post-quantum cryptography (PQC) for authentication. In this session, learn how AWS helps you start and stay PQ-ready while preserving backwards compatibility, performance, and AI-friendly security by default. We will demystify the present state and future trajectory of PQ authentication. We discuss the updated CNSA 2.0 dates when RSA and EC will no longer satisfy authentication requirements and the uncertainty around PQ public certificate formats and Merkle Trees in non-browser scenarios.

title: Keeping Your Lakehouse Fast: Optimization Methods for Performance & Cost (sponsored by Cloudera) (ARC205-S)
description: A common challenge with large-scale Apache Iceberg tables is keeping performance and costs under control as use and volumes grow. Optimizing tables is the solution, but it’s a tough problem to solve. As data volumes grow, querying effectively requires deliberate tuning and optimization strategies. Streaming ingestion, small files, delete files, aging metadata can gradually increase query latency and costs. In this session, you’ll learn the core optimization techniques that every Iceberg developer should understand, including partitioning, compaction, clustering, cleaning, and data skipping. You'll also learn how these techniques improve query planning and when to apply them. At the end of the session, you’ll see how these best practices can be automated using Cloudera Lakehouse Optimizer to improve performance and reduce costs. This presentation is brought to you by Cloudera, an AWS Partner.
location: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Keep sleeping at 3am: Elastic watches your Prometheus metrics so you don't have to (sponsored by Elastic) (BIZ208-S)
description: When your kubernetes cluster fires at 3am, who's investigating? In this session we'll show Elastic Nightshift — our autonomous AI SRE — detecting a real Kubernetes incident and working it end to end: from alert to root cause to remediation, with its reasoning made transparent at every step. Nightshift draws on native Prometheus and PromQL metrics in Elastic. Kubernetes logs, out-of-the-box EKS dashboards and workflows, and ES|QL subqueries that correlate metrics with logs and traces in a single investigation. We'll also show how the 30x faster columnar metrics engine and full telemetry retention give Nightshift the complete context it needs to work like your best engineer This presentation is brought to you by Elastic, an AWS Partner.
location: Venetian | Level 2 | Ballroom F | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Keep your open source observability, move to managed scale
description: Teams standardized on Prometheus, Grafana, and OpenSearch should not have to abandon their tools to get scale and lower operational overhead. In this hands-on builders session, you will learn about instrumentation and collection powered by OpenTelemetry, and explore that telemetry into managed open source services: ship metrics to PromQL in Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, logs and traces in Amazon OpenSearch Service, and correlate all signals in Amazon Managed Grafana. Own your telemetry pipelines end-to-end with open standards and AWS managed services.

title: Kiro Crew: Architecture of an open source AI coding agent built on Kiro
description: Kiro Crew is an open source AI coding workspace built on Kiro CLI that grew from a side project to 39,000 users and nearly 500 contributors inside Amazon. Unlike single-session assistants, Kiro Crew combines multi-step task orchestration, tool-use planning, and a shared context layer for real engineering workflows. In this chalk talk, we'll walk through how Kiro Crew decomposes complex tasks, selects and chains tools, manages execution state, and integrates with existing developer environments. We'll discuss the design trade-offs that enabled rapid adoption and our journey to open source.

title: Kiro Writes the PR. Nobody Validates the App. (sponsored by TestMu) (AIM396-S)
description: Kiro can now build a whole feature on its own: write the spec, implement it, and open the PR without anyone sitting in the loop. That’s real progress. But nothing in that pipeline actually runs the app and checks it against what the spec promised. The checks that gate the PR look at the code, not the behavior. So the PR arrives looking done, and “done” is still just a guess someone has to trust. The good news is Kiro already produces the one thing a testing agent needs to close that gap: a clear, structured spec of what the feature is supposed to do. We’ll show Kane-CLI plugged in as a Kiro Power, reading that spec, actually running the app the way a user would, and reporting back proof, not just a checkmark, before the PR merges. This presentation is brought to you by TestMu, an AWS Partner.
location: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Builder Theater

title: KNFSD File Cache: Extending Your NFS Storage into the Cloud
description: Need to cache and serve NFS data from on-premises filers, across Availability Zones and Regions, or from other cloud providers with full read and write-back support? In this chalk talk, dive into KNFSD File Cache, an open-source, kernel-based NFS caching proxy on Amazon EC2 that transparently extends existing NFS storage into AWS. A single Terraform module stands up a production-ready, autoscaling cluster with high throughput and at low cost. Discuss hybrid and burst-compute patterns across M&E, HPC, Financial Services, and Life Sciences industries—eliminating latency without migration, client changes, or vendor lock-in.

title: Knowledge Representations for Autonomous Software Lifecycle Management
description: What formal properties must a software representation satisfy for agents to manage entire application lifecycles autonomously — reasoning at the specification level, not the code level? This session examines the open scientific questions behind agentic code understanding: encoding both structural topology and business semantics into a unified knowledge graph, extracting and grounding business rules when institutional context has been lost, enabling agent reasoning over large heterogeneous graphs without coherence degradation, and establishing deterministic validation signals that replace human judgment with formal guarantees. Drawing from graph theory, knowledge representation, specification mining, and formal verification research, we explore what makes these problems hard, where current approaches break at scale, and what architectural principles make full-lifecycle autonomy tractable. Attendees will leave with a rigorous understanding of the representation and reasoning foundations required for agents that don’t just generate code but understand, validate, evolve, and replace software as knowledge.

title: Know your data: discovery, context, and AI agents in Amazon S3
description: Organizations store billions of objects in Amazon S3 but struggle to answer basic questions: What do I have? Where did it come from? Is it still relevant? Learn how S3 Metadata and annotations turn your storage into a searchable, context-rich data estate. See how to attach business meaning directly to objects, query metadata at petabyte scale through managed Apache Iceberg tables, and drive governance workflows from metadata signals. Then discover how the AWS MCP Server and Agent Toolkit give AI agents governed access to your data, and how AWS Context lets them reason over relationships across your S3 data.
location: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Kubernetes-native agentic AI on Amazon EKS with open source primitives
description: Production agentic AI needs a scalable runtime, governed LLM access, persistent memory, observability, tool discovery, and secure code isolation. In this workshop you'll build all six on Amazon EKS using native Kubernetes primitives and open source projects. Tackle all six end-to-end or take individual modules home. Deploy LiteLLM as a multi-model gateway, Mem0 for user-scoped memory, Langfuse for observability into reasoning and tool calls, an MCP registry for tool discovery, and sandboxes for hardware-level code isolation. Leave with a scalable, GitOps-ready, portable reference architecture.

Production KYC, live code — and the cost and abandonment numbers that make it matter.

description: Lab Maker on AWS Skill Builder generates personalized hands-on labs from natural language prompts, allowing you to learn and experiment in the Console without incurring costs or risking production environments. During this session, we will generate a custom lab in real time before saving and sharing it with a team, demonstrating the full creation-to-collaboration workflow. We will then push Lab Maker further by generating a lab for a recently launched AWS service and uploading real organizational constraints to show how the tool adapts to your specific environment. You will leave this session with the knowledge and confidence to create your own labs.
