title: Lambda for every scale and workload shape
description: Honeycomb spends millions of dollars a year on Lambda. Every cold query runs through a map-reduce backend that used to mean one tier, Lambda Functions, regardless of shape. We outgrew Lambda Functions, not Lambda: Managed Instances now absorbs steady-state baseline traffic at roughly 7.5x lower cost than Functions, MicroVMs takes spikes of load tolerating 1.5 seconds of added latency, and Functions still catches bursty spillover. We'll walk through the observability and benchmarks that drove each cutover, and the routing logic deciding which tier a query lands on before it executes. You'll learn how to scale your serverless workloads multiple orders of magnitude without linear cost.
location: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Lambda Managed Instances: Always-on Serverless Compute
description: Some Lambda workloads run constantly. For steady-state, high-throughput functions, per-invocation pricing becomes more expensive than running the same code on EC2, but you don't want to manage instances. Lambda Managed Instances give you EC2 economics with multi-concurrency while Lambda handles instance lifecycle, patching, and scaling. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard the decision: when Managed Instances beat standard Lambda pricing, what workloads migrate cleanly versus what needs adaptation, and how to model your break-even point. Bring your Lambda bill. We'll help you find where Managed Instances save money and where they don't.

Bring your Lambda bill. We'll help you find where Managed Instances save money and where they don't.

title: Lambda Managed Instances: EC2 Power with Serverless Simplicity
description: AWS Lambda Managed Instances enables you to run Lambda functions on your choice of EC2 compute. With Lambda Managed Instances, you can optimize the performance and cost efficiency of your functions by utilizing specialized EC2 instance types and EC2 pricing benefits, while maintaining the familiar Serverless programming model and benefits like automatic patching, scaling, and 200+ AWS services integration for event-driven workloads. This session will provide an in-depth overview of how to get started with Lambda Managed Instances, recent launches like 90-minute function timeout, enhanced observability, and a behind-the-scenes look at how Lambda manages and scales your instances to ensure a seamless serverless experience.

title: Lambda MicroVMs: Secure stateful sandboxes for code execution
description: AI agents generate code, customers upload plugins, and third-party extensions need execution environments. All of it requires strong isolation. In this chalk talk, we discuss Lambda MicroVMs: VM-level, isolated sandboxes with filesystem state that persists across invocations. We cover the security model (how isolation boundaries prevent lateral movement), stateful session management for multi-turn agent interactions, lifecycle controls that limit resource consumption, and integration patterns with Step Functions and EventBridge for orchestrating sandboxed workloads. Bring your multi-tenant architecture questions. We'll whiteboard where MicroVMs fit versus standard Lambda.

title: Lambda MicroVMs: The Missing Serverless Primitive for Multi-Tenant Agents
description: Lambda Functions are stateless and time out after 15 minutes. Fargate tasks are expensive to keep warm. When building multi-tenant agent platforms, I needed per-tenant isolation without per-tenant cost. Lambda MicroVMs solve this: Firecracker VM-level isolation, 8-hour stateful execution, auto-suspend when idle, instant resume on next request. This session walks through the architecture I built, replacing always-on containers with MicroVMs as per-tenant agent sandboxes. I'll share the tradeoffs, what surprised me, and a deployable pattern you can take home and ship.

title: Lambda performance tuning and cost optimization
description: Most Lambda functions run at default memory settings, which means you're paying more for slower execution. Right-sizing memory often reduces cost and latency at the same time. In this chalk talk, we go beyond memory tuning: cold start elimination with SnapStart and provisioned concurrency, architecture-level savings like batching and right-sizing event source mappings, and when Lambda Managed Instances deliver better economics than per-invocation pricing. We whiteboard the decision points using real cost data and discuss which CloudWatch and Cost Explorer metrics actually drive optimization decisions.

title: Lessons from Netflix's distributed PostgreSQL migration to Aurora
description: In this session, explore the migration playbook and lessons learned from moving some of Netflix's largest workloads from a self-managed, distributed PostgreSQL-compatible database on Amazon EC2 to Aurora. Discover how PostgreSQL compatibility minimized code changes while the shared storage architecture of Aurora eliminated cross-node coordination overhead, delivering up to 75% lower, more predictable latency and up to 28% cost savings. Learn about workload selection and sequencing, near-zero downtime cutovers with data consistency validation and rollback planning, and post-migration operational lessons including vacuum debt, connection management, and query plan stability.

title: Lessons in Scale and Innovation Through the Deployment of AI Agents
description: AI agents on AWS are transforming how Amazon teams build, ship, and operate at velocity and scale. Discover how Amazon Finance Operations, supporting 6,000+ analysts across nine global service centers, deploys AI agents to resolve millions of contacts and hundreds of thousands of cases annually, automating low-value tasks and running autonomous workflows in a high-stakes finance environment. Then explore how Amazon Operation’s Workforce Intelligence & Scheduling Engine (WISE) enables them to orchestrate the operating, management, and adjustment of labor and flow across more than 1,200 facilities. When a gap in a tool, process, or service appears, it spins up autonomous coding agents on Bedrock AgentCore to build, test, and deploy solutions or mechanisms to close the gaps. Leaders will share the innovations that enabled them to stop managing systems and start orchestrating them.

AI teammates orchestrate more than 18 forecasting tools and models trained on Amazon data, then harmonize statistical forecasts, customer commitments, and cross functional inputs into one consensus plan. You will leave knowing how to reach a forecast your whole team trusts, how the system keeps accuracy honest over time, and how to stop reconciling numbers in spreadsheets before every planning cycle.

description: In this session, we'll dive into advanced bot mitigation using the AWS WAF SDK and label evaluations. We'll explore programmatically managing WAF rules, leveraging labels for granular request inspection, and integrating SDK workflows to automate threat response across mobile app, JavaScript, and API traffic integrations. Through real-world scenarios, you'll see how to distinguish legitimate traffic from sophisticated bots, reduce false positives, and maintain application performance across surfaces. Bring your questions and learn how to implement scalable, intelligent bot protection at the edge.

title: Lifecycle of a pod: trust boundaries in VM-isolated containers
description: Trace a pod from kubelet's RunPodSandbox call to process execution inside a VM isolated sandbox, then dissect the hard problems at each boundary crossing: how do you enforce policy on what runtime actions are allowed? How do you transport container images into an isolated environment the parent cannot read? Where does attestation fit, and how can you truly trust what is running inside? We examine how the trust model shifts between untrusted host and untrusted guest, explore the tradeoffs between CRI compatibility and security invariants, and discuss how EKS is approaching VM-level workload isolation

Great demo, wrong architecture. When real users arrived, the demo cracked. So we pivoted. Long-running agents moved off Lambda onto ephemeral ECS Fargate tasks. API keys swapped for firewalled Amazon Bedrock, feature-branched CI/CD with dev-to-prod promotion, and Next.js behind CloudFront, S3, and Lambda@Edge. We break down each tradeoff from first idea to first customer. Leave knowing how to tell demo-grade architectures from customer-grade ones — and when to make the jump.

title: Live-code inference patterns for agentic workloads on Amazon Bedrock
description: Agentic workloads are multi-step, tool-calling, and retrieval-augmented, which means they stress the inference layer differently than a single prompt. In this code talk, we build three patterns live: function calling, multi-step reasoning chains, and retrieval-augmented generation with Knowledge Bases. For each, you see how it behaves at the inference level, including token consumption, latency, and retry logic, and how to tune it for cost and speed. You leave with working code for all three patterns that you can adapt to your own agents.

title: Load-bearing coupling: Finding the coupling you can't cut
description: Teams break up monoliths to move faster, then find the pieces still fail together. Some coupling is doing real structural work: invariants spanning writes, ordering guarantees, timing assumptions baked into callers. Cut it and you get a distributed monolith, the same dependency with new failure modes. In this session, we whiteboard real systems, insert seams, and price what each dependency costs to cross a boundary: consistency, backpressure, retry semantics. Apply a simple test: if a circuit breaker can't open here without breaking correctness, that coupling is load-bearing. Bring your hardest dependency; leave knowing which coupling to cut, which to keep, and why.

description: "Living off the land" (LOTL) attacks use native OS tools to evade detection. In 2026, techniques evolved to "Living off the Agent" (LOTA), compromising enterprise AI agents through subtle prompt injections to exfiltrate data, escalate privileges, and move laterally. Red team studies identified vulnerabilities in production AI agents with distinct LOTA patterns. This chalk talk explores the LOTA taxonomy, detection strategies, and architectural containment patterns. Bring your architecture diagrams, and we'll whiteboard defenses together.

This session proves how 5th-Gen AMD EPYC "Turin" on EC2 runs general-purpose workloads faster and smaller, delivering >30% OpEx savings you can redirect from IT overhead into AI budgets. title: Make every GPU count: Maximizing GPU efficiency for inference at scale
description: When an inference fleet spans thousands of interconnected NVIDIA GPUs in NVL72 racks, scheduling decisions cascade. Place a job wrong, and it fragments a capacity block, starves NVLink bandwidth, or strands GPUs behind a topology boundary. In this session, AWS and OpenAI will share scheduling and bin-packing strategies developed for production inference on Amazon EC2 UltraServers. Explore rack-aware placement that respects 72-GPU NVLink domains, approaches for mixed workload profiles (prefill vs. decode vs. batch), capacity block utilization maximization, and Kubernetes scheduling primitives that enforce topology constraints. Leave with actionable blueprints to efficiently schedule GPU inference at scale.
location: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

See how Confluent Tableflow turns Kafka topics into Apache Iceberg tables and registers them in the AWS Glue Data Catalog—eliminating the need for custom streaming pipelines. Discover how this integration enables data engineers to reduce ingestion complexity, strengthen governance and put real-time data to work for analytics and AI with Amazon Athena. title: Make your vector search faster, more relevant, and cost-efficient
description: You have a vector workload running and questions piling up: How do I raise relevance? How do I control cost as I scale? Which ranking technique fits my data? We give you a quick tour of vector capabilities in Amazon OpenSearch Service, then spend the rest of the session working through your problems. Topics on the table include hybrid search combining lexical and vector results, ranking with reciprocal rank fusion, maximal marginal relevance, and filtering strategies, when to reach for Automatic Semantic Enrichment or neural sparse vectors instead of building your own embedding pipeline, and cost optimization techniques including quantization, tiered storage, GPU-accelerated indexing, and auto-optimization. Come with a workload in mind and leave with tuning direction for your specific situation.

title: Making your Amazon Aurora cluster more resilient
description: Amazon Aurora is a cloud-native relational database with unparalleled high performance and availability at global scale. Hundreds of thousands of organizations trust Aurora for their workloads today. In this session, learn about features such as Aurora Global Database and Amazon RDS Proxy, and discover best practices to achieve high availability for Aurora MySQL and Aurora PostgreSQL database clusters. The session includes a whiteboarding discussion on high availability and disaster recovery solutions to help maximize application resilience.

speakers.name: Tim Stoakes
speakers.title: Sr. Principal Technologist, Amazon Web Services

title: Malware Protection: hands-on detection and response for malicious files
description: In this one-hour builder session, get hands-on with the core capabilities of Amazon GuardDuty Malware Protection. Configure on-demand S3 scanning using the SendObjectMalwareScan API, set up automated EBS volume scanning for EC2 instances, and build event-driven response pipelines that quarantine infected objects before they spread. Walk through real malware samples triggering findings, interpret scan results, and integrate with Security Hub for centralized visibility. Leave with a working malware detection and response workflow deployed in your own account.
location: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1

title: Manage cloud costs and AI spend with AWS Cost Management
description: Join this breakout to learn how AI is helping teams manage cloud costs more effectively, and why managing the cost of AI itself is becoming just as important. We cover AWS FinOps enhancements across both dimensions. On the "AI for FinOps" side, learn how your team can operate more efficiently through automation and agentic workflows. On the "FinOps for AI" side, see how you can access and manage your AI spend with granular cost data and governance. Walk away with a repeatable governance model as you scale AI with confidence.
location: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Red Theater

speakers.name: Bowen Wang
speakers.title: Principal Product Manager Outbound, Amazon Web Services

title: Managing and monitoring AWS Direct Connect at scale: customer lessons
description: AWS shares customer best practices for managing and monitoring AWS Direct Connect at hyperscale. Network teams discusses how they operate one of the world's largest Direct Connect footprints, spanning multiple regions and supporting AI training workloads that serve billions of users. We deep-dive into new monitoring capabilities: Amazon CloudWatch metrics for BGP session health and prefix counts, VIF rate limiters that prevent bandwidth contention across shared connections, and Network Synthetic Monitor for proactive path-level health diagnostics. Attendees will learn strategies for alerting, capacity planning, and building unified dashboards for cross-Region network visibility.
location: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Managing Bots, Mentoring Brains: The Future of Hybrid Leadership
description: The traditional playbook for executive leadership is undergoing fundamental change as hybrid ecosystems of human employees and autonomous AI agents become commonplace, with agents acting as co-workers, specialists, and decision-makers. This shift requires executives to expand their skill set, dividing organizational goals between human creative strategy and agentic operational execution. Moving past the AI hype, this session examines how human roles must evolve from executors to context engineers and decision architects, and how career progression must be rewritten when entry-level and repetitive work is owned by digital labor. Explore how women in leadership will adapt and build tomorrow's leaders.

title: Managing Lambda Runtimes at Scale for Platform Teams
description: Lambda's managed runtimes work until your platform team needs a pinned language version, a pre-loaded monitoring agent, or an SDK that every function must use. Today that means managing custom layers, coordinating updates across teams, and hoping nobody is running a version you deprecated last quarter. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard strategies for taking control of your Lambda runtime layer. Bring your runtime requirements and the constraints you're working around today.

title: Managing software vulnerabilities in the agentic world
description: Vulnerability management is evolving beyond detection. As AI agents generate and deploy code at machine speed, security teams need a fundamentally different approach to identifying, prioritizing, and resolving software vulnerabilities. In this session, explore how AWS thinks about the future of vulnerability management — from contributing to open source vulnerability databases and detecting malicious packages before they reach your pipeline, to enforcing remediation at scale without slowing development velocity. Learn how to shift from reactive CVE chasing to a proactive posture that accounts for AI-generated code, autonomous deployments, and the expanding software supply chain.
location: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | White Theater

speakers.name: Anthony Verleysen
speakers.title: Sr. Product Manager Technical - External Services, AWS

title: Map once and prove everywhere across multiple compliance frameworks
description: Regulatory frameworks like SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, and the EU AI Act each demand separate assessments, yet a significant portion of their requirements overlap. You spend time collecting duplicate evidence for controls you already have. This chalk talk introduces the control inheritance approach and shows how a single AWS Config rule or organizational policy can satisfy requirements across multiple frameworks. You walk through real examples of framework overlap, automation patterns that eliminate duplicate evidence collection, and a governance approach you can implement immediately.

title: Mapping and Securing the Enterprise AI Attack Surface (sponsored by Zscaler) (AIM290-S)
description: AI is racing across the enterprise—showing up in endpoints, apps, workflows, agents, and data paths faster than most security teams can track. But securing AI takes more than knowing where it exists; it requires understanding how data flows, where it comes from, where it goes, and which users, devices, apps, and AI endpoints interact with it along the way. In this session, we’ll explore how to map the AI attack surface and its data lineage while securing the AI endpoints where innovation actually happens. This presentation is brought to you by Zscaler, an AWS Partner.

speakers.name: Mark Ryan
speakers.title: Vice President, AI Strategy & Architecture, Zscaler, Inc.

title: Master Agent Skills: From Desktop Builds to Production Deployment
description: Build, govern, and scale production-ready agent skills across your enterprise on Amazon Quick. Author custom skills on Quick, then shift to the admin perspective: register skills in Quick Catalog for org-wide discovery, configure access policies, and schedule autonomous execution at scale. Through two business-driven use cases — churn prevention from contact center data and intelligent claims processing that eliminates manual back-office work — you'll deploy measurable automation. Leave with working skills, a governance framework for hundreds of agents across teams, and a playbook for communicating ROI to leadership.
location: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Milano I

speakers.name: Leo Mentis Raj Selvaraj

speakers.title: Senior Specialist Solutions Architect - Amazon Quick, Amazon Web Services

title: Mastercard: Training a large transaction model on billions of transactions
description: Large language models transformed text. Large transaction models (LTMs) aim to do the same for payment and commerce data. Instead of brittle, hand-crafted feature pipelines feeding hundreds of specialized models, LTMs are transformer-based foundation models pre-trained directly on billions of anonymized transactions, learning rich representations of transactions, merchant behavior, consumer activity, and financial risk. This session introduces Mastercard's LTM program, the architectural choices behind it, and the unique challenges of tokenizing and training on tabular and sequential financial data at massive scale. We show how foundation models power diverse production use cases, from fraud detection to personalization to reaching underserved cardholders.
location: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Red Theater

speakers.name: Gurinder Singh
speakers.title: Principal Solutions architect, Amazon web services

title: Mastering agentic development: skills, custom agents, and steering
description: The best results from agentic AI don't come from clever one-off prompts, but from shaping how agents work. In this session, go beyond prompting to learn techniques that apply to any agentic coding tool. Craft reusable skills that encode your team's know-how, build custom agents tuned to specific jobs, and use steering files to carry your conventions and architecture across sessions. We'll cover how to set goals the agent will actually follow, when to let it run autonomously, and how to tell a skill that's useful versus noise. We'll demo live in Kiro, but the principles transfer wherever you work.

title: Mastering LLM tokenomics: From token costs to business outcomes
description: Financial institutions are scaling generative AI and agentic workloads to production and need strategies to keep costs aligned with business value. With enterprise workloads requiring retrieval, orchestration, validation, and governance layers, understanding token economics becomes critical to sustainable growth. In this chalk talk, we'll walk through design patterns for controlling token consumption while maintaining quality, including prompt compression, semantic caching with Amazon ElastiCache, tiered model routing with Amazon Bedrock, and cost attribution using Amazon CloudWatch. We'll whiteboard the hidden cost drivers in agentic AI systems and share design patterns that financial institutions use to control token consumption while maintaining quality.

title: Maximize EKS efficiency: Auto Mode, Graviton, and Spot best practices
description: Achieving optimal compute efficiency on Amazon EKS demands more than choosing the right instance -- it requires an intelligent infrastructure layer that continuously optimizes on your behalf. In this chalk talk, learn how teams use EKS Auto Mode to eliminate infrastructure toil with up to 40% faster node boot times, over 40% faster scale-out, and up to 70% faster consolidation. Discover how pairing Auto Mode with AWS Graviton5 (M9g, C9g) and EC2 Spot can reduce total cluster spend by up to 40%. You'll leave with actionable strategies for multi-architecture scheduling, right-sizing, and EFA placement for ML workloads.

title: Maximize GPU utilization across training and inference on HyperPod
description: Join this interactive chalk talk to explore how SageMaker HyperPod serves as a unified GPU pool for data processing, training, post-training, and inference without re-platforming. Through live whiteboarding, demos, and production architectures; we'll cover how customers are maximizing GPU utilization across workloads, regions, and multiple teams with shared architectures and GPUs. Then learn how SageMaker Studio gives give data scientists, AI researchers, and machine learning engineers an easy way to to iterate on jobs all on the shared pool of resources. We'll also see how Humain has optimized utilization of compute resources across two large HyperPod clusters, onboarding multiple teams of researchers with team isolation and advanced task submission strategies. Participants will walk away with practical patterns for running the full model lifecycle on resilient, shared infrastructure

title: Maximizing block storage performance for high-intensity workloads
description: Amazon EBS handles over 222 trillion I/O operations daily. Performance matters, a lot, but it’s not just about average performance, it’s about stable low latency that minimizes outliers or tail latency. io2 Block Express volumes are designed for that purpose with consistent sub-millisecond latency and 99.999% durability for critical applications such as SAP HANA, Oracle, Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL, and more. Learn about how its performance characteristics optimize compute utilization, leading to cost efficiency and the success of many performance-demanding use cases.
location: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | White Theater

title: Maximizing EC2 NVMe local storage
description: Discover how to leverage the latest high-performance Nitro SSDs in EC2 storage-optimized instances for data-intensive workloads. This technical session explores new capabilities for monitoring and managing NVMe instance storage, including enhanced performance metrics—latency, IOPS, and throughput—to optimize and troubleshoot your workloads. We also demonstrate the new AWS Local Instance Storage (LIS) CSI driver for simplified NVMe volume management in Amazon EKS. Learn best practices for storage performance monitoring and integrating the LIS CSI driver in containerized applications.

title: Maximizing GPU utilization for inference at scale on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
description: In this session, infrastructure architects will learn how to build scalable systems with GPUs that maximize utilization and turn shared infrastructure into a profitable, multi-tenant service. Multiverse Computing will demonstrate how they scaled GPU utilization from 30% to over 80% across 1,000+ H200 and B300 GPUs on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod. We'll dive into the architecture decisions - tenant isolation, fair-share scheduling with Kueue, GPU partitioning with MIG, per-customer quotas - and the operational patterns that make it possible to serve diverse customer workloads from a single cluster in a true SaaS model.
location: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

speakers.title: Principal Product Manager - Tech, Amazon Web Services

title: MCP and A2A for SaaS: making your product agent-ready
description: Agentic AI is reshaping how SaaS products reach end customers. Alongside browser and API interactions, exposing capabilities through Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and distributing agents via the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol is fast becoming the norm. In this session, build the two pieces every multi-tenant, agent-ready SaaS needs: an MCP server exposing your tools and resources, and an A2A endpoint with agent cards for inter-agent calls. Discover reference architectures for MCP in front of existing APIs, A2A agent cards, and authentication and authorization on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Leave with a blueprint for being a citizen in the agentic ecosystem.
location: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 1

title: MCP is Just An MVP. Knowledge Lakes Are The Sequel. (sponsored by Atolio) (BIZ205-S)
description: MCP lets agents connect to systems. It's a minimum viable product, not a complete way to run that connection at scale. Raw database access hit the same wall decades ago, before warehouses and data lakes brought structure and governance at scale. Point-to-point agent connections hit it again: costs climb with every added tool call, latency stacks with every cross-system hop, and permissions rarely travel with retrieved data, making synthesized knowledge a sharper security risk than raw SQL ever posed. This session traces that history, breaks down each failure mode, and maps what a knowledge lake built for agents solves. This presentation is brought to you by Atolio, an AWS Partner.
location: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Builder Theater

title: MCP Meets GraphQL: A Typed Foundation for Enterprise AI Agents (sponsored by Apollo GraphQL) (AIM112-S)
description: Enterprises connecting AI agents to systems of record face three unsolved problems: can an agent discover what data exists and what it means, get that context without runaway token cost, and touch only what it's authorized to touch. GraphQL, the proven Linux Foundation-backed standard beneath many of the world's largest customer experiences at brands like Netflix, AirBnB, Shopify, Walmart, and countless others, already solves all three through self-describing schemas and field-level queries. This talk lays out the architecture for combining GraphQL with MCP, including Apollo's approach to graph-based orchestration for cost and reliability. This presentation is brought to you by Apollo GraphQL, an AWS Partner.
location: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Builder Theater

title: Measuring emergent risks in frontier models
description: As frontier models scale in capability, so does their potential for deceptive and manipulative behavior—risks that static, single-turn evaluations fail to capture. We present our multi-layered approach to measuring emergent deception under Amazon's Frontier Model Safety Framework (FMSF), combining automated benchmarks, expert red-teaming, and uplift studies. We will dive deep into two innovations: D-REX, a benchmark detecting discrepancies between benign outputs and malicious internal chain-of-thought reasoning; and LH-Deception, a multi-agent simulation revealing emergent "chains of deception" across extended task sequences. Together, these tools address critical gaps in frontier safety evaluation and inform deployment governance.

title: Meet Your AI Teammate for WorkSpaces Administration
description: Whether you run WorkSpaces today or are evaluating cloud desktops for the first time, operational overhead follows every virtual desktop deployment: ongoing monitoring, systemic issues that surface as tickets, and end-user requests that consume administrator time. Most teams operate reactively, triaging problems after they surface and manually guiding users through resolution. This session explores how Amazon WorkSpaces Advisor is using AI to reduce resolution time for both IT administrators and end users. We'll walk through the operational challenges we're hearing from customers, share our approach to solving them, and demonstrate early results from production environments. Bring your deployment architecture questions.

title: Migrate and modernize infrastructure from your IDE with agentic AI
description: Migration and modernization involve dozens of manual steps across landing zones, networking, and containerization. What if you could drive the entire workflow from your IDE? In this code talk, you'll see how Kiro and AWS Transform work together as an agentic toolkit. First, generate a multi-account landing zone as infrastructure as code. Next, feed a VMware configuration export to the network agent and get Terraform modules or CDK constructs for VPCs, security groups, and production-ready network topology. Then point the containerization agent at a repo to produce ECR images and deploy to Amazon EKS.

title: Migrate on-premises storage to AWS with agentic AI
description: Migrating on-premises storage to AWS typically means weeks of manual assessment, business case building, and wave planning before a single byte moves. AWS Transform's agentic AI capabilities handle the full lifecycle, from automated assessment and business case generation to wave planning and execution, reducing that timeline to hours. In this lightning talk, see how to migrate storage from VMware estates, enterprise databases, and associated data with AI handling the complexity. Leave knowing how to start your first Transform project and accelerate time to results.
location: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Lightning Theater

title: Migrate SQL Server to Aurora PostgreSQL with AI-powered conversion
description: Migrating SQL Server databases with stored procedures, triggers, and complex T-SQL constructs to Aurora PostgreSQL typically takes weeks of manual schema conversion and dependency resolution. In this workshop, you'll walk through the end-to-end workflow using AWS Transform's agentic AI: assess your SQL Server database, automate schema conversion, resolve dependencies, then hand off to your local IDE where you review, refine, and deploy converted database objects directly. You'll leave knowing how to reduce weeks of manual effort to hours while improving conversion accuracy and confidence.

title: Migrate to Amazon DynamoDB with AI-powered schema design
description: Amazon DynamoDB schema design is the number one barrier to adoption, requiring upfront knowledge of access patterns and partition strategies, which most teams learn through trial and error. New AI-powered schema design tools for DynamoDB change that. In this live coding session, follow along as a banking payment-processing application is migrated from a relational database to DynamoDB. The session covers workload analysis, optimized table design generation, cost and throughput tradeoff comparisons, and iterative refinement toward production-quality schemas, including reviewing AI-generated code, refining the implementation, migrating data, and demonstrating the complete end-to-end solution.

title: Migrate workloads to Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)
description: Running self-managed document databases at scale introduces significant operational burden, version lock-in, and rising infrastructure costs. Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) addresses these challenges with a fully managed, highly available service. In this session, examine compatibility features that simplify migration from existing document database environments, and work through architecture decisions affecting performance, cost, and reliability. Discover how enhancements in version 8.0 deliver up to 5x compression and 7x query performance improvement. Discuss common migration blockers, schema transformation approaches, and newest compatibility additions that reduce friction during cutover. Learn a framework for planning and executing document database migrations on AWS.

title: Migrate your NAS to the cloud: Building AI-ready file storage
description: Enterprises store vast amounts of business-critical data on NAS systems, but aging hardware and rising costs are only part of the story. Legacy file storage also locks data away from modern AI workloads. Learn proven strategies for migrating NAS environments to Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP, then connecting that data to AWS analytics and AI services, including options like S3 Access Points, Amazon Bedrock, and SageMaker. We cover assessing your NAS estate, executing migrations with minimal disruption, and choosing the right path to unlock your data for modern workloads. You leave with a practical framework for modernizing file storage.
location: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Red Theater

title: Migrating a Managed Assistant API to Strands Agents SDK
description: As organizations scale AI agent deployments, the gap between managed APIs and production-grade frameworks becomes a migration challenge. This talk describes a large-scale migration from a managed assistant API serving hundreds of agent projects to Strands Agents, selected for its deterministic orchestration, multi-provider portability, and open-source extensibility. The migration replaced three subsystems (orchestration, conversation persistence, and observability) while preserving all existing tool implementations. This session details the architectural decisions, backward-compatible tool migration, security constraints for production deployment, and evaluation methodology that validated quality parity. These patterns generalize to any organization migrating from managed AI APIs to open-source agent frameworks.
location: Caesars Palace | Promenade South | Octavius 4 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

speakers.name: Ryan Coleman
speakers.title: Principal Product Manager, Amazon Web Services

title: Migrating legacy ETL to serverless with AWS Glue
description: Enterprises using traditional ETL tools on-premises infrastructure face mounting pressure from licensing costs, scaling limits, and operational overhead. Migrating these entrenched pipelines to a serverless model is achievable with the right patterns, but the path is rarely a straight lift-and-shift. In this chalk talk, we'll work through proven migration patterns for moving legacy ETL workloads to AWS Glue. We will tackle topics such as converting complex transformation logic, handling incremental and change-data-capture loads, preserving data quality and lineage, and phasing cutover to minimize risk. Bring your toughest migration questions and leave with a practical framework f of how serverless ETL changes the economics and operations of data integration.

title: Migrating petabytes of data: Real-world strategies with AWS DataSync
description: Learn how to plan, build, and implement the migration of 10 petabytes of on-premises data with AWS DataSync. Through interactive discussion and whiteboarding, explore effective approaches for data categorization and creating transfer job manifests that map directly to cost-optimized S3 storage classes. Discover how this data migration architecture accelerates the migration of client data to Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP. This chalk talk provides practical insights and best practices for executing large-scale data migrations to AWS.

speakers.name: Wali Akbari
speakers.title: Principal AI Infra Specialist, Amazon Web Services

title: Mitigating prompt injection with structured outputs in Amazon Bedrock
description: Prompt injection works because LLM outputs are unconstrained. Structured outputs in Amazon Bedrock compiles a JSON Schema into a grammar and enforces it during decoding so every token the model emits is a valid position in the schema. In this code talk, we live-code defense schemas for sentiment analysis, intent classification, and SQL validation, then attack them with real injection payloads. We cover provider differences between Claude and open-weight models, strict tool use for agentic workflows, and how to combine grammar enforcement with input validation for defense in depth.
location: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Code Talk

speakers.name: Aswath Ram A Srinivasan
speakers.title: Sr. WW Specialist Solutions Architect- Bedrock, Amazon Web Services

title: ML, automotive, and robotics simulations at scale on AWS Batch
description: Simulation and ML workloads share a hard problem: they must burst to enormous scale, run to completion reliably, and do it without a standing fleet draining budget between runs. This session shows how AWS Batch orchestrates large-scale simulation and training pipelines end to end. See how AWS Batch schedules and scales compute on demand, so jobs run when needed and nothing sits idle otherwise. Learn how simulation outputs flow through a shared data lake into GPU-accelerated training, closing the loop between data and models. Discover the orchestration and scheduling patterns that keep a real customer's high-throughput pipeline efficient.
location: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

speakers.name: Nikita Buldakov
speakers.title: Sr. Product Manager Technical - External Service, AWS

title: Modeling Human Preference: Pairwise Battles to Agentic Systems
description: Every time we rank an LLM, we're building a model of human preference — yet for most queries there's no ground truth, only a person's sense of which answer is better, shifting with expertise, culture, and expectations. This session examines how we model preference across two regimes: pairwise battles, arena-style voting ranked through Bradley-Terry, and agentic systems, where preference spans long-horizon, multi-step, tool-using tasks. Reward models and LLM-as-judge are themselves learned preference models; from our experience at Amazon, we examine when to trust them and how to separate progress from preference-overfitting. Attendees will learn what modeling preference at scale demands.

title: Modernize a Legacy Telecom Billing App with AWS Transform Custom
description: Got an old telecom application buried under decades of technical debt? In this hands-on session, you'll take a legacy BSS billing system and modernize it using AWS Transform Custom. Start by analyzing the codebase to understand business logic, dependencies, and technical debt. Then apply a built-in catalog transformation to upgrade the language and framework instantly. Next, define your own custom transformation in natural language to convert legacy interfaces to modern APIs. Validate, test for functional equivalence, and deploy to AWS. Walk away with a running modernized app and reusable transformation recipes, plus hands-on experience modernizing real-world telecom applications.
location: Caesars Forum | Level 1 | Forum 120 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2

speakers.name: Efrat Nir-Berger
speakers.title: Principal Solutions Architect, Amazon Web Services (AWS)

title: Modernize and containerize legacy apps to Amazon ECS with AWS Transform
description: Your application runs on an old Java runtime with outdated dependencies. You know it belongs in containers but the upgrade path feels daunting. In this builders session, take a legacy monolithic application and use AWS Transform to identify blockers, upgrade dependencies, generate multi-stage Dockerfiles, build and scan container images for vulnerabilities, and deploy to Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate. See how the agent handles multi-repo applications and validates containers before production. Walk through the full lifecycle without writing a single Dockerfile by hand. Bring your laptop to build alongside an AWS expert.

title: Modernize and migrate edge applications with AWS Outposts
description: Organizations running workloads on legacy virtualization platforms at the edge are looking to modernize these applications to be more resilient, portable, and operationally consistent with their cloud workloads. Simultaneously, AWS Outposts has released new second-generation single- and multi-rack offerings that deliver new instance types and Amazon EBS storage, up to 40% better price-performance, and enhanced networking features for monitoring and security. In this session, we'll cover modernization and migration strategies for organizations looking to move to a cloud operating model at the edge, as well as strategies for existing Outposts users to upgrade to the latest generation.

speakers.name: Brianna Rosentrater

title: Modernize confidently with production intelligence
description: Static code analysis tells you what to modernize. It doesn't tell you what breaks when you do. Runtime dependencies, real traffic patterns, and operational risk stay invisible until cutover, when surprises are most expensive. AWS DevOps Agent adds the missing ingredient: production intelligence fed directly into your AWS Transform modernization plan. The result is assessments grounded in reality and migrations that stay safe through execution. In this chalk talk, we discuss how to incorporate production intelligence from DevOps Agent into an automated migration pipeline by Transform Custom. Bring your modernization challenges to discuss.

AWS Transform reverse-engineers business rules from legacy code across platforms with full traceability, and Kiro translates that understanding into microservices specifications, generates production code, and creates Infrastructure as Code for AWS deployment. Leave with a repeatable pattern for reimagining batch workloads as real-time, event-driven microservices built on business rules that took decades to refine. Laptop required.

title: Modernizing .NET to Serverless: Native AOT and SnapStart, live
description: .NET workloads on Lambda have historically meant slower cold starts and JIT warmup time that doesn't match Serverless execution patterns. Native AOT and SnapStart on .NET 10 close that gap, bringing cold starts under 200ms, but modernization isn't flip-a-switch. In this code talk, modernize a .NET function to AOT live, watch it fail, then fix it on stage: serialization with source generators, reflection-based DI replaced, trimming warnings resolved. See real measurements across AOT, SnapStart, and the managed runtime. Walk away with a library compatibility matrix and modernization patterns for your own .NET Serverless journey.

title: Modernizing VMware workloads with Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP
description: Migrating VMware workloads to AWS often means rethinking storage, but it doesn't have to. In this chalk talk, we explore how Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP provides a storage foundation built for VMware migrations. Learn how FSx for ONTAP delivers multi-protocol support, enterprise data management, and ONTAP compatibility that VMware administrators already know. We'll discuss real world migration patterns, cost optimization through deduplication and compression, and high availability with Multi-AZ and zero RPO. Bring your questions and join us to design a migration strategy that minimizes disruption and maximizes your existing ONTAP investments.

title: Modernizing your compute stack with Lambda's new execution models
description: You're running workloads across Lambda, EC2, and containers because no single service handled orchestration, always-on compute, and isolated execution. Lambda's new execution models change that: durable functions add checkpointed orchestration, Managed Instances provide always-on compute at EC2 economics, and MicroVMs offer hardware-level sandboxes with persistent state. In this breakout, we discuss the operational decision tree: which execution model to standardize on for each workload class, how to manage mixed-model deployments, monitoring differences across models, and when to migrate workloads between them. Bring your workload portfolio. We'll help you build an operational playbook for multi-model Lambda.

title: Monetize AI Bot Traffic: Agent-Ready Media with AWS WAF & AI Analysis
description: More than half of web traffic now comes from AI bots that consume content built for humans while returning little value to publishers. This hands-on workshop tackles both the content and the monetization side. First, you'll build a pipeline that converts images, video, and audio into concise, agent-friendly markdown summaries including interpreting what's shown, said, and meant, while preserving the originals for human readers. Then you'll monetize bot traffic with AWS WAF AI traffic monetization, setting per-request pricing by bot verification tier and collecting payment via the x402 protocol. You'll build a working dual-audience pipeline and WAF pricing configuration you can deploy against your own media.

title: Monitoring and optimizing Amazon S3 with observability tools
description: As your S3 data estate grows across buckets, tables, and directory storage, operational visibility becomes critical for cost control, performance tuning, and security investigations. In this chalk talk, learn how to build a comprehensive observability strategy for Amazon S3. We will introduce S3 Storage Lens for organization-wide metrics and recommendations, server access logs for request-level diagnostics, CloudWatch metrics for real-time alerting, and S3 Metadata for storage analytics. We will walk through use cases for each tool, including when to reach for one over another, and deep dive into Storage Lens for optimizing at scale. Bring your monitoring questions as we work through real scenarios for identifying cost anomalies, diagnosing latency issues, and auditing access patterns across multi-account environments.

description: Great health checks tell you exactly how your application is really performing, not just that a port is open. Bring your architectures, including diagrams, napkin sketches, or draw live on the whiteboard, and we'll design your health strategy together. Leave knowing when to orchestrate, when to choreograph, and how to combine both in one architecture. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Multi-Region hedging: Where it works and where it breaks
description: Failover recovers after impairment; hedging survives it. This chalk talk examines where multi-Region hedging holds and where it breaks. We trace hedging across the stack: racing requests through Route 53 ARC and Elastic Load Balancing, containing blast radius with cell-based routing, and confronting the write path, where Aurora Global Database's asynchronous replication surfaces a consistency-versus-continuity trade-off that routing alone cannot resolve. Bring your availability-critical workload; we'll map its hedgeable read and routing paths against those that force an explicit consistency decision.

title: Multi-tenant isolation with IAM: ABAC, session tags, and token vending machines
description: Multi-tenant SaaS has two isolation options: application-layer filtering or IAM enforcement. Filtering requires every query and API call to add tenant scoping — one missed filter leaks data. IAM enforcement holds even when code has a bug, and Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) makes it work without per-tenant policy explosion. We cover the stack: ABAC session tags, a Token Vending Machine minting tenant-scoped STS credentials, IAM condition keys for DynamoDB/S3 partition boundaries, and a credential-caching model that keeps latency acceptable at millions of requests per second across thousands of tenants. Leave with a deployable reference architecture and policy template.

description: Amazon EKS has become the runtime of choice for ISVs building agentic SaaS, offering the control, workload isolation, and networking flexibility that managed runtimes cannot. In this workshop, build a multi-tenant agent deployment on EKS with tenant isolation across namespaces and network policies, IRSA-backed credentials per agent workload, and per-tenant observability via OpenTelemetry. Walk through real investigation scenarios where AI handles the repetitive evidence gathering while analysts focus on judgment calls: scoping impact, deciding containment actions, and validating findings. description: Achieving consistent, low-latency block storage at cloud scale requires rethinking every layer of the IO stack. Bring your questions and leave with an understanding of how EBS delivers high performing block storage for your mission-critical applications.

description: One firewall, many ways to deploy it, and each mode unlocks a different architectural superpower. This session maps your options: distributed, centralized, multi-endpoint, explicit proxy, and the newest firewall modes. Through real architectures, you'll see where each one shines, how they scale, and the patterns that make your network security clean, flexible, and future-ready. Whether you're protecting a single VPC or a global multi-account estate, you'll leave knowing exactly which mode fits your environment and why. title: Network observability on Amazon EKS: from blind spots to insights
description: As container workloads grow more distributed and interconnected, the network between them becomes the hardest thing to see. Traffic sprawls across pods, nodes, and AZs, quietly driving up cost through inter-AZ transfer and NAT processing, and when latency spikes, it is hard to tell which flows are responsible. See how to trace traffic across pods, nodes, and AZs. Learn how to attribute network cost and latency to the workloads driving them, and turn those signals into action.

description: In April 2026, an AI coding agent deleted a company's entire production database in nine seconds, without being asked. In this session, we recreate that incident live using Amazon Bedrock, walk through every failure in the chain, then rebuild the architecture with six hardening layers: Bedrock Guardrails, human approval gates, least-privilege IAM, deletion protection, isolated backups, and real-time monitoring. Walk away with a concrete checklist for designing AI-assisted systems that plan for when the AI is wrong, not just when it performs perfectly.

title: Nitro Isolation Engine: Formally verifying confidentiality
description: What does it mean, *precisely*, for the data of a virtual machine to be confidential? Answering this question will take us on a journey into low-level systems and high-level mathematics as we unpack this question in the context of the AWS Nitro System, the underlying virtualization platform that powers Amazon EC2. You will discover the low-level hardware and software that isolate virtual machines, our precise mathematical definition of confidentiality, and the methods we use to establish this crucial property for the AWS Nitro Isolation Engine. No background in virtualization systems or formal verification is expected.

Regulated industries must balance accuracy alongside their drive to innovate. Barr Moses, co-founder & CEO of Monte Carlo, will delve into this challenging topic with leaders from GE Healthcare. They’ll dissect some of the most difficult failure modes for agents & discuss how reliability practices have to evolve as teams scale agentic workflows in high-stakes environments. Discussed: how AI itself can be turned back on the problem of observing, resolving, and optimizing agents as well as building the guardrails, ownership models, & trust infrastructure that let a highly regulated organization move quickly without compromising on trust. We cover the OAuth grant flows that matter for agents, including authorization code for user-delegated access, client credentials for machine-to-machine calls, token exchange for on-behalf-of propagation, and Rich Authorization Requests (RAR) for fine-grained permission scoping. description: Your data lives in one platform. Your reports live in another. Your documents live somewhere else. Every time someone needs an answer, they spend time figuring out where to look before they can act. Decisions slow down. Teams duplicate work because they cannot find what already exists. New employees take months to become productive because institutional knowledge is trapped in systems they do not know how to navigate. Hear from a customer who solved this by giving their team a single AI assistant that connects across all their enterprise systems. Instead of training people on where to find information, they ask Amazon Quick and get answers grounded in their real business data, regardless of where it lives. Learn how they configured the integration, how their teams adopted it, and what changed about the speed and quality of decision-making across the organization.

title: One Context Layer, Every Surface: Enterprise Knowledge for Agents That Work Anywhere
description: Your AI agents are only as smart as the data they can reach. In most enterprises, that data is scattered across dozens of systems, siloed, ungoverned, and invisible to the agents that need it most. In this chalk talk, we architect a context layer from the ground up: connecting enterprise knowledge into a unified index, then enriching that foundation with a knowledge graph that maps organizational relationships, business rules, and domain context, giving agents permission-scoped, relationship-aware intelligence at runtime. Then we take that intelligence to where users work: browser, desktop, mobile, collaboration tools, and productivity suites. Each surface independently governed yet sharing one agent identity, one memory, and one set of guardrails. Bring your architecture. We'll whiteboard the end-to-end path together.

title: One Control Plane for Every Agent: Architecture Patterns for Cost, Risk, and ROI (sponsored by Boomi) (AIM262-S)
description: Every agent call carries cost, permission, and blast radius, and as agents multiply across tools, frameworks, and SaaS, the gaps compound: uncapped spend, unapproved permissions, no shared record. This session breaks down an AI infrastructure layer, running on AWS, that governs every model, agent, and system. A design-time layer publishes an approved catalog of agents, tools, and MCP servers; a runtime layer routes, meters, and enforces policy on every call before it executes. See how spend caps, in-tenant SLMs, and governed APIs turn cost into a controlled input, while one trace gives finance, security, and engineering a shared, audit-ready record. This presentation is brought to you by Boomi, an AWS Partner.

title: One Control to Rule Them All: Guardrail Automation for Every Identity (sponsored by Sonrai Security) (SEC226-S)
description: Separate guardrails for humans, machine identities, and AI agents get messy, and rewriting every IAM policy takes forever. SCPs deployed at scope are easy to write. What follows is not. Nobody can say what a policy will break, so it never deploys. Someone gets blocked and the fix becomes a two hour hunt. The tenth control behaves nothing like the first. New accounts inherit none of it. This lightning talk answers all four using only AWS Organizations, SCPs, and RCPs. See how usage data makes a default deny safe, how access returns in seconds, and how least privilege holds. This presentation is brought to you by Sonrai Security, an AWS Partner.

In this session, we’ll explore how Databricks on AWS brings these workloads together with Lakehouse//RT, Lakebase, and the Lakehouse Transactional Application Platform (LTAP). See how teams serve low-latency, high-concurrency analytics, power operational applications and AI agents with live transactional data, and analyze data where it is created—all from one platform and one governed copy of data. You’ll leave with practical architecture guidance for building reliable real-time and AI applications on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Databricks, an AWS Partner.

title: One query across every signal: centralized security investigations at scale
description: When an alert fires, your first question is "what else happened?" Answering it means correlating API calls, network flows, DNS queries, and application logs, often across dozens of accounts and regions. In this session, we show how security practitioners centralize every signal into a single queryable layer using Amazon CloudWatch unified data store, then investigate incidents with faceted queries that span all telemetry types at once. We walk through building always-on visibility dashboards, running cross-account investigations without switching tools, and using AI-assisted analytics to surface context before you need to go looking for it. You leave with a reference architecture for turning centralized logs into faster investigations and clearer security posture.

description: "AWS turns 20 this year. Starting fresh in 2026 means navigating hundreds of services with no clear map for which decisions are one-way doors. I'll share how we built a CFTC-regulated exchange and clearinghouse from the AWS Organizations up. The full security stack (Access Analyzer, Config, GuardDuty, Macie, Security Hub, and WAF) built in the right order from day one. We almost walked through the wrong door. A pre-launch architecture review with our engineers and AWS solution architects caught it in time. Here's how to have that conversation before it's too late."

title: On-Policy Distillation on HyperPod EKS: Train Smarter Small Models
description: Frontier models are powerful but costly to deploy. On-policy distillation, adopted by Qwen3, MiMo, and GLM-5, lets you compress a large teacher into a lean, domain-specialized student by training on the student's own rollouts with dense token-level feedback. Unlike Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards, it's cheaper, more stable, and doesn't require a verifier. In this code talk, walk through a working implementation on HyperPod EKS: orchestrate teacher inference and student training across GPU pools, manage the rollout buffer, and evaluate convergence.

description: You're running workloads across Lambda, EC2, and containers because no single service handled orchestration, always-on compute, and isolated execution. title: Powering Interactive Agents with Live Context (sponsored by Materialize) (DAT202-S)
description: How do you keep an agent's understanding of the world fresh enough for it to act on? Interactive agents need current context about the customers, orders, inventory, accounts, and other entities they reason about. But assembling that context from constantly changing operational systems is complex, forcing teams to choose between stale data, expensive recomputation, or complex pipelines. This talk will show how to build continuously updated context in SQL that is trustworthy enough for agents to rely upon. You'll learn how to transform operational data into agent-ready representations, keep attributes and relationships up to date as the underlying data changes, and propagate those changes to search indexes and embeddings when needed. Attend if you're deploying AI agents to production and want to give them fresher, more complete context and tighten their read-act-react loop. This presentation is brought to you by Materialize, an AWS Partner.

title: Powering your agentic AI experience with AWS streaming and messaging
description: Organizations are accelerating innovation with generative and agentic AI—and getting there depends on a handful of real-time data primitives: durable, high-throughput ingestion; stream processing and enrichment; low-latency, event-driven delivery; and a scalable place to land and serve data. In this session, learn how these primitives come together to power the real-time patterns behind agentic AI—and where each one fits: streaming into a real-time semantic layer for fresh retrieval context, event-driven agent invocation so agents act the instant something happens, and continuously sourcing agentic data stores with live data. We'll show how to satisfy each primitive—spanning multi-Region resilience, seamless migration off self-managed infrastructure, direct landing into open table formats and object storage, and simplified networking

description: Secure authentication of your humans and machines is a challenge every organization faces, especially if your proof of identity is not already in AWS. title: Prefill, decode, schedule: LLM inference without bubbles
description: Disaggregated inference separates prefill and decode onto distinct GPU pools, but creates new problems. Head-of-line blocking on prefill, stragglers on decode, and pipeline bubbles when phases switch. This session goes deep on how to solve them. We cover temporally-disaggregated pipeline parallelism to eliminate phase-switching bubbles, adaptive scheduling across heterogeneous instances, tensor vs. pipeline parallelism tradeoffs for latency and throughput, constrained decoding with context-sensitive grammars for structured output without sacrificing token throughput, and KV-cache parallelism for multi-million context serving.

You'll build data perimeter policies for real-life security scenarios and validate their effectiveness using an assessment tool. By the end, you'll have practical knowledge on how to help ensure only trusted identities access trusted resources from expected networks.

title: Processing PII without exposing it: KYC with Nitro Enclaves
description: Know Your Customer (KYC) pipelines must screen personally identifiable informaiton (PII) against sanctions lists and politically exposed person (PEP) databases while proving to regulators that data was never exposed to unauthorized systems. Traditional Spark pipelines may give executors access to decrypted PII, creating compliance risk. In this workshop, learn how to combine AWS Nitro Enclaves with Amazon EMR on EKS to process PII at scale without exposing plaintext to the compute layer. You'll configure KMS key policies with PCR0 attestation, deploy enclave sidecars as Kubernetes DaemonSets, and run Spark jobs where only screening decisions leave the enclave boundary.

title: Protect EKS and ECS workloads without chasing pod IPs

title: Quantum Error Correction - Progress, Hardware, and What's Next
description: Quantum computers have the potential to solve some of today's most challenging computational problems — but they suffer from significantly higher error rates than their classical counterparts. In this talk, we introduce quantum error correction (QEC) and compare the hardware requirements of leading QEC methods against the commercial roadmaps of quantum hardware companies. To ground the discussion, we begin with a brief revisit of classical error correction before walking through recent breakthroughs in quantum error correction. Attendees will leave with an informed perspective on where QEC stands today and the challenges that will define the field's progress in the coming years.

title: Quantum-proof your IoT fleet: migrate devices to Post-quantum cryptography OTA
description: NIST has announced post-quantum cryptography (PQC) standards and CNSA 2.0 requires quantum-resistant algorithms by 2027. IoT devices deployed today operate for 10–20 years, so they need to be quantum-resistant from day one. In this workshop, migrate a real ESP32-S3 SoC from classical TLS to post-quantum cryptography over the air with zero physical access required. Connect to AWS IoT Core, trigger an OTA delivering ML-KEM and ML-DSA with quantum-safe certificates from AWS Private CA, and watch your device reboot into PQC-secured MQTT. No embedded experience needed. You leave with the ESP32-S3 and open-source code to quantum-proof your fleet at scale.

Using SQS and Lambda, you configure queue types and concurrency controls, tune batching behavior, and observe how your consumer scales under each configuration. Each scenario forces a trade-off between throughput, ordering, isolation, and cost. You leave knowing which trade-offs to accept for your workload and why. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Ransomware resilience with Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP
description: Ransomware does not wait for a scheduled backup window, and neither should your defenses. In this chalk talk, learn how Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP's built in Autonomous Ransomware Protection uses machine learning to catch abnormal file activity and automatically create protective snapshots before damage spreads. We cover configuring detection policies, integrating alerts with AWS security services, locking down recovery points with SnapLock, and building automated response workflows. Bring your questions as we design a defense in depth strategy together, one that gets your file data back fast when an attack happens, not just one that flags it.

title: Ready before the surge - smart ELB capacity reservations
description: Your Load Balancer scales automatically for most traffic, and now you can prepare it for predictable spikes before they arrive. Product launches, flash sales, live events, and Monday-morning market opens deserve a load balancer that's ready instantly. Load Balancer Capacity Unit (LCU) Reservation pre-provisions a capacity floor so your infrastructure is never caught cold. In this session, we introduce new capacity management capabilities across ALB, NLB, and GLB that turn reservation planning into a data-driven workflow. Learn how to analyze historical patterns, set the right capacity floor, and release reservations with confidence.

title: Real-time agentic architecture on AWS: from batch to real-time AI
description: Batch jobs and cron schedules fail silently and delay agentic AI outcomes: a missed run, a stuck lock, or a partial write goes unnoticed, adding lag between the moment an event occurs and the moment an agent responds. This advanced deep dive rethinks the architecture—loosely coupled services that deploy and fail independently, wired through events. We show how shifting transactional and analytical workloads to real-time, event-driven patterns fuels responsive agentic AI on AWS.

AI coding agents break that assumption, and validation becomes the longest part of the cycle. Explore how RWX rebuilt the layer underneath continuous integration for agent driven work, including content based caching that skips work already proven unchanged, graph based task execution, a container runtime built for reuse, and a command line interface agents call directly rather than waiting on Git. title: Recover and prove your full stack without disrupting production
description: Meeting your recovery time and point objectives is non-negotiable. For your critical workloads, that means orchestrated, tier-aware recovery within minutes, with a plan you've actually tested. Most teams haven't, because testing often means disrupting production. So, the plan stays on the shelf and RTOs stay theoretical. In this session, see AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery replicate servers into low-cost staging and recover the full stack in the right order, in minutes, then rehearse the same failover without production noticing. Learn how to run non-disruptive recovery drills against your own environment and prove your RTOs before an incident does it for you.

title: Recovering AWS Graviton workloads with orchestrated DR
description: You moved to AWS Graviton for better price-performance, but is your disaster recovery keeping pace? A recovery that lands on the wrong architecture, or brings tiers up out of order, turns a routine failover into an outage. In this chalk talk, whiteboard with disaster recovery experts how AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery (DRS) now protects Graviton-based (arm64) Linux servers and recovers them onto Graviton instances, keeping the architecture intact end to end with nothing extra to configure. Then design a recovery plan that brings your application back tier by tier, in the right order, with wait times and critical-server gates. Bring your toughest arm64 and recovery-order questions, and leave with a DR design you can drill on Monday.

title: Red, green, re-architect: Test-driven infrastructure
description: AI can write your infrastructure in seconds — but did it build what you asked for? In this workshop, you'll apply test-driven development to AI-generated infrastructure. Describe your architecture in plain English, then use Kiro's spec-driven development to decompose it into discrete, testable behaviors. Kiro iterates through each one: writing a failing CDK assertion that encodes it (red), generating minimal infrastructure to pass it (green), then advancing to the next. Once green, refactor toward production readiness using cdk-nag rule packs to enforce Well-Architected practices. Leave with meaningful test coverage and a repeatable pattern for raising your organization's infrastructure coding standards. Bring your laptop to participate.

description: The best way to secure an AI agent is to think like the attacker. In this CTF-style session, you start with a production-realistic agent - AgentCore runtime, Bedrock Guardrails, Cognito authentication, and three MCP tools - and you systematically exploit it. Across 6 challenges, you poison trusted data sources, bypass prompt-level access control, jailbreak an authenticated session, compromise a third-party MCP server, exfiltrate data through authorized channels, and burn the inference budget. title: Reinvent cloud security with runtime and AI (sponsored by Upwind) (SEC215-S)
description: This session explores the evolution of cloud security and why traditional approaches fall short in the era of ephemeral compute and agentic AI. While legacy CloudSec relied on static scanning for visibility, today’s environments are dynamic, real-time, and increasingly autonomous, resulting in blind spots, excessive noise, and incomplete protection. We’ll examine how AI-driven and hybrid cloud architectures introduce new challenges across visibility, protection, and validation, from cross-provider gaps to real-time attack vectors and model vulnerabilities. To address this, Cloud and AI security must move beyond static analysis to a unified, runtime-driven approach. By continuously monitoring activity across the environment and embedding security throughout the SDLC, including production, organizations gain real-time context, better prioritization, and proactive threat mitigation. This presentation is brought to you by Upwind, an AWS Partner.

title: Reliable data processing with AWS serverless services
description: In this chalk talk, learn how to optimize your serverless data processing workflows at scale. We cover AWS Step Functions Distributed Map for massive parallel batch processing and AWS Lambda durable functions for durable execution workflows. See how to combine these with Lambda event source mappings for stream and queue processing. We discuss cost optimization strategies and when to choose each approach for your data workload.

title: Renaissance Dad: building an agentic learning app for my 9-year-old with Kiro
description: Werner Vogels told us to become Renaissance Developers — curious polymaths who blend disciplines and own what they build. I took it literally: as a dad, I used Kiro and agentic AI to build a learning app that helps my 9-year-old practice math and school lessons. In this session, I'll share the full architecture: an OCR agent that imports exercises from photos of school notebooks, an adaptive agent that personalizes difficulty, and a coaching agent that guides instead of correcting. We'll deep-dive into multi-agent orchestration patterns, vision model integration, spec-driven development with Kiro, and the guardrails required when your end user is a child. Attendees will leave with reusable agentic patterns applicable far beyond education.

title: Replacing eligibility rules engines with Neurosymbolic AI in HHS
description: State HHS agencies spend hundreds of millions maintaining eligibility rules engines built on Drools or proprietary tooling. These systems are brittle, expensive, and impossible to audit. No hallucinations. Provable correctness. We walk through the architecture, show a working prototype processing SNAP and Medicaid policy, discuss pricing at scale, and share early results from state engagements.

title: Resilient by design: Simplifying last-mile connectivity with AWS
description: Establishing resilient private connectivity from data centers and branch offices to AWS has traditionally required weeks of partner coordination, physical cross-connects, and manual resilience configurations. Yet true resilience demands more than provisioning a second connection. In this chalk talk, we will whiteboard how AWS Direct Connect and AWS Interconnect each address location diversity, device diversity, BGP routing policy, and failover validation. Compare dedicated links with full routing control to fully managed connections with built-in redundancy, explore integration with AWS Transit Gateway and AWS Cloud WAN, and evaluate maximum versus high resiliency models. Bring your hybrid connectivity challenges.

title: Resilient Cloud Ops: From IaC to Fault Injection
description: Production infrastructure needs two guarantees: repeatable deployment and proven resilience. In this bootcamp, use AWS CDK and CloudFormation to define and provision cloud resources as code, eliminating manual configuration drift. Then validate your architecture under stress. Troubleshoot VPC connectivity using flow logs, inject controlled faults with AWS Fault Injection Service, and confirm your infrastructure recovers gracefully. Deploy it right, then prove it holds.

title: Resilient VLM Training at Scale on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
description: Training vision-language models at scale fails in predictable ways — node crashes mid-epoch, checkpoints corrupt, and GPU clusters sit idle during recovery. In this hands-on workshop, build resilient VLM training pipelines on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod that survive real-world failures. Configure automatic health monitoring and node replacement, implement fault-tolerant checkpointing strategies, and design distributed training topologies that resume without losing progress. Using open-source frameworks on multi-node GPU clusters, you'll train a VLM end-to-end while simulating and recovering from infrastructure failures. Leave with battle-tested patterns for keeping large-scale training runs alive.

description: Incident investigation on Amazon ECS means correlating signals across task logs, service events, deployment history, and CloudWatch metrics - scattered data that takes hours to piece together. In this builders session, deploy AWS DevOps Agent against an ECS workload and experience autonomous incident response. The agent discovers your service topology, receives CloudWatch alarms, investigates autonomously by testing hypotheses against telemetry data, and delivers root cause analysis with specific remediation steps. Practice the full workflow from alarm to resolution without manually searching a single dashboard. Bring your laptop to build alongside an AWS expert.
