title: Responsible AI Enablement: Balancing Innovation, Governance and Control (sponsored by Island) (AIM135-S)
description: Most organizations are currently stuck between two worlds: the urgent need to adopt AI to remain competitive, & the critical mandate to protect corporate data & reputation. AI is evolving faster than any tool in IT history, and faster than any organization can keep up with. The temptation to simply block access to AI is strong, but just saying "No" means ceding the advantage to those able to say "Yes!". The 3 Pillars of a "Secure Yes": Visibility: Knowing what AI is being used across the org. Accountability: Defining who owns the data & the output. Resilience: Building frameworks that adapt as regulations change. In this session, we will outline the framework for secure AI adoption. We will move past the hype to discuss how leaders can build visibility, maintain accountability, and foster a culture of responsible innovation. This presentation is brought to you by Island, an AWS Partner.
location: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: Rethinking Agentic Security: How Cyera Scaled AI Securely in Days (sponsored by Cyera) (AIM387-S)
description: As AI shifts from assistive systems to autonomous agents, data becomes the control surface. Agents need a goldilocks balance of data, identity, and process access: enough to be effective, too much and you end up on Twitter. Cyera solved this internally, reaching 88% weekly AI usage across engineering and non-engineering teams in 17 days. Adoption was not the hard part. The wiring was. How do you govern access and give builders a permit path so they ship instead of wait? Join us for what we learned, and what it means on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by Cyera, an AWS Partner.
location: Venetian | Level 2 | Hall B | Expo | Global Impact Theater

title: Rethinking the AWS SDK for Python: Async, streaming, and more
description: If you've ever wrapped boto3 in asyncio, juggled thread pools for concurrent AWS calls, or wished for proper streaming support, this session is for you. With the new AWS SDK for Python, async is native, concurrent calls no longer require thread-pool workarounds, and bidirectional streaming enables use cases like live transcription and speech-to-speech that go beyond what's available in boto3 today. Follow along as we put those capabilities to work with clean concurrent calls, Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Transcribe streaming, and a practical path to migrating your own code to the new SDK.

title: Rethinking the boundary between messaging and streaming
description: Modern event-driven architectures still separate cleanly into "queues" and "streams," but real workloads no longer do. Replay, request-response, ordering, and high throughput increasingly appear across both patterns, making the wrong service choice costly to unwind. This session explores the architectural spectrum across messaging and streaming systems, drawing on services such as Amazon SQS, Amazon EventBridge, and Amazon MSK. Through a real CQRS architecture, we build a practical decision framework for when to choose messaging, streaming, or a hybrid approach, and which trade-offs matter most.

title: Rethink release management for the agentic coding era
description: GitOps was designed for human-speed change. Agentic coding tools now generate pull requests faster than any team can review and safely release. Your release process is the new bottleneck. In this code talk, we'll live-code a GitOps release workflow where AWS DevOps Agent acts as an intelligent release manager, validating the results through a release pipeline at every promotion gate. Instead of manual approvals, DevOps Agent uses production intelligence (runtime dependencies, service health, deployment risk) to make real-time go/no-go decisions. Learn how to wire DevOps Agent into your GitOps reconciliation loop so releases match the velocity of agentic code generation without sacrificing safety.

title: Right Compute, right time, right price: A decision framework for HPC and AI at scale
description: Large-scale HPC and AI workloads share the same hard problem: getting the right compute, at the right time, at the right price. In this chalk talk, we cover the architecture and provisioning decisions that matter when you move beyond a single instance. Architecture side: cluster design for distributed AI training and tightly coupled HPC simulation, networking trade-offs and where CPUs (x86, Graviton) fit alongside GPUs in production pipelines. Provisioning side: Capacity Blocks for predictable GPU bursts, On-Demand Capacity Reservations for sustained workloads, Spot for fault-tolerant jobs, and Savings Plans for steady-state fleets. We share real customer examples leveraging Amazon EC2 across HPC and AI/ML. Bring your hardest capacity and cost questions.

description: Financial institutions deploy dozens of models and manual workflows that struggle to work together at scale. Machine learning excels at fast, explainable decisions while agentic AI orchestrates multi-step workflows with reasoning and adaptability. Real value is knowing when to use each and combining them into one system. In this chalk talk, we present a decision framework and demonstrate an architecture where machine learning models score and detect while agents reason, act, and close the loop while delivering the auditability regulators require. We walk through a Know Your Customer (KYC) example, then open the floor. Bring your use case.

title: Right workload on the right cloud - multicloud workload placement
description: You operate a multicloud organization, and every new workload raises the same challenge: which cloud should this workload run on? Too often the answer comes down to habit, existing vendor relationships, or whoever argues loudest, and workloads end up somewhere that adds complexity, risk, or complicates compliance. In this session you will learn how to approach multicloud workload placement so that the decisions you make are explainable, repeatable and auditable.

title: Ring's Security Evolution: From Doorbell to Enterprise Platform (sponsored by Ring LLC) (SEC107-S)
description: Ring started with a simple mission: make neighborhoods safer with a video doorbell. That mission has scaled — from 100M+ residential cameras to SMB storefronts and jobsites with mobile security towers, to an AI-powered Appstore unlocking entirely new use cases across elder care, workforce analytics, and beyond. Now, Ring is making its boldest leap yet: a cloud-native enterprise platform built on AWS, combining video management, intelligent alerting, third-party camera ingestion, and access control. description: Discover why Rivian chose AWS Outposts to support mission-critical manufacturing applications that produce vehicles at its Normal, Illinois, plant. Explore how Rivian architected highly redundant infrastructure across multiple Outposts racks, using fast Amazon EC2 provisioning and scaling to meet production line demands. This session covers Multi-Availability Zone deployment for high availability, Amazon RDS read replicas across racks for database resilience, and AWS Unified Operations for proactive observability across its hybrid environment. Learn how Rivian plans to scale this model into its 9-million-square-foot mega factory in Georgia.

title: Route, cache and batch: a multi-model decision framework on Bedrock
description: Treating every request the same is what makes inference expensive at scale, and most of that cost is repeat work you already paid for. This chalk talk whiteboards how prompt caching on Amazon Bedrock eliminates redundant computation across system prompts, shared context, and multi-turn conversations, then shows where Intelligent Prompt Routing and batch inference extend the savings further. We walk through cache-hit economics, how to structure prompts for maximum reuse, and when routing or batching is the better lever. Bring your traffic patterns and questions, and leave with a caching-first cost strategy tuned to your workloads.

title: Route or escalate: Confidence boundaries in multi-domain AI agents
description: Building a GenAI system that answers questions across technology domains is straightforward — until the model doesn't know the answer and doesn't say so. For builders designing multi-agent or RAG-based systems, this session presents the confidence-gated routing architecture behind AWS Specialist Agent: classifying every query into high-confidence retrieval, low-confidence escalation to a human specialist, or cross-domain composition. We cover why flat vector retrieval fails multi-domain queries, the trade-offs of graph-based knowledge ontology, and the evaluations framework measuring confidence calibration. Walk away with a routing pattern you can apply any time your AI system must self-report uncertainty rather than hallucinate with authority.

description: Amazon Braket offers access to the latest trapped-ion quantum hardware alongside advanced error mitigation techniques, unlocking the largest, highest-fidelity quantum workloads on the platform. title: SaaS Agents Anywhere
description: Customers make deliberate choices about where their workloads run. For SaaS vendors delivering agentic products, that means the runtime has to meet the workload where it is, not the other way around. This chalk talk teaches the everywhere agent pattern for SaaS: keep the control plane on AWS, run the agent runtime and data-plane execution wherever the customer's data lives. Learn three decisions: which destinations to support and when (multi-cloud, on-prem, or both), how to run agent runtimes outside AWS without rewriting your control plane (packaging, model backend selection, dependency portability), and how to manage identity, observability, and lifecycle across environments you don't own. Leave with the decision framework for shipping SaaS agents anywhere the customer's data lives.

title: SaaS Agents Anywhere: building distributed agentic deployments
description: SaaS vendors deploy agents across a spectrum: fully provider-hosted, fully tenant-controlled, and hybrid models in between. In this workshop, build a distributed agentic deployment on AWS spanning your accounts and a tenant's, then exercise the three concerns that surface everywhere on the spectrum: lifecycle management of agents you can't directly see, observability across account boundaries, and reliability when the agent runs somewhere you don't operate. Leave with a working reference deployment you can adapt to your own tenancy model.

title: Securing AI Agents on AgentCore
description: A customer runs a support agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that reaches destinations nobody reviewed and takes requests from any caller. In this SimuLearn session, you work the case as their security expert. Behind Amazon API Gateway, AWS WAF Bot Control labels each script and AI crawler, and you write the rule that refuses them with a 403 that names the reason. On the way out, AWS Network Firewall tags every destination by content category. You watch in alert mode, then reject AI and search categories while permitted sites still load. You leave knowing how to classify, then control, what enters and leaves an agent.
location: Caesars Palace | Emperors Level | Palace Ballroom II

title: Securing AI and Autonomous Agents: Protecting the Lifecycle Across Any Platform (sponsored by Fortinet) (AIM2203-S)
description: AI agents are actively running code, accessing databases, and making critical business decisions across every industry. But as these systems gain independence, they also introduce complex security risks throughout their lifecycle. Are you ready to protect a system that learns and acts on its own as your organization embarks on the AI journey? Join our panel of top AI and cybersecurity experts as they break down the end-to-end security of AI systems and agentic applications. We will explore real-world customer challenges and share practical strategies to safeguard autonomous agents across cloud and on-premises environments. This presentation is brought to you by Fortinet, an AWS Partner.
location: MGM Grand | Level 3 | Chairman's 363 | Content Hub | White Theater

title: Securing AI coding agents: defense in depth across the development lifecycle
description: AI coding agents optimise for task completion, not security, generating code faster than humans can review. This chalk talk presents a defence-in-depth framework spanning five phases - pre-generation, authoring, PR, pipeline, and deployment - with three lines of defence at each: deterministic controls, AI screening, and human judgment. We cover author-time techniques (steering, specs, scoped MCP, hooks) and build-time gates (SAST, SCA, IaC scanning, AI-assisted review, approval) using Kiro, AWS Security Agent, and CodePipeline. Leave with a layered model you can apply on Monday.

title: Securing applications at machine speed in the frontier model era
description: Frontier AI models discover code vulnerabilities in minutes. Security teams still take days or weeks to validate, prioritize, and fix them. AWS Continuum closes that gap with one continuous workflow: discover risks in your code, prioritize by real exploitability, validate in a sandbox with reproduction steps, and remediate at machine speed within guardrails you define. In this session, we walk through how Continuum operates end-to-end: building a security context graph from your infrastructure, identity, and code to determine what is reachable, confirming exploitability through sandboxed proof-of-concept, and generating validated fixes. You see graduated trust in action, starting with human approval and promoting to autonomous remediation as confidence builds. You leave understanding how to move from manual triage to continuous discovery, validation, and remediation.
location: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Securing Multi-Agent Systems
description: Multi-agent systems create a larger attack surface than single-agent deployments: prompt injections that propagate across agent boundaries, identity spoofing, tool-chain escalation, and data exfiltration through natural-language covert channels. In this chalk talk, we threat-model this risk using the OWASP Agentic AI Top 10, then whiteboard defense-in-depth patterns for validating inter-agent messages, enforcing least-privilege orchestration, and detecting anomalous behavior before it cascades. Leave with a set of recommendations and architectures that demonstrate how to layer security controls in a multi-agent system.

title: Securing OpenClaw deployments on AWS
description: In this session, we introduce the OpenClaw architecture, compare the major variants and their security posture differences, and then map the threat landscape for AWS-hosted deployments. Drawing on years of experience helping customers deploy, we cover the infrastructure and runtime threat landscape. You will leave with a reference architecture that applies defense-in-depth principles to such OpenClaw deployments on AWS, minimizing risk without sacrificing capability.

title: Securing software and AI supply chains with Network Firewall at Coupang
description: Coupang, South Korea's largest e-commerce platform, runs millions of daily transactions on AWS. At that volume, each open source library, container base image, and AI model weight pulled from the internet is a supply chain risk. This session goes deep on the AWS Network Firewall architecture and its newer capabilities, including centralized management and container-aware egress inspection. Coupang shows how it built egress control that scales automatically across a container-first fleet, automates allowlist management, and limits exposure to rogue AI dependencies and dynamic payloads without slowing developers down.

title: Securing the AI-Native Cloud (sponsored by Upwind) (SEC222-S)
description: In this session, we will demonstrate how AI is redefining cloud security by moving beyond static posture management to real-time, context-aware protection. The session will showcase how organizations can gain continuous visibility across their environments and respond to threats as they emerge. Attendees will see how AI-driven analysis of runtime behavior enables faster detection of anomalies, prioritization of real risks, and automated response across dynamic, multi-cloud infrastructures. The session will highlight how security teams can reduce noise, strengthen security processes, and proactively respond to threats before they escalate. This presentation is brought to you by Upwind, an AWS Partner.

title: Securing the Bedrock: A Strong API Foundation for AI Innovation (sponsored by Kong) (AIM252-S)
description: AI moves fast until it hits production. Then agents that looked solid in a POC start making calls they shouldn't, hammering the vector database, or failing quietly under load, because the API layer underneath wasn't built for it. This session covers what a strong API foundation does for AI at scale: fine-grained authorization keeps context retrieval inside its data privacy boundaries, touching only what it's permitted to touch; rate limiting protects vector databases from resource exhaustion; edge caching cuts query latency without extra engineering; and circuit breaking plus canary deployments let teams ship changes without compromising security or compliance. You'll leave with architectural blueprints and real enterprise examples showing how the right API foundation turns governance from a blocker into what lets AI teams move faster. Presented by Kong an AWS Partner, alongside FanDuel. This presentation is brought to you by Kong, an AWS Partner.

title: Securing the Enterprise in the Age of AI Agents: From Zero Trust to Agentic Security (sponsored by Zscaler) (AIM292-S)
description: AI isn’t just another workload—it’s introducing agents that act, connect, and make decisions at machine speed. This session reframes Zero Trust for an agent-driven world: how to govern agent-to-agent communication, constrain access to sensitive data, and reduce risk without slowing the business. This presentation is brought to you by Zscaler, an AWS Partner.
location: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Blue Theater

title: Securing your AI-accelerated software supply chain with AWS Well-Architected
description: Modern software depends on open-source packages from npm, PyPI, and Maven. AI assistants pull them into your codebase faster than ever, sometimes suggesting packages that don’t exist or shouldn’t be trusted. Attackers exploit this through “slopsquatting.” Supply chain incidents show registries targeted via credential compromise, typosquatting, and token farming at scale. This workshop builds a layered defense aligned to the AWS Well-Architected Security Pillar. You replace long-lived credentials with OIDC, sign artifacts with AWS Signer, and govern dependencies with CodeArtifact package groups. You scan AI-generated and human-written code with Amazon Inspector, then detect threats with GuardDuty and Security Hub. You leave with a defense-in-depth blueprint that scales with AI-accelerated development across your environment.

title: Security leverage at AI velocity: the operating model shift
description: The speed AI gives your developers is also available to attackers, so AI investment is now a security decision as much as an engineering one. This session covers three changes to how security teams work when engineers pair with frontier agents. Agents carry application context across design, code, and pen testing, so security coverage keeps pace with development. When an agent builds a working proof of exploit for a finding, or shows that an existing control already blocks it, the security team no longer has to argue over whether the finding is real, and the false-positive queue shrinks. Agentic development environments also let you put preventive controls on what agents generate. We cover how to adopt these practices and which signals show they're working.
location: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | White Theater

title: Security → Zero-Trust Identity & Data Protection in the Agentic Era
description: Security reviews stall AI rollouts more than any capability gap, and agentic AI raises the bar. This chalk talk goes past "is it secure?" to the architecture that gets a CISO to yes. We'll whiteboard the full identity path: SSO through providers like Okta and Ping, with end-user identity propagated to the data so authorization is enforced per user, in real time, across 1P AWS and 3P sources. Then we extend that trust to agents: agent identity, deterministic policy checks on every tool call, and data protection—Purview DLP, default guardrails, deny-by-default, full SIEM auditability.
location: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Neopolitan I

title: See the routes change: Live BGP with AWS Direct Connect
description: AWS Direct Connect can feel like a mystery beneath the surface, and many customers never get hands-on access. In this show and tell, we change that. Starting from a live connection and on-premises router, watch a Direct Connect maintenance unfold in real-time from both sides of the BGP session. See how AWS signals maintenance ahead of time through AS path prepending, graceful shutdown, and how traffic shifts to the backup path before any route is withdrawn. Whether you run 1G or hundreds of 100G ports, leave with the policy and checklist to get through your next maintenance without a page.

Add attribution by IAM principal and cost-allocation tags, then assemble a dashboard that maps spend to teams, workloads, and models while accounting for each source's freshness and granularity. Turn that visibility into action: match steady workloads to Reserved Tier, choose models for price-performance, and set budgets and alerts. Leave with working code and a repeatable, finance-ready cost view.

title: Select and launch the right EC2 instance for your workload and budget
description: With hundreds of EC2 instance types spanning compute, memory, storage, and accelerator families, choosing the right one can be overwhelming. In this session, learn a practical framework for matching your workload characteristics—CPU, memory, network, and storage requirements—to the optimal instance type and size. We cover cost-performance tradeoffs across On-Demand, Spot, and Savings Plans, share real-world selection patterns for common workloads, and demo tools that simplify decision-making. Leave with a repeatable process to right-size from day one.

title: Self-healing data pipelines with agentic AI and Apache Iceberg
description: Join this session to experience the power of agentic AI and Apache Iceberg coming together on AWS to build a self-correcting data pipeline. We will dive in to an agentic architecture for an Iceberg-based data pipeline - governed end-to-end through AWS Glue Data Catalog - where critical telemetry signals such as data loss, schema drift, cost spikes are not only detected and diagnosed but also remediated and verified - all in real time. Attendees will walk away with a blueprint on how to unify DataOps, MLOps, and FinOps for their data pipelines, with Glue Data Catalog as the metadata backbone tying governance, lineage, and discovery together across the pipeline.

title: Self-Healing Enterprise-Wipro & AWS Moving from System of Record to System of Action (sponsored by Wipro) (BIZ204-S)
description: For decades, enterprises have invested in technologies that digitize, automate and optimize work. Yet when disruptions occur, decisions still depend on emails, escalations, meetings and manual coordination across teams. The next phase of enterprise transformation is about creating enterprises that can sense change, assess impact, coordinate responses and drive outcomes at speed. Wipro and AWS demonstrate how intelligent agents, enterprise systems and human expertise come together to create a Self-Healing Enterprise, one that can proactively identify issues, orchestrate actions across functions and continuously adapt while keeping humans accountable for critical business decisions. Through a realistic business disruption scenario, see how organizations can evolve beyond visibility and automation towards systems of action that improve resilience, responsiveness and operational efficiency. This presentation is brought to you by Wipro, an AWS Partner.

title: Self-managed agentic AI at the hybrid edge with AWS Outposts and AWS Local Zones
description: As organizations use agentic AI to automate complex infrastructure operations, many face constraints around data residency, low latency, and security that prevent reliance on cloud-hosted AI services alone. This session explores how customers deploy self-managed agentic AI at the hybrid edge to meet these requirements while unlocking autonomous operations. Learn how to provision, configure, and optimize AI agents across customer environments spanning AWS Outposts and AWS Local Zones. Attendees learn how to architect and operate AI agents that run locally, satisfying data sovereignty, latency, and security mandates while delivering intelligent, autonomous infrastructure management across hybrid environments.

title: Self-verifiable watermarks: defending AI provenance against forgery
description: As organizations deploy generative AI at scale, watermarking has become the critical trust layer for establishing content provenance, meeting emerging regulatory requirements, and protecting brand integrity. But what if an adversary could stamp a fake watermark onto any image and frame your service? We show a diffusion-based forgery attack bypasses current defenses with just 1,000 samples. To close this gap, we introduce a self-verifiable message mechanism—SeedBind and ContentBind—that transforms verification into a structural consistency check, reducing forged bit accuracy to near-random without modifying the underlying watermarking pipeline. Discover how to harden AI provenance at scale.

title: Sell to AI agents through AWS Marketplace
description: Today, buyers are using autonomous AI agents for discovery and digital purchases on their behalf. AWS Marketplace enables buyers' agents to discover partner solutions, transact securely, and meet their enterprise governance controls. As a seller in AWS Marketplace, learn how to sell products that support agentic discovery and procurement to position your offerings for this new frontier.

title: Sell to the AI Buyer, Scale Revenue, and Build Long-Term Value
description: The buying journey is shifting to AI agents and assistants that evaluate and procure software autonomously. If your solution isn't readable and transactable by a machine, you're invisible to a growing share of the market. This session shows AWS Partners how to show up for the AI buyer, from listing optimization to working alongside other agents, and how a growth toolkit (trials, bundling, demand generation) turns visibility into compounding revenue. Walk away with an implementation path that covers day-one discoverability through long-term governance.

title: Serverless at 1M RPS: Lambda, DynamoDB & SQS Scaling Lessons
description: We push Lambda, DynamoDB, and SQS to one million requests per second and share what breaks. Learn partition-aware DynamoDB design for extreme write throughput, Lambda concurrency shaping to prevent downstream crush, SQS as a backpressure buffer with adaptive batching, and retry amplification math that turns a blip into a cascade. We present real numbers: cold start budgets at scale, the exact crossover point where serverless cost exceeds containers, and the operational trade-offs at each threshold.

title: Serverless compute built for the web
description: Modern web applications demand fast iteration, automatic scaling, and minimal operational overhead. In this session, see how to build full-stack web applications entirely on AWS serverless services, from API endpoints and business logic to data persistence and authentication. We cover architectural patterns for handling HTTP routing, server-side rendering, static assets, and real-time features without managing servers, and how serverless simplifies common web framework patterns while delivering built-in high availability and pay-per-use economics. Whether you're migrating an existing web app or starting from scratch, you'll leave with practical blueprints for production-ready serverless web development.

title: Serverless developers in the agentic era: What changes, what doesn't
description: Serverless architectures that worked well for API backends and event processing now have a new type of consumer: AI agents that call your functions as tools, generate events, and write code that deploys alongside yours. In this session, we cover what actually changes: function design patterns for agent consumption, orchestration choices for non-deterministic workflows, cost governance when an agent loop calls 200 functions in a single reasoning chain, and observability that tracks token spend alongside invocation metrics. We also cover what doesn't change, and where existing Serverless patterns hold up without modification.
location: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Purple Theater

title: Serverless Java in 2026
description: Java on Lambda used to mean cold start anxiety and compromised JIT performance. Not anymore. SnapStart and GraalVM native AOT deliver sub-second startup, and Lambda Managed Instances give steady-state JVM workloads full JIT optimization at EC2 economics. In this chalk talk, we go beyond cold starts: discuss refactoring patterns for moving Java monoliths to serverless, framework choices that work well on Lambda (and ones that don't), and how AI-assisted tools identify decomposition boundaries and generate Lambda handlers from existing service classes. Bring your Java architecture.

description: The next major leap in AI is predicting and interacting with the physical world. World models bridge digital reasoning with real-world execution, introducing new infrastructure demands for video generation, robotics, and gaming workloads at scale. We'll explore the emerging architecture of world models and why AWS Trainium, purpose-built for better price-performance, is well suited to serve them. Learn how native PyTorch support with torch.compile fuses operations into optimized device graphs, and how NKI custom kernels accelerate critical operators like attention. description: Every organization is building their AI architecture in real-time: deciding which agents to use, which data sources to connect them to, and figuring how to get teams to collaborate across it all. These different layers have been arranged over many years of procuring tools, but can sometimes feel like a jumbled mess in the AI era. This session offers a practical way to reexamine your tech architecture. We'll cover four patterns that recur across organizations as they try to structure their business for the AI era, plus pitfalls to avoid to ensure your tech stack is optimized for AI. We'll break down when to choose each service based on access patterns, performance, and cost. You'll see how real teams run stateful microservices using EFS on ECS/EKS, leverage FSx for high-performance file system workloads on Fargate, and unlock POSIX capabilities to S3 object data for analytics and AI workloads with S3 Files.

description: Your agents are reviewing PRs, shipping code, and answering messages. They communicate on your behalf, surfacing every weak relationship in your org. Security teams have historically operated at a remove: by org chart, tooling, and reputation. That distance becomes a liability when agents reduce the time between decision and consequence. This session is about building a security function whose core output is shared judgment with the engineers it serves.

description: Kiro agents execute code, invoke models, and interact with external services on behalf of developers. We built a centralized governance system backed by Dogwood/Cedar that compiles admin-authored policies into governance documents enforced across every client (IDE, CLI, Web,Mobile) and server-side services. The system separates governance from configuration, uses deny-wins semantics with fail-closed enforcement, and scopes rules by hierarchies. Learn how we use Kiro itself to author and analyze governance policies to make enterprise controls human-friendly and manageable.

title: Simplify Data Analytics operations with AI-powered Apache Spark agents on AWS
description: Running analytics workloads at scale carries a hidden operational tax: teams commonly lose significant engineering time to debugging failures, leave performance and cost improvements on the table, and spend months on each version upgrade. In this talk, we walk through a family of AI-powered agents for AWS Glue, Amazon EMR, and Amazon Athena. The Spark Troubleshooting Agent finds the root cause of a failure and recommends the code or config fix - cutting debugging time from hours to minutes. The Spark Upgrade Agent plans an upgrade, transforms the code, and validates both runtime and data quality - turning months into hours. We share what worked in production for both agents - the design choices, failure modes, and validation strategies that made them reliable - and distill lessons that generalize to any team applying LLMs to complex infrastructure.

description: As organizations unify data across Amazon S3 data lakes, S3 Tables, and Amazon Redshift using the open data lakehouse architecture, securing access at scale becomes critical. description: Getting the most out of AWS often means manually setting up the same optimizations, integrations, and best-practice patterns across your applications. In this chalk talk, we explore emerging approaches for running AWS-authored logic in isolated, secure-by-default environments alongside your applications, implementing common patterns on your behalf and simplifying how you consume AWS services. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard how to bring every instance under one operational model with AWS Systems Manager, no matter where it runs, and then get metrics and logs from all of them into Amazon CloudWatch. We work through the tradeoffs and patterns that hold at scale. Leave able to run and observe your whole fleet as one.

title: SQL Server to Amazon RDS: lessons from Xero's 900 database migration
description: What does it take to migrate the databases behind 5 million small businesses without anyone noticing? Xero, the global cloud accounting platform, moved 900 SQL Server databases to Amazon RDS for SQL Server with near-zero downtime. In this session, Xero shares how the team orchestrated cutovers, approached schema migration, and used managed patching, automated backups, and capacity planning in Amazon RDS to return engineering time to product development. The session covers the migration planning and decision points most relevant to engineering teams running large SQL Server fleets on aging self-managed infrastructure.

title: State of the art Fairness and Admission Control
description: Preventing long outages, meta-stable events, thundering herds, Denial of Service Attacks, resource or concurrency starvation, or noisy neighbor issues all depend on fairness and admission control. We’ll do a deep, interactive dive into practical techniques that prevent or mitigate real-world issues. We’ll get into details of back-pressure, PID control loops, shuffle sharding, floodgates, and other novel techniques that we’ve developed at AWS, and we’ll cover common mistakes that we see in the industry.

Every resource stays within policy guardrails before it reaches production. Learn how integrating AI agents into the DevOps lifecycle accelerates delivery while maintaining governance and security across the enterprise.

description: Many AI programs start with a model, a prompt, and a narrow workflow. title: Stop Rolling Back AI Agents: Production Patterns That Work
description: The demo shipped. The agent went live. Then someone pulled it back. 74% of organizations that have deployed an AI agent have rolled it back or shut it down, and the rate rises to 81% among those reporting fully mature guardrails. Getting agents into production got easier. Keeping them there without hurting customers did not. We'll walk through the failure patterns behind rollbacks: agents that fail silently, prompts treated as safety boundaries, and monitoring blind to non-deterministic failures. You'll leave with the patterns that prevent them: infrastructure-level guardrails, blast radius containment, and observability built for probabilistic systems.
location: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Roman I

title: Stop the bleed: control and optimize agent costs on AgentCore
description: Your agent cost $0.02 per session in testing. In production it's $0.14 and climbing. Token consumption grows unpredictably as agents retry, loop, and fan out across tools, and most teams have no visibility into where the money goes. This chalk talk breaks down where agent costs actually hide and how to control them on AgentCore: per-session budgets that kill runaway loops, model routing that drops to cheaper models for simple subtasks, cost attribution at the team and workload level, prompt caching strategies, and how to measure the tradeoff between cost and quality with evaluations.

See how deeper integration with other AWS security services, expanded DNS threat detection, wider visibility, and a growing partner ecosystem come together to strengthen your first line of defense. Whether you run a single VPC or a global network across AWS and hybrid networks, you'll leave with a clear picture of how DNS security for egress traffic is advancing and how to put it to work.

description: When your business delivers cloud services to your customers, how you map tenants to storage is one of the earliest architectural choices, and it shapes everything that follows: onboarding automation, billing boundaries, isolation guarantees, and how accounts, users, and data relate to each tenant. Your workload mix adds another dimension, because data types using object, file, or block storage drive the handling of tenancy differently. In this chalk talk, we walk through silo, bridge, and pool deployment models, examining how workload profile, tenant count, and business requirements drive the choice. description: Peak SSD IOPS and throughput dominate benchmarks, but production workloads tell a different story. We'll walk through how workload profiles map to different performance dimensions (throughput vs. IOPS vs. latency consistency), how real-world write mixes reveal true storage performance, and how emerging AI workloads are creating demand for an entirely new storage performance profile.

title: Surviving the drop: Build a flash-sale control plane with CloudFront
description: Product drops, ticket on-sales, and viral promotions can spike traffic 50x in seconds. Origin infrastructure is the wrong place to absorb it. In this workshop, build a complete launch-day control plane using Amazon CloudFront Functions and CloudFront KeyValueStore. Implement a launch gate with VIP early access, a percentage-based throttle that dials traffic to your purchase origin in real time, sticky A/B testing for product pages, and a global kill switch - all controlled by KeyValueStore updates that propagate worldwide in seconds, with zero deployments and zero origin changes. Along the way, use edge location metadata for geo-staggered launches and trace every gate decision with CloudFront Functions access logging. Leave with patterns you can apply to any high-demand launch event. Attendees must bring a laptop.

title: Switch models without disrupting customers on Amazon Bedrock
description: Your application is working in production, and then a newer model arrives with better benchmarks or lower cost. You need to decide whether moving is worth the risk. A switch can change outputs, break prompts, raise costs, and create weeks of retesting. This session shows how to reduce that disruption on Amazon Bedrock. Test candidate models against your own use cases, compare quality, latency, and cost, and update prompts without rewriting them by hand. See how Bedrock Evaluations and Advanced Prompt Optimization help you measure the impact before rollout. Leave with a practical plan for switching models without disrupting customers.

title: Tackling a $30M fraud crisis with ML: California Community Colleges
description: The California Community Colleges, the largest higher education system in the U.S. serving 1 in 4 community college students nationally. Since 2024, it has faced a fraud crisis targeting over $30M, as stolen-identity breaches and generative AI made ghost-student attempts cheaper and harder to catch. Machine learning (ML) on Amazon SageMaker now screens applicants centrally, driving a 64% decrease in attempted fraud year over year. Campus-level detection tools add a second layer, catching 2x more fraudulent applications than human review alone. This session covers the ML architecture, how it integrates across 116 campuses, and how reclaimed seats and aid dollars directly improved access for legitimate students.

description: AI agents can already search, reason, and call tools. What changes when they can spend money, too? This talk explores the shift from human checkout to machine-native commerce, where payments become part of an agent's reasoning loop. We will look at how agents can discover and purchase products today, then explore Stripe’s Machine Payments Protocol and a future where agents autonomously pay for APIs, compute, data, and other capabilities needed to complete a task. When software becomes the buyer, developers may need to rethink not only checkout, but also how software itself is discovered, priced, and consumed. This presentation is brought to you by Stripe, an AWS Partner.

title: Teaching Quick to Remember and Connect with Memory and Knowledge Graphs
description: Every conversation with an AI assistant starts from scratch. Your agent doesn't remember what worked yesterday, can't tell you who owns a project without searching again, and repeats the same mistakes because failures are never captured. In this chalk talk, we show how Amazon Quick breaks out of statelessness with two primitives: a continuous-learning memory layer where a background agent extracts reusable knowledge after each session and scores it with a probabilistic confidence model, and a personal knowledge graph that connects people, projects, decisions, and evidence across your tools so the agent has a map of your world before it reads a single document. We'll whiteboard the architecture and the tradeoffs that shaped it, then open it up — bring your hardest questions about memory staleness, confidence calibration, graph noise, or making agents that actually get better over time.
location: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Neopolitan III

title: Teaching Telemetry to Think: From Raw Signals to Root Cause
description: An AI agent investigating an incident starts cold: no sense of normal, no topology, no causal history. It rebuilds context from raw documents every time. What if the telemetry understood itself first? We'll examine an intelligence layer for agentic observability, where streaming detectors and a live service graph distill billions of signals into incident observations, then fine-tuned reasoning models, built on open-weight LLMs, correlate them into ranked root causes. Whiteboard with us on the hard parts: what to teach a model versus retrieve at inference, how domain fine-tuning beats frontier scale, and where reasoning models still fail.

description: Managing memory for hundreds of tenants in SaaS shouldn't require hundreds of IAM policies — yet most products scaling multi-tenant agents on AWS end up there: a namespace per tenant-agent pair, a policy per tenant, deployment times that climb with every customer. In this chalk talk, learn how to isolate both layers of agent memory in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore — short-term session events and long-term extracted records — with one Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) policy backed by AWS Security Token Service (STS) session tags. We cover the actorId and namespace conventions, the Token Vending Machine that mints per-tenant credentials, and the anti-patterns that break isolation as you scale. Leave with the reference architecture and the IAM policy template you can use on Monday.

title: Testing serverless and event-driven applications
description: You're shipping faster with serverless, but your testing strategy hasn't kept up. Local mocks drift from cloud behavior. Integration tests require full deployments. Contract changes between services break downstream consumers silently. In this chalk talk, whiteboard testing approaches that match how serverless developers actually work: unit testing business logic in isolation, integration testing service interactions without deploying everything, and contract testing event schemas between producers and consumers. We cover local versus cloud testing tradeoffs, when each makes sense, and chaos engineering techniques like injecting message delays, duplicates, and out-of-order delivery to catch failures before your users do.

title: The cost of over-engineering: When your architecture fights you
description: Not every workload needs microservices, event-driven patterns, or serverless. In this chalk talk, examine real-world anti-patterns: services split too small, queues added without purpose, and abstractions that add latency without value. We’ll whiteboard decision frameworks for right-sizing architecture, including the signals that tell you when decomposition earns its complexity and when it doesn’t. Bring your diagrams and discuss where simplification improves speed, reduces cost, and strengthens reliability. Leave able to right-size your own architecture with confidence.

title: The Evaluator Is the Algorithm: Evolving SOTA for $15
description: We discovered a phase transition in LLM-guided code evolution: when the evaluation function provides smooth gradient signal, SOTA emerges automatically regardless of model choice; when it doesn't, no compute compensates. This "evaluator-dominance principle" emerged from stress-testing evolutionary search across 403 problems in 27 domains on Amazon Bedrock — 20× the scale of Google's original AlphaEvolve — achieving 96% SOTA-matching at $15/problem median cost. We'll present the Bedrock-native architecture (MAP-Elites, staged evaluation cascade, Opus/Haiku phase routing), a production vehicle routing deployment saving 1.28% on 100,000-customer routes at $530 total spend, and the evaluator design methodology that determines success or failure.

title: The judgment gap: when Terraform scans clean but fails the audit

title: The security you inherit: how the AWS platform protects your workloads by default
description: Every organization has finite security resources. The more the platform handles, the more your team can focus on securing what is unique to your application — your data, your logic, your users. In this session, we explore the security capabilities built into the AWS platform that work before you write a single IAM policy. From threat intelligence that blocks malicious actors at the network edge, to Nitro's zero operator access architecture that eliminates an entire class of insider risk, to automated reasoning that mathematically proves your policies behave as intended — these are protections you inherit just by running on AWS. We also cover PrivateLink for eliminating public internet exposure, default encryption, and S3 Block Public Access. Understand what the platform already handles so you can direct your security investment where it matters most: the application layer.

You'll see how the team structured the agents, what they found, and where the approach is headed.

title: Thousands of Databases, $250 a Month: Operating an Agentic Database Estate on AWS (sponsored by CockroachDB) (ARC338-S)
description: What if ~1,000 production-grade databases cost $250/month? Most teams pay more to keep a few clusters idle, each sized for peak load, running at 85–95% unused capacity and provisioned ticket by ticket. That model is breaking. AI agents create databases faster than platform teams can provision, secure or retire them. One engineering group grew from 13 databases to 392 in four months. At 1,000, managing one cluster at a time stops working. This session shifts focus to the estate with three architectural changes on AWS: Separate storage from compute, eliminating upfront capacity. Run isolated virtual clusters on shared hosts without creating sprawl. Use agentic operations to observe the estate and recommend actions your team approves. See live demos, a reference architecture and cost model behind the numbers. Bring your hardest questions about running stateful workloads at agent speed. This presentation is brought to you by CockroachDB, an AWS Partner.

Using Amazon GuardDuty and AWS Security Hub alongside CloudWatch and AgentCore Observability, you'll triage findings, correlate security events with application traces, map entity relationships, isolate compromised resources, and build automated remediations. You see how ThreatForest, an agentic tool built on the Strands framework, generates attack trees and MITRE ATT&CK mappings on its own, and how to build a mitigations catalog your organization can reuse. Raw web pages, HTML boilerplate, and 10 blue links padded with irrelevant text quietly multiply token spend and degrade answer quality. This lightning talk walks through how Exa engineered retrieval to hand LLMs exactly the text they need: neural search that returns precise passages instead of whole pages, highlight extraction tuned to the query, and context-budgeting techniques that cut input tokens dramatically without hurting accuracy. Using real production traces, we'll show how token-efficient retrieval changes the economics of agents at scale on AWS, and give you a practical checklist you can apply to any RAG or agent pipeline this week. This talk covers a working pattern for enterprise inference on AWS: PaletteAI Inference Launchpad running local open-weight models for routine requests, Amazon Bedrock as the burst target to extend capacity, and frontier models as needed for complex work. Instead of just storing logs and treating logs as text to grep during an outage, use centralization rules that bring telemetry together across accounts and regions, telemetry pipelines that enrich and route data in flight, intelligence tiering that matches storage cost to query value, and AI-assisted log analytics that surface answers instead of waiting for you to ask the right question. title: Turn PQC readiness into the trust story your board needs

With NIST PQC standards finalized, the algorithm question is settled, the open question is how to plan and fund the transition. You leave with a practical framework to scope your inventory, prioritize transitions, modernize how you protect data, and build the board narrative that funds your migration program.

title: Turn your coding agent into an always-on dev team with AgentCore
description: Claude Code, Kiro, and Codex are impressive individually, but in an enterprise they run stateless, isolated from team context, and invisible to governance. AgentCore turns any coding agent into a production system: shared memory so the agent understands your architecture across sessions, microVM isolation so jobs run in parallel without interference, identity propagation so agents access only what they should, and full trace observability so you know what every agent did and why. This session shows what changes when you pair popular coding agents with a production platform, and how our customer deployed this across hundreds of developers.

title: Twenty years of cloud architecture
description: Instant, vast scale and elasticity. Infrastructure as Code. Eventual consistency. Immutable infrastructure. Serverless. Event-driven computing. Internet of Things. Chaos engineering. Zero trust. Pervasive observability. Twenty years of cloud have produced an extraordinary density of patterns — each arriving with conviction and shaping what came next. Some became invisible foundations we build on without thinking. Others evolved in ways nobody predicted. And the evolution continues — now with agentic architectures. What has stood the test of time? What's still evolving? And what can we learn to be ready for the next twenty years?

These activities are time-consuming, error-prone, and delay study timelines. AI-driven multi-agent systems can intelligently automate protocol reviews, edit check programming, data validation, and query management accelerating study timelines, improving data accuracy, and enabling teams to focus on strategic, high-value activities. Know how integrating advanced AI-driven automation with human expertise enhances data accuracy, streamlines workflows, and accelerates decision-making processes, empowering clinical teams to achieve superior research outcomes. title: Under the hood of Kiro Crew: orchestration, memory, and safe autonomy
description: Handing real work to a crew of agents raises real questions: How does it coordinate parallel subagents without losing the thread? How does memory save across sessions so agents don't start cold? How do you give agents access to your code and CI while staying safe? In this chalk talk, we'll dig into how Kiro Crew works: observable multi-agent orchestration over Agent Client Protocol, self-evolving memory and skills you can inspect and edit, scheduled and webhook-triggered jobs, and defense-in-depth security with sandboxing, denied-by-default commands, and signed audit logs. Bring your architecture and security questions and we'll whiteboard through them.

title: Under the hood with Amazon EBS: Achieving sub-millisecond latency
description: Amazon EBS powers mission-critical applications with consistent sub-millisecond latency across millions of volumes. This session offers a behind-the-scenes look at the architectural innovations and engineering practices that make this possible. Learn how EBS leverages the AWS Nitro System, purpose-built hardware, and advanced I/O path optimizations to deliver reliable low-latency performance at hyperscale. Gain insights into how these capabilities translate into performance benefits for databases, analytics platforms, and latency-sensitive workloads.

title: Unexpected resilience: Lessons from a thousand incidents
description: After years of investigating incidents - both within AWS and across customer industries - some resilience lessons stand out. Not the obvious ones, but surprises no runbook could anticipate. We share the strangest, most counterintuitive findings from years of troubleshooting under pressure: failure modes nobody planned for, fixes that made things worse, and patterns that only emerge after enough failures. This isn't a best-practices talk - it's a field guide to building resilience from the unexpected. You'll leave with a sharper eye for hidden risks in your infrastructure - and fresh leads on things you didn't know were there.

title: Unified Commerce Intelligence for Amazon Sellers on Amazon Quick
description: Brands selling on Amazon generate rich signals across commerce and advertising — order trends, catalog performance, competitive pricing, campaign metrics, and customer engagement. The opportunity lies in connecting these signals into a unified view that drives faster, smarter decisions. In this chalk talk, we design an architecture that composes two Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers — the SP-API MCP Server for Selling Partner operations and the Amazon Ads MCP Server for campaigns and reporting — behind Amazon Qucik as a conversational layer. We'll whiteboard how brands can build cross-domain queries, like correlating ad spend with order velocity or surfacing catalog insights that inform campaign strategy. Leave with production-grade patterns for building agentic commerce workflows tailored to your brand's data

title: Unified observability with Amazon OpenSearch Service
description: Most teams run observability across fragmented tools: one for metrics, another for logs and traces, each with its own cost model and blind spots. In this session, you work hands-on to consolidate your observability stack on Amazon OpenSearch Service. You integrate Amazon Managed Prometheus for metrics, configure native OpenTelemetry ingestion for traces and logs, and see how a single pane of glass eliminates the context-switching that slows down investigations. Then you optimize for cost and scale: warm tiering, direct query for infrequently accessed data, and O-series instances for log-heavy workloads. Finally, you use AI-powered investigation to perform natural-language root-cause analysis across your unified telemetry and monitor your agents' behavior in production. You leave with a working observability setup that scales, costs less, and investigates faster.

title: Verifying Post-Quantum Cryptography at Speed
description: Traditionally, cryptographic engineering involves a performance/assurance trade-off: clean code is easy to audit and maintain, yet slow; handwritten assembly is fast, yet hard to validate. Discover how automated reasoning helps to overcome this tension, following the example of mlkem-native and mldsa-native, two open-source post-quantum cryptography libraries co-maintained by AWS and deployed in AWS-LC, Amazon's cryptography library. In these libraries, constraint solving enables automated superoptimization at the assembly level, while formal verification vets the result. Contrary to the popular belief that assurance costs speed, it is automated reasoning that enables deep optimization, verification and rapid deployment of cryptographic code at cloud scale.

title: What Can Neurosymbolic AI Prove About Agent Behavior?
description: AI agents that write and execute code autonomously create a fundamental trust problem: how do you guarantee behavioral boundaries without constraining the flexibility that makes agents useful? This chalk talk examines how neurosymbolic AI is making provable guarantees practical at scale: autoformalization translating natural-language constraints into temporal logic, satisfiability solvers whose exponential improvement keeps pace with exponentially harder verification problems, and LLMs guiding proof search in theorem provers like Lean, creating a virtuous cycle where better proofs yield stronger provers. We'll stratify what can be proved today, what requires LLM-discovered inductive invariants, and where undecidability still draws a hard line.

title: When Guardrails Break: Defense in Depth for Non-Deterministic AI (sponsored by Darktrace) (AIM287-S)
description: Organizations are deploying copilots, AI agents, and LLM-driven workflows faster than governance and security can adapt. Non-deterministic AI creates a new attack surface across prompts, agents, data, and runtime behavior, and acts as both defensive force multiplier and adversarial accelerant. Static guardrails are necessary but insufficient: they miss novel behavior, unsafe tool use, and risk that only surfaces when AI interacts with identities and downstream systems. This session presents a defense-in-depth model for securing AI at runtime, using NIST's Secure/Defend/Thwart framing: an identity control plane for agents, least-privilege and JIT access, runtime observability, behavior detection, and autonomous investigation and containment. We'll share a blueprint for a minimum viable AI security baseline, and why behavioral oversight is the decisive layer for securing AI at scale. This presentation is brought to you by Darktrace, an AWS Partner.

title: When one tenant spikes 100x, your architecture decides who pays
description: One tenant spikes 100x. The architecture either isolates the blast radius or turns it into every tenant's outage. Multi-tenant platforms face four decisions at this boundary. Where to place isolation so one workload cannot starve another. How fan-out creates backpressure that propagates upstream. When fair queuing replaces custom throttling code. What qualifies as real-time versus safely queueable. In this chalk talk you decide where your isolation boundaries belong and what trade-offs each placement creates. Bring your own scaling problem. We draw the architecture together.

We share the lessons implemented with customers, the internal changes AWS made to operate as a more secure AI-first organization, and practical steps every security team can take now.

description: Software is becoming more than something companies build. It is becoming the system through which they improve. The next generation of software factories will turn business signals into production software, measure the outcomes, and use those outcomes to improve each cycle of development. Engineers set the goals, architecture, policies, and approval gates, while the system handles execution and continuously improves itself. Factory cofounder Eno Reyes will share what this future looks like, what has to be true to build it, and why self-improving software will fundamentally change how every company operates. title: When tags run out: cost allocation for AI and multi-tenant workloads (sponsored by DoiT) (AIM296-S)
description: Tag-based allocation works until the resource stops belonging to anyone. A multi-tenant EKS cluster, a shared inference endpoint, a queue five services write to: each lands on the bill once, charged to whoever provisioned it. No amount of tagging discipline fixes that, because there is nothing to tag. This session covers where tag coverage structurally breaks down, and the alternative: measuring the running system to attribute shared spend to the team, feature, and customer that caused it, then reconciling back to the bill so the allocation still foots. Includes what this looks like in production on AWS. This presentation is brought to you by DoiT, an AWS Partner.

title: Where do agents fit? A capability-first approach to agentic AI
description: Not every workflow needs an agent, and applying agentic AI where it doesn’t fit adds nondeterminism, cost, and failure modes a deterministic design would have avoided. This chalk talk introduces a capability-first methodology for architects and engineering leaders evaluating agentic paths in their workflows, manual or software-driven. We’ll ideate on a scoring framework that assesses the inherent nature of the work to reveal where agentic approaches thrive. You’ll apply the PERCEIVE-REASON-ACT pattern for isolating AI reasoning from orchestration, and walk away with a repeatable rubric your teams can adopt immediately.

title: Where embeddings live: Designing production retrieval on AWS
description: Where should vector embeddings live? In your operational database, a dedicated vector store, or across several? In this session you evaluate the trade-offs across latency, data freshness, cost, and retrieval quality. You implement the same retrieval pattern across three engines: Amazon OpenSearch Service for combined lexical and vector search, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with pgvector for SQL-native filtered retrieval, and Amazon S3 Vectors for cost-optimized scale. You then combine them into a hybrid architecture that orchestrates a single query and merges the results with reciprocal rank fusion. You leave able to answer where your embeddings should live, backed by patterns you built yourself. Bring your laptop to participate.

title: Who Checks the Agents? Quality and Governance for the Agentic SDLC (sponsored by Qodo) (DVT223-S)
description: Agents now plan work, write code, generate tests and open PRs—sometimes without human review before production. Yet most teams rely on a trust model built for a slower SDLC: one reviewer, one merge gate and one chance to catch what went wrong. That model fails when agents operate at every stage and final review can’t reveal what happened upstream. This session treats trust as a property of the pipeline, not a final checkpoint. We’ll explore why the system generating code shouldn’t also verify it, how to turn tribal standards into enforceable, auditable controls, and where independent review belongs between spec and deploy. Key takeaways: Why end-stage review fails in an agent-driven SDLC. How to enforce and trace standards across teams, repos and AI tools. How to decide what can merge automatically, what needs human review and how to document that decision for auditors. This presentation is brought to you by Qodo, an AWS Partner.

title: Who’s Pulling the Strings? Securing GitHub from Rogue AI Agents (sponsored by Zscaler) (SEC231-S)
description: With the rise of autonomous AI agents like Devin, Cursor, and Amazon Q, the security boundary has shifted from the network perimeter directly to the developer's workspace. These AI tools and automated integration pipelines establish dynamic, encrypted connections straight to GitHub, third-party repositories, and cloud workloads—creating blind spots that legacy firewalls cannot see. Join us as we map out this highly interconnected AI developer ecosystem and showcase why traditional security fails. We will share a unified, proxy-based Zero Trust architecture that inspects encrypted developer traffic, secures access to critical repositories, and isolates untrusted AI actions. You’ll leave with an actionable blueprint to protect your code, APIs, and AI integrations while maintaining peak developer velocity. This presentation is brought to you by Zscaler, an AWS Partner.

title: Who's Your Security MVP? Here's How AI Ranks Them (sponsored by Trellix) (AIM2207-S)
description: Yeah, yeah, AI SOC, we get it. But what really goes into getting wins out of AI in security vs saving a couple of clicks? This talk will show the importance of small (dumb) LLM's and how they create opportunities for secops by allowing you to use more tokens, anywhere you want. It will demo how you can go beyond enriching a few alerts to stack rank your most valuable security tools in an ROI thunderdome. You'll learn the AI confidence guardrail framework you need so you to actually start taking actions on your behalf without accidentally deleting all your VM's when you asked it to "eliminate all vulnerabilities." Seeing is believing, so there will be real-world demos of where AI works, where it doesn't, and why--bring your 3D glasses. This presentation is brought to you by Trellix, an AWS Partner.

title: Why Enterprise RAG Fails: Document AI and Ontology Patterns on AWS
description: Most teams blame embeddings, vector databases, or foundation models when RAG systems underperform. In practice, failures often originate earlier in the pipeline where business meaning is lost during document ingestion. This session explores production Document AI patterns on AWS, including layout-aware extraction, ontology-driven classification, semantic chunking, metadata enrichment, and retrieval optimization. Using financial services examples, we demonstrate how domain ontologies improve extraction accuracy, retrieval relevance, and explainability. Attendees will learn practical architecture patterns, implementation tradeoffs, and a framework for building scalable, trustworthy RAG systems for enterprise workloads.

title: Why Multi-Agent Systems Fail in Production (And How to Fix It) (sponsored by MongoDB) (AIM263-S)
description: Most AI agents don't fall apart in production because the model isn't smart enough. They fail because state is fragmented: one agent can't see what another already learned, and nobody can reconstruct what was retrieved, decided, or handed off. In a multi-tenant setting, that's a governance problem, not just a debugging one. This session shows an architecture that fixes it by giving every layer a clear job: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore manages session context and end-to-end tracing, MongoDB Atlas handles durable memory, tenant-aware vector search, and audit history, and the MongoDB MCP Server connects the two so access stays governed. You'll watch agents share state, retrieve tenant-scoped data, and leave a replayable decision trail. Leave with a reference architecture for multi-agent state sharing and a model for what audit-ready really looks like. A MongoDB & AWS technical session. This presentation is brought to you by MongoDB, an AWS Partner.

title: Workload Identity Federation in multicloud environments
description: Eliminating long-lived credentials across clouds is essential for secure multicloud operations. This session presents three proven identity federation patterns: using SPIFFE/SPIRE for cryptographic workload identity across Kubernetes clusters, leveraging native OIDC providers from GKE and Azure to assume AWS IAM roles with short-lived tokens, and federating Kubernetes service accounts across cloud boundaries. Attendees leave with actionable blueprints for credential-free multicloud access.

title: World models for indoor robots: what breaks and why
description: World models promise to give robots predictive understanding of their environment, yet applying them to indoor robotics exposes fundamental gaps in how transformers reason about geometry. In this session, we present findings from building a trajectory-conditioned lidar world model for Diligent Robotics' hospital fleet on AWS. We examine why standard loss metrics fail for generative spatial predictions, why rotation breaks factored attention even with explicit conditioning, and the minimal set of inductive biases needed to restore geometric coherence. Attendees leave with a diagnostic framework for spatial reasoning failures in transformer-based world models.

title: You cannot write the eval for a failure you have not seen yet (sponsored by Arize AI) (BIZ211-S)
description: LLM-as-a-judge works beautifully when you already know what you're looking for. You write the rubric, validate it against human labels, and it catches the failure you designed it to catch. But agents in production don't fail the way you anticipated. They fail as they meet new tools, new users, and environments that shifted underneath them, and every new failure arrives after the rubric was written. This talk argues the evaluation layer itself must become agentic. Instead of specifying a metric, you describe the behavior you want, and a judge with tool access inspects the trace, finds the spans that matter, classifies what went wrong, and generates labels you can monitor against. We'll cover why this became viable only recently, where it fails, and how to keep an agentic judge honest against human labels, so you know when to reach for one and how to validate it. title: Your runtime Is being deprecated. Your weekend isn't.
description: Your inbox fills with runtime deprecation notices—hundreds of Lambda functions on Node.js 20, Python 3.10, and whatever's next. Handling them one by one drains capacity you'd rather spend on features. This hands-on workshop flips the script: instead of chasing individual apps, you'll modernize a fleet. Using AWS Transform custom, you'll run AWS-provided transformations to upgrade Lambda runtimes at scale, then stand up continuous modernization to scan repositories against a baseline, prioritize what's drifting, and open pull requests automatically. Turn a wall of end-of-support alerts into a queue of ready-to-merge PRs. You must bring your laptop to participate.

title: Your system made a decision. you cannot explain it.
description: Your system makes a decision. A human makes a decision. Both write to the same log in the same format. Three months later you need to know which was which. You cannot tell. This is not a logging problem. It is a runtime architecture problem. If decision origin is not captured at the boundary when the decision happens, no system can recover it after. Whether you need this for compliance, debugging, or customer trust, the architectural fix is identical. In this chalk talk you will decide: what to capture at the decision boundary, how much context to store, and when reproducibility justifies the cost.

title: Your Users Aren't Waiting to Build AI Agents. Are You Ready?
description: The spreadsheet wizards and automation tinkerers in your organization are already reaching for low-code and visual builder tools to assemble AI agents on their own. Call it citizen agent building: either governance sprawl, or your fastest path to scale. This interactive chalk talk gives platform, security, and data leaders a reference pattern that puts low-code builders on top and Amazon Bedrock beneath, so the security, data residency, and governance enterprises need come from the foundation rather than from each agent. Amazon Bedrock makes governance possible; your architecture makes it the default.

title: Your WAN, reimagined: SD-WAN on the AWS global backbone
description: Your enterprise WAN was built for a world where applications lived in data centers. That world is gone, but you're still paying for MPLS circuits and waiting weeks for new sites. What if you could replace that backbone entirely? AWS offers the largest global infrastructure footprint of any provider: resilient, agile, low-latency, and encrypted. In this chalk talk, we will whiteboard how to connect your SD-WAN to AWS Cloud WAN, maintain segmentation from branch to VPC, and pay only for what you use—no long-term contracts. Bring your WAN architecture and we'll show you what it looks like without the middlemen.

title: Zero-Shot Demand Forecasting with Chronos 2, SMUS, and Quick Suite
description: Stockouts and overstocks quietly erode margin for retail and CPG brands, driving lost sales, markdowns, and working capital tied up in the wrong inventory. Traditional forecasting models take months to train and tune, and struggle with the cold-start problem for new products and locations. In this chalk talk, we whiteboard how to architect zero-shot demand forecasting pipelines using Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio with the Chronos 2 time-series foundation model, developed by the Amazon Science team and proven on Amazon's own retail and CPG demand at scale, requiring no historical model training. We walk through the end-to-end design: SMUS notebooks for rapid experimentation, Chronos 2 for multi-variate time series prediction, and Amazon Quick Suite for conversational analytics that let planners explore forecasts in natural language..

title: Zero to multimodal in 60 mins: Building Live Sync on Connect Customer
description: What does it take to synchronize a live voice conversation with a real-time visual interface — and make it feel like magic? In this chalk talk, we'll answer that question by building one from scratch. Starting from first principles, we'll construct a fully functional voice AI agent that leverages the patented Live Sync on Amazon Connect Customer: the signaling that keeps voice and visual in lock-step, the state machine that drives bi-directional interaction, and the rendering layer that turns conversational intent into on-screen UI in real time. No slides, no hand-waving — just building, live, from zero to a working multimodal agent in 60 minutes. At the end, we'll deploy what we built and every phone in the room becomes a live demo.
location: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Code Talk

title: Zero-Trust by Design: How Bee Protects Personal Data Even from Itself on AWS
description: Personal agentic AI represents a new frontier; devices that understand you deeply enough to act on your behalf. Bee is Amazon's AI wearable that helps users capture and act on insights from their daily lives. But deep personalization demands deep trust and privacy. In this session, learn how the Bee team architected a zero-trust pipeline using AWS Nitro Enclaves and confidential computing to keep sensitive data cryptographically isolated at every stage. We'll share the attestation models, data minimization tradeoffs, and design principles you can apply to build AI-powered experiences your users trust from day one.
location: Caesars Palace | Promenade Level | Neopolitan III

title: Zero trust for non-human identities: IAM for autonomous agents
description: Agents access tools, call APIs, and delegate to other agents. They need layered identity controls at every stage. In this builders' session, apply zero trust principles to a multi-agent environment using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. You'll configure agent identities with OAuth providers, enforce least privilege via OBO token exchange, differentiate agents from humans with IAM MCP condition keys, and set Gateway rules blocking unauthorized access. Then, you stress test your setup using cross-chain access, privilege escalation, identity spoofing to see each blocked by a different layer you built.
location: Wynn/Encore | Upper Convention Promenade | Cristal 2 | Content Hub | Builders' Session 2
